definition_zh: 民间世代口耳相传的故事、歌谣、信仰与习俗的总称
definition_en: the traditional stories, songs, beliefs and customs of a community, passed on by word of mouth
core_image: 村口的老槐树下，几个孩子围着一位老人，听他讲一个没有书的故事
scene: 村口的老槐树下，几个孩子围着一位老人，听他讲一个没有书的故事。 The folklore of the valley survives mainly in songs sung at harvest.
sceneCN: 这里 folklore 指「民间口耳相传的故事与习俗之总称」（第 1 个义项：一个社群传下来的口头传统）；句意为这个山谷的民间文化主要靠丰收时唱的歌流传。可辨识物件：老槐树、老人、孩子、歌谱。

derivatives.zh: 民间文化的
民俗学者
民俗学
民众；民间的
朴实民间的
民俗研究

senses.title: A community's oral inheritance
senses.titleCN: 社群口耳相传的文化遗产
senses.definition: the body of stories, songs and customs that a community passes on without writing them down
senses.definitionCN: 一个社群在不依靠书写的情况下传递的故事、歌谣与习俗整体
senses.example: The folklore of the valley survives mainly in songs sung at harvest.
senses.exampleCN: 这个山谷的民间文化主要靠丰收时唱的歌流传。
senses.why: folk names the people and lore names what they teach, so the compound is learning that lives in a community rather than a library.
senses.whyCN: folk 指民众，lore 指他们所教的东西，因此这个复合词指活在社群中而非图书馆里的学问。

senses.title: Traditional tales and legends
senses.definition: narrative folklore such as fairy tales, ghost stories and local legends
senses.definitionCN: 如童话、鬼故事与地方传说这类叙事性民俗
senses.example: Every village tells a folklore tale about the old bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 每个村庄都有一则关于那座旧桥的民间故事。
senses.why: stories are the part of folklore that travels furthest without being written.
senses.whyCN: 故事是民俗中最能在不书写的情况下远行传播的部分。

senses.title: Songs and ballads
senses.definition: sung folklore, including work songs, laments and ballads
senses.definitionCN: 歌唱形态的民俗，包括劳动号子、挽歌与叙事歌谣
senses.example: The folklore of the fishing villages is carried by work songs.
senses.exampleCN: 渔村的民间文化由劳动号子承载。
senses.why: melody is a memory aid, so song is the oldest archive of the unschooled.
senses.whyCN: 旋律是记忆的助手，因此歌谣是未受教育者最古老的档案。

senses.title: Popular beliefs and superstitions
senses.definition: unwritten beliefs about luck, spirits, omens and protective practices
senses.definitionCN: 关于运气、鬼魂、预兆与护身做法的成文之外的信念
senses.example: Folklore about the crossroads kept travellers from walking at night.
senses.exampleCN: 关于十字路口的民间说法让旅人不敢夜行。
senses.why: beliefs explain misfortune cheaply, and folklore stores them where no doctrine reaches.
senses.whyCN: 信念能廉价地解释不幸，而民俗把它们储存在教义触及不到之处。

senses.title: Craft and material folk culture
senses.definition: traditional making of tools, cloth, food and dwellings
senses.definitionCN: 工具、织物、食物与居所的传统制作方式
senses.example: The museum collects folklore in the form of baskets and looms.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆以篮子与织机的形式收藏民间工艺。
senses.why: lore is not only told but made, and objects carry instruction in their shape.
senses.whyCN: 学问不只靠讲述，也靠制作，器物在形状里携带技艺。

senses.title: The object of a scholarly discipline
senses.definition: the material that folklorists collect, classify and interpret
senses.definitionCN: 民俗学者采集、分类与解释的材料
senses.example: The journal treats folklore as evidence, not as quaint decoration.
senses.exampleCN: 该期刊把民俗当作证据，而非古雅的装饰。
senses.why: once a field has a name for its material, the material becomes an object of study.
senses.whyCN: 当一个领域为自己的材料命名，这些材料就成了研究对象。

senses.title: The oral tradition of one group
senses.definition: the specific verbal inheritance of a people, region or occupation
senses.definitionCN: 某个民族、地区或职业特有的口头遗产
senses.example: Miners kept their own folklore of underground spirits.
senses.exampleCN: 矿工有自己的地下神灵传说。
senses.why: occupations form their own risk-sharing culture with its own stories.
senses.whyCN: 职业会形成自己的风险分担文化，也有自己的故事。

senses.title: Folk creation in the internet age
senses.definition: jokes, memes and stories that spread anonymously online in the old folk manner
senses.definitionCN: 以古老民间方式在网上匿名传播的笑话、模因与故事
senses.example: Researchers now study the folklore of message boards.
senses.exampleCN: 研究者如今研究论坛上的民间创作。
senses.why: the medium changed, but anonymous communal retelling is the same act as before.
senses.whyCN: 媒介变了，但匿名集体复述仍是同一种行为。

senses.title: A story dismissed as untrue
senses.titleCN: 被当作「传说」的不实说法
senses.definition: used dismissively of a claim that people repeat without evidence
senses.definitionCN: 轻蔑地指人们无证据却反复传播的说法
senses.example: The idea that the tower has no foundations is pure folklore.
senses.exampleCN: 说那座塔没有地基纯粹是民间传说。
senses.why: when a repeated story is doubted, folklore becomes a word for unverified belief.
senses.whyCN: 当反复流传的故事受到怀疑，folklore 就变成「未经证实的说法」之词。

intro.en: Folklore is a deliberately coined English compound: folk, from Old English folc 'people', plus lore, from Old English lār 'teaching, learning'. It was proposed in 1846. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: folklore 是一个有意造出的英语复合词：folk 来自古英语 folc「民众」，lore 来自古英语 lār「教导、学问」。这个词于 1846 年被提出。年代均为约数。

items.en: Folc meant 'people, crowd, tribe'. The pre-Germanic shape is reconstructed, so the earlier form is not witnessed in any text.
items.cn: folc 意为「民众、人群、部族」。日耳曼语之前的形态属重构形式，更早的词形没有任何文本书证。

items.en: Lār meant 'teaching, instruction, learning', and still survives in lore and in learned.
items.cn: lār 意为「教导、传授、学问」，仍存于 lore 与 learned 之中。

items.en: In 1846 William Thoms proposed folklore to replace 'popular antiquities', and the word spread quickly through learned journals.
items.cn: 1846 年威廉·汤姆斯提出用 folklore 取代「民间古物」一词，这个词很快在学术刊物中传播。

items.en: It first meant the whole inherited culture of ordinary people, then narrowed to stories, songs and beliefs, then widened again to include craft and online creation.
items.cn: 它先指普通民众继承的整体文化，后收窄到故事、歌谣与信念，再扩展到工艺与网络创作。

items.en: The word now also serves as a mild dismissal of a claim that circulates without evidence.
items.cn: 如今这个词也用来轻微否定一种无证据却流传的说法。

items.en: Source uncertain (pre-Germanic origin): the older Germanic shape of folc is a reconstruction, and the pre-Germanic source of lār is not established.
items.cn: 来源不确定（日耳曼语之前的来源）：folc 更早的日耳曼语形态属重构形式；lār 在日耳曼语之前的来源无定论。

note.en: Group one holds forms built from the two halves of the compound; group two holds narrative or traditional genres often mistaken for it.
note.cn: 第一组是由复合词两半构成的词；第二组是常被与之混淆的叙事或传统类别。

entries.definition: Ordinary people or a particular people; folklore is what they pass on.
entries.definitionCN: 指普通民众或某一民族；folklore 是他们传下的东西。

entries.definition: Traditional knowledge on a subject, as in plant lore or seafaring lore.
entries.definitionCN: 指某一方面的传统知识，如植物知识或航海知识。

entries.definition: A person who collects and studies folklore; the suffix -ist names the person, not the material.
entries.definitionCN: 指采集与研究民俗的人；后缀 -ist 指人，而非材料。

entries.definition: Means 'of folklore', often used of art that borrows folk material.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「民间文化的」，常用于借用民间素材的艺术。

entries.definition: A story about a person or place, told as if historical; folklore is the whole field that contains it.
entries.definitionCN: 指关于某人或某地、仿佛历史般讲述的故事；folklore 是包含它的整个领域。

entries.definition: A story about gods or origins, usually tied to belief; folklore can be secular and everyday.
entries.definitionCN: 指关于神祇或起源的故事，通常与信仰相连；folklore 可以是世俗日常的。

entries.definition: Anything passed between generations, including law and craft; folklore stresses oral and communal forms.
entries.definitionCN: 指代代相传的一切，包括法律与技艺；folklore 强调口头与集体形式。

entries.definition: Recorded personal memories of events; folklore is communal and often older than any witness.
entries.definitionCN: 指记录下来的个人事件记忆；folklore 是集体的，往往比任何见证者更古老。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real word partnerships and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: folk 'people' plus lore 'teaching' gives 'the teaching of the people'.
normal.cn: folk「民众」加 lore「教导」，得「民众的学问」。

normal.en: The word was coined in 1846 to replace the phrase popular antiquities.
normal.cn: 这个词于 1846 年造出，用来取代「民间古物」这一说法。

normal.en: The family runs folk, lore, folklore, folkloric, folklorist and folkloristics.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 folk、lore、folklore、folkloric、folklorist 与 folkloristics。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: local folklore, rural folklore, folklore collector, folklore and myth.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：地方民俗、乡村民俗、民俗采集者、民俗与神话。

normal.en: The same word now covers memes and message-board stories, because the spread is still anonymous and communal.
normal.cn: 这个词如今也涵盖模因与论坛故事，因为传播仍是匿名且集体的。

abstract.en: Picture a library with no shelves, only voices.
abstract.cn: 想象一座没有书架、只有声音的图书馆。

abstract.en: Picture a story that changes a little each time it is told, and survives by changing.
abstract.cn: 想象一个故事每讲一次就变一点，并靠变化而存活。

abstract.en: Picture a path kept open by the people who retell it.
abstract.cn: 想象一条因不断被复述而保持畅通的路。

examples.en: She collected folklore from fishermen along the whole coast.
examples.cn: 她沿着整条海岸采集渔民的民间故事。

examples.en: The film borrows folklore but invents its own ending.
examples.cn: 这部电影借用了民间传说，却自编了结局。

examples.en: Online folklore spreads faster than any village tale.
examples.cn: 网络民间创作传播得比任何村中故事都快。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「folk（民众）+ lore（学问）」——老百姓口口相传的学问

root: 古英语 folc「民众」+ 古英语 lār「教导、学问」；1846 年由威廉·汤姆斯造出，取代「民间古物」。日耳曼语之前的形态均属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one channel: knowledge is passed mouth to ear, and that channel then carries tales, songs, beliefs, craft, a discipline's evidence, one group's tradition, online creation and finally an unverified claim.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿同一条渠道展开：知识从口传到耳，这条渠道再依次承载故事、歌谣、信念、工艺、学科证据、某群体的传统、网络创作，最后承载未经证实的说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a library with no shelves, only voices passing a story hand to hand without paper.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座没有书架、只有声音的图书馆，故事不用纸便一手手传下去。

branches.en: THE CHANNEL AND ONE GROUP: the general inheritance, and the specific version kept by a people or trade.
branches.cn: 渠道与某一群体：普遍的继承，以及某个民族或行业保有的特定版本。

branches.en: STORIES: narrative is the part of the inheritance that travels furthest.
branches.cn: 故事：叙事是这份遗产中传播最远的部分。

branches.en: SONGS: melody carries what writing cannot reach.
branches.cn: 歌谣：旋律携带书写触及不到的东西。

branches.en: BELIEF AND OBJECT: superstition explains misfortune, and craft teaches through shape.
branches.cn: 信念与器物：迷信解释不幸，工艺通过形状传授技艺。

branches.en: EVIDENCE, NEW MEDIA, DOUBT: the material becomes a science, then a meme, and finally a word for what cannot be proved.
branches.cn: 证据、新媒介与怀疑：材料先成为科学，再成为模因，最后成为「无法证明之物」的说法。

intro.en: Folklore is a modern compound of two Old English words, so its parts are transparent and its family is built with English suffixes.
intro.cn: folklore 是两个古英语词构成的现代复合词，其成分清晰，词族由英语后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: No Latin borrowing stands behind this word; both halves are Old English, so no Latin source forms are recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词背后没有拉丁借词；两半都来自古英语，因此不列拉丁语源形式。

items.example: Folc is the ancestor of folk.
items.exampleCN: folc 是 folk 的祖先形式。

items.example: Lār survives in lore and in learned.
items.exampleCN: lār 存于 lore 与 learned 中。

items.example: Folk can also be an adjective, as in folk music.
items.exampleCN: folk 也可作形容词，如民间音乐。

items.example: Lore often appears in compounds such as plant lore.
items.exampleCN: lore 常出现在植物知识这类复合词中。

items.example: The compound replaced an older phrase.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词取代了更早的说法。

items.example: Folkloric means relating to folklore.
items.exampleCN: folkloric 意为与民俗有关的。

items.example: Folklorist names a collector or scholar.
items.exampleCN: folklorist 指采集者或学者。

items.example: Folkloristics names the discipline itself.
items.exampleCN: folkloristics 指这门学科本身。

items.meaning: deliberately plain and rural in style
items.example: Folksy is often a criticism of manufactured simplicity.
items.exampleCN: folksy 常批评人为制造的朴素。

items.meaning: the customary ways of a people
items.example: Folkways are everyday custom rather than formal law.
items.exampleCN: folkways 指日常习俗，而非正式法律。

definition_zh: 原始的；早期的；简陋的；基本的
definition_en: belonging to an early stage of development; simple or basic rather than advanced
core_image: 一根削尖的树枝与一块打制的石片，旁边摆着一台精密仪器，两者对照出「最初的样子」
scene: 展柜里，削尖的树枝与打制石片被标为最初阶段，旁边是一台精密仪器。 A primitive toolkit of sharpened sticks and knapped stone lay beside a precision instrument.
sceneCN: 这里 primitive 指「属于最早阶段的、未加工的」（第 1 个义项：原始的、早期的）；句意为展柜里一套削尖树枝与打制石片的原始工具放在精密仪器旁边。可辨识物件：树枝、石片、展柜、仪器；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 原始的；早期的；简陋的；基本的；原始派的

derivatives.zh: primitive（原始的）+ -ly（古英语 -līce，方式副词）→ 原始地；简陋地
primitive（原始的）+ -ness（古英语 -nes，性质名词）→ 原始性；简陋
primitive（原始的）+ -ism（拉丁 -ismus，主义）→ 原始主义
primitive（原始的）+ art（艺术）→ 原始派艺术
primitive（原始的）+ -ist（主义者）→ 原始主义者

senses.title: Belonging to the earliest stage
senses.definition: belonging to an early stage of development, before refinement
senses.definitionCN: 属于发展的早期阶段，尚未精细化
senses.example: Primitive tools were made by striking one stone against another.
senses.exampleCN: 原始工具是把一块石头往另一块上打制而成的。
senses.why: The word is built on Latin primus 'first', so its core sense is simply 'of the first stage'.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由拉丁 primus「第一」构成，核心义就是「属于第一阶段」。

senses.title: Simple and rough
senses.definition: simple to the point of being uncomfortable or inadequate
senses.definitionCN: 简单到令人不适或不够用的程度
senses.example: The camp had only primitive washing facilities.
senses.exampleCN: 营地只有极为简陋的洗浴设施。
senses.why: Because early stages lack refinement, 'first' easily slides into 'rough' when applied to living conditions.
senses.whyCN: 由于早期阶段缺少打磨，「第一」用于生活条件时很容易滑向「粗糙」。

senses.title: A dated word for peoples
senses.titleCN: 未开化的（旧用法，含贬义）
senses.definition: an old and now discredited label for peoples considered less advanced
senses.definitionCN: 旧时对被视为不发达民族的一种标签，如今已被否定且含贬义
senses.example: Nineteenth-century writers used primitive in ways that modern anthropology rejects.
senses.exampleCN: 19 世纪作者使用 primitive 的方式，现代人类学已予否定。
senses.why: The label assumed a single ladder of progress, and the word inherited that assumption.
senses.whyCN: 这个标签预设了一条单一的进步阶梯，词义也继承了这一预设。

senses.title: Undeveloped in biology
senses.definition: in an early or undifferentiated form, as a cell or tissue
senses.definitionCN: 处于早期或未分化状态，如细胞或组织
senses.example: The embryo's primitive streak marks the first axis of the body.
senses.exampleCN: 胚胎的原条标出身体的第一条轴线。
senses.why: Biology uses 'first-stage' literally: the structure appears before its later specializations.
senses.whyCN: 生物学把「第一阶段」用得很实：该结构出现在后来的特化之前。

senses.title: Taken as basic in logic
senses.titleCN: 逻辑与数学中的初始的
senses.definition: accepted without definition, as a starting notion in a system
senses.definitionCN: 在系统中作为起点而不加定义地接受
senses.example: Point and line are primitive notions in that geometry.
senses.exampleCN: 在那套几何里，点与线是初始概念。
senses.why: A primitive notion is one you cannot derive, so the word keeps its 'first' sense exactly.
senses.whyCN: 初始概念是无法推导的东西，因此这个词精确保留了「第一」义。

senses.title: Art outside the academic tradition
senses.definition: art by self-taught makers or from traditions outside formal training
senses.definitionCN: 自学作者或学院传统之外的艺术
senses.example: The exhibition placed primitive art beside trained portraiture.
senses.exampleCN: 展览把原始派艺术与受过训练的人像画并置。
senses.why: Collectors used the word for work they saw as untrained, and the label survived in art history.
senses.whyCN: 收藏家用这个词指他们眼中未受训练的作品，这个标签在艺术史中保留下来。

senses.title: A self-taught painter's style
senses.definition: a style marked by flat perspective and strong outline
senses.definitionCN: 以平面透视与强烈轮廓为特征的风格
senses.example: The primitive painter filled the canvas with flat houses and bright roofs.
senses.exampleCN: 这位自学画家在画布上排满平面房屋和鲜艳屋顶。
senses.why: The style sense comes from the makers rather than the period, so a modern untrained painter can still be called primitive.
senses.whyCN: 风格义来自作者而非年代，因此现代的自学画家仍可被称为原始派。

senses.title: A root word in linguistics
senses.definition: a word that is not derived from another word in the same language
senses.definitionCN: 在同一语言中不由别的词派生的词
senses.example: Hand is a primitive word, while handful is derived.
senses.exampleCN: 「手」是词根词，而由它加后缀构成的「一把之量」是派生词。
senses.why: Linguistics borrows the 'first' sense: the word stands at the base of a derivational family.
senses.whyCN: 语言学借用了「第一」义：这个词位于一个派生词族的基底。

intro.en: Primitive comes from Latin primus 'first' through the derived adjective primitivus and French. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: primitive 来自拉丁 primus「第一」，经派生形容词 primitivus 与法语进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Primus meant 'first'; it also gives prime, primary, primate and primal, so the family is large.
items.cn: primus 意为「第一」，也产生 prime、primary、primate 与 primal，因此词族很大。

items.en: Primitivus meant 'first of its kind, earliest', built from primus plus the adjective ending -ivus.
items.cn: primitivus 意为「同类中最早的」，由 primus 加形容词词尾 -ivus 构成。

items.en: Old French primitif carried the adjective into English in the fifteenth century, first in religious language.
items.cn: 古法语 primitif 在 15 世纪把这个形容词带入英语，最初用于宗教语言。

items.en: From the nineteenth century the word was used for art outside academic training and for peoples judged less advanced, a use now rejected.
items.cn: 从 19 世纪起，这个词被用于学院训练之外的艺术，也被用于被判定为不发达的民族，后者如今已被否定。

items.en: Biology and logic kept the literal 'first' sense: a primitive structure or notion is one that comes before the rest.
items.cn: 生物学与逻辑学保留了字面的「第一」义：初始结构或初始概念都先于其余部分。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root and first date): the Indo-European root behind primus is reconstructed as per 'forward, before', a reconstruction and not a recorded form; the fifteenth-century English date is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根与首见年代）：primus 之前的印欧词根被重构为 per「向前、在前」，属重构形式而非有记录的形式；英语 15 世纪的首见年代为约数。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Latin 'first' root with different ranks; group two holds near meanings that describe stage or finish.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁「第一」词根、但等级不同的词；第二组是描述阶段或完成度的近义词。

entries.definition: From Latin primus 'first'; it means first in importance or the best period, not earliest in time.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 primus「第一」；指地位首要或全盛期，而非时间上最早。

entries.definition: From Latin primarius 'of the first rank'; it means first in order or basic.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 primarius「居首的」；指次序第一或基础性的。

entries.definition: From Latin primas 'of the first rank'; the animal order was named as the 'first' order by Linnaeus.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 primas「居首位的」；动物目名是林奈把它列为「第一」目而来。

entries.definition: From primus plus -al; it stresses what is earliest and most instinctive.
entries.definitionCN: 由 primus 加 -al 构成；强调最早、最本能的部分。

entries.definition: Simply first in time, with no judgment about refinement.
entries.definitionCN: 仅指时间上早，不含精细程度的判断。

entries.definition: Rough and unrefined, often implying poor workmanship rather than an early stage.
entries.definitionCN: 粗糙未加工，常指做工差，而非发展阶段早。

entries.definition: Serving as a foundation, with no suggestion of being outdated.
entries.definitionCN: 作为基础的，不含过时之意。

entries.definition: Not yet grown or elaborated, used of land, ideas or organisms.
entries.definitionCN: 尚未成长或展开，用于土地、想法或生物。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real primus family and the scientific senses that keep 'first' literally.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的 primus 词族，以及保留字面「第一」的科学义项。

normal.en: Latin primus 'first' gives prime, primary, primate and primal.
normal.cn: 拉丁 primus「第一」产生 prime、primary、primate 与 primal。

normal.en: The comparative is more primitive, not primitiver.
normal.cn: 比较级是 more primitive，不写作 primitiver。

normal.en: Biology keeps 'first' literally in primitive streak and primitive cell.
normal.cn: 生物学在「原条」「原初细胞」中保留字面的「第一」。

normal.en: Logic uses primitive notion for a starting idea taken without definition.
normal.cn: 逻辑学用 primitive notion 指不加定义的初始概念。

normal.en: The anthropological label is now avoided in careful writing.
normal.cn: 人类学的旧标签如今在严谨写作中已被避免。

abstract.en: Picture a sharpened stick lying beside a polished instrument.
abstract.cn: 想象一根削尖的树枝躺在一台光亮的仪器旁。

abstract.en: Picture a drawing with a flat sky and a bright roof, made by someone who never trained.
abstract.cn: 想象一幅天空扁平的画，屋顶鲜亮，出自从未受过训练的人之手。

abstract.en: Picture a first step on a staircase whose top you cannot yet see.
abstract.cn: 想象楼梯的第一级，顶端还看不见。

examples.en: The primitive plough was no more than a pointed branch.
examples.cn: 原始犁不过是一根削尖的树枝。

examples.en: The village had primitive drainage and no running water.
examples.cn: 这个村子排水简陋，也没有自来水。

examples.en: Point and line are primitive notions in the system.
examples.cn: 点与线在该系统中是初始概念。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「pri（第一）＋mitive」——排在第一、最早的样子 → 原始的

root: 拉丁 primus「第一」+ 形容词词尾 -ivus 构成 primitivus「同类中最早的」，经古法语 primitif 入英语；primus 之前的印欧词根为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses start from the literal first stage, then move to rough conditions, the discredited label for peoples, undifferentiated biology, logic that takes its starting notions without definition, art outside training, a self-taught style and a root word.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从字面的第一阶段出发，随后是简陋条件、已被否定的民族标签、未分化的生物结构、不加定义的逻辑起点、学院外的艺术、自学画风与词根词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sharpened stick beside a precision instrument, the first step before the polished one.
core.cn: 核心意象：削尖树枝与精密仪器并置，光洁之前的第一级台阶。

branches.en: FIRST STAGE: what comes earliest is also what lacks finish.
branches.cn: 第一阶段：最先出现的也往往最缺打磨。

branches.en: REJECTED LABEL: the old word for peoples rested on a false ladder.
branches.cn: 被否定的标签：旧时对民族的称法建立在虚假的阶梯上。

branches.en: LITERAL FIRST: biology and logic keep the sense of what comes before the rest.
branches.cn: 字面的第一：生物学与逻辑学保留「先于其余」之义。

branches.en: UNTAUGHT ART: makers outside training are named by their distance from the academy.
branches.cn: 未受训的艺术：学院之外的作者以其距离学院而得名。

branches.en: ROOT WORD: the base of a derivational family is 'first' again.
branches.cn: 词根词：派生词族的基底又回到了「第一」。

intro.en: Primitive belongs to the large Latin primus family, and its prefixes and suffixes show how 'first' branches into rank, time and foundation.
intro.cn: primitive 属于庞大的拉丁 primus 词族，其词缀显示「第一」如何分出等级、时间与基础三层。

latinIntro.en: Latin primus 'first' gives primitivus, primarius, primas and primal; the English endings -ly, -ness and -ism build the rest.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 primus「第一」产生 primitivus、primarius、primas 与 primal；英语后缀 -ly、-ness 与 -ism 构成其余部分。

items.example: Primus is the root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: primus 是整个词族的词根。

items.example: The Latin adjective passed through French.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁形容词经法语传来。

items.example: The ending forms primitivus.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾构成 primitivus。

items.example: A primitive tool needs no finishing.
items.exampleCN: 原始工具无需精加工。

items.example: The room was primitively furnished.
items.exampleCN: 这个房间陈设简陋。

items.example: The primitiveness of the camp surprised them.
items.exampleCN: 营地的简陋让他们吃惊。

items.example: Primitivism shaped early modern painting.
items.exampleCN: 原始主义影响了早期现代绘画。

items.meaning: first in rank or the best period
items.example: He was in his prime.
items.exampleCN: 他正当壮年。

items.example: Primary education comes first.
items.exampleCN: 初等教育排在最先。

items.example: The primate is our closest relative among mammals.
items.exampleCN: 灵长类是哺乳动物中与我们最近的亲属。

primitivus, primitiva, primitivum (adj., first and second declension)

primitive（原始的）+ -ness（古英语 -nes，性质名词）→ 原始性；简陋

definition_zh: 社会学的；从社会结构角度解释的
definition_en: relating to sociology, or explaining behaviour by social structures rather than individual choices
core_image: 把一间屋子的墙拆掉，露出与整条街相连的水管
scene: 一份关于通勤时间的报告不再归咎于个人选择，而是追问住房与地铁线路的布局。 The report offers a sociological explanation of lateness.
sceneCN: 这里 sociological 指「从社会结构出发来解释的」（第 2 个义项：以社会结构而非个人来解释）；句意为这份报告对迟到给出了社会学解释。场景要素：通勤路线图、住房分布、报告封面。

pos.zh: 社会学的；从社会角度解释的

derivatives.zh: 由 sociological 去掉形容词后缀构成的名词，指社会学
由 sociological 加副词后缀构成，指从社会学角度
由 sociology 加表人后缀构成，指社会学者
与 sociological 同根但更宽，泛指社会的
由 society 加形容词后缀构成，指整个社会层面的

senses.title: Relating to the discipline
senses.titleCN: 与社会学这门学科有关
senses.definition: belonging to or produced within the academic field of sociology
senses.definitionCN: 属于社会学领域或在该领域内产生的
senses.example: The journal published a sociological study of remote work.
senses.exampleCN: 该期刊发表了一项关于远程办公的社会学研究。
senses.why: The adjective is simply the discipline's name with its regular ending, so its first job is to attach things to the field.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词就是学科名加上常规词尾，因此它的第一项工作是把事物挂到这门学科上。

senses.title: Explaining by social structure
senses.definition: explaining an outcome through structures such as class, housing or institutions rather than personal choice
senses.definitionCN: 通过阶级、住房或制度等结构，而非个人选择，来解释某个结果
senses.example: A sociological account of dropout rates begins with catchment areas.
senses.exampleCN: 对辍学率的社会学解释，从学区划分开始。
senses.why: The discipline's main move is to shift the cause outward, so the adjective most often modifies explanation and account.
senses.whyCN: 这门学科的主要动作是把原因向外移，因此这个形容词最常修饰「解释」与「叙述」。

senses.title: Concerned with groups and institutions
senses.definition: focused on collectivities, organisations and shared practices rather than single persons
senses.definitionCN: 以集体、组织与共同实践为焦点，而非单个个人
senses.example: The sociological view treats a family budget as a product of wages and rents.
senses.exampleCN: 社会学视角把家庭预算看作工资与房租的产物。
senses.why: Once the unit of analysis is the group, the adjective marks that choice of unit.
senses.whyCN: 一旦分析单位是群体，这个形容词就标出这一选择。

senses.title: Using social-science methods
senses.definition: produced with surveys, interviews, observation or official statistics
senses.definitionCN: 通过调查、访谈、观察或官方统计得来的
senses.example: Her evidence was sociological rather than anecdotal: three thousand interviews.
senses.exampleCN: 她的证据是社会学的而非轶事式的：三千份访谈。
senses.why: Methods are what separate this adjective from mere social commentary, so it often appears before data and evidence.
senses.whyCN: 方法把这个形容词与单纯的社会评论区分开，因此它常出现在「数据」「证据」之前。

senses.title: Stressing collective causes
senses.definition: attributing outcomes to shared conditions instead of to individual effort or character
senses.definitionCN: 把结果归于共同处境，而不是个人努力或性格
senses.example: A sociological reading of absenteeism points to shift patterns, not laziness.
senses.exampleCN: 对缺勤的社会学解读指向轮班安排，而不是懒惰。
senses.why: The shift of blame from person to condition is the adjective's most contested use, and it is where arguments usually start.
senses.whyCN: 把责任从人移到处境，是这个形容词最有争议的用法，争论通常也从这里开始。

senses.title: Framing a private trouble as a public issue
senses.titleCN: 把个人困扰框定为公共议题
senses.definition: in the tradition of the sociological imagination, connecting personal difficulty to public arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 在社会学想象力的传统中，把个人困境与公共安排连起来
senses.example: The lecturer gave a sociological name to what students had felt as private failure.
senses.exampleCN: 讲师给学生们的私人挫败感起了一个社会学的名字。
senses.why: The most famous version of this move turns one person's unemployment into a question about how work is distributed.
senses.whyCN: 这一动作最著名的版本，是把一个人的失业变成关于工作如何分配的问题。

senses.title: Relating to a named subfield
senses.definition: describing work inside a specialised branch such as the sociology of medicine or of science
senses.definitionCN: 形容医学社会学或科学社会学等专门分支内的工作
senses.example: The sociological study of diagnosis compared two hospital wards.
senses.exampleCN: 关于诊断的社会学研究比较了两个医院病区。
senses.why: Every institution can be looked at this way, and each such look adds a compound to the adjective's range.
senses.whyCN: 每个制度都可以这样看，每一次这样的看都为这个形容词增加一个复合用法。

senses.title: Treating social facts as external constraints
senses.titleCN: 把社会事实视为外在约束
senses.definition: in the classic formulation, treating social facts as things that constrain individuals from outside
senses.definitionCN: 在经典表述中，把社会事实当作从外部约束个人的事物
senses.example: A sociological treatment of language policy treats the rules as external facts.
senses.exampleCN: 对语言政策的社会学处理把规则当作外在事实。
senses.why: The strongest form of the outward turn is to treat social arrangements as objects with force of their own.
senses.whyCN: 向外移最彻底的形态，是把社会安排当作自有力量的对象。

intro.en: Sociological is sociology plus the adjective ending -ical; the noun is a nineteenth-century compound of Latin and Greek. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: sociological 是 sociology 加形容词词尾；那个名词是十九世纪由拉丁语与希腊语构成的复合词。年代均为约数。

items.en: The root meant 'companion, ally', and its deeper origin is not established; a link to the verb for following is a hypothesis.
items.cn: 这个词根意为「同伴、盟友」，其更早来源未得到证明；把它与表「跟随」的动词相联系的说法只是假说。

items.en: The Greek element meant 'the study of' and had already built names such as biology and geology.
items.cn: 这个希腊成分意为「……之学」，此前已造出 biology、geology 一类名称。

items.en: The noun is generally attributed to Auguste Comte in the eighteen thirties, who wanted a science of society.
items.cn: 这个名词一般认为是孔德在十九世纪三十年代所造，他想要一门关于社会的科学。

items.en: The ending -ical is the ordinary English way of turning a Greek-derived discipline name into an adjective.
items.cn: 词尾是英语把希腊来源的学科名变成形容词的常规方式。

items.en: The adjective spread with the discipline in the twentieth century and now also describes any explanation that stresses social causes.
items.cn: 这个形容词在二十世纪随学科传播，如今也形容任何强调社会成因的解释。

items.en: Source uncertain (first printed use of the adjective and the origin of the companion word): the earliest citation is not settled, and the pre-Latin origin of the root is unknown, so any older form offered for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（这个形容词的最早书证与「同伴」一词的来源）：最早用例尚无定论；该词根在拉丁语之前的来源亦不可考，凡为其提出的更早形式均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds same-root adjectives that are easily confused; group two holds adjectives that also explain by structure.
note.cn: 第一组是同根形容词，极易混淆；第二组是同样以结构作解释的形容词。

entries.definition: Relating to society or to interaction; it can describe a party or a policy, while sociological points to the discipline or its style of explanation.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指与社会的或互动有关的，可形容聚会或政策；而 sociological 指学科或其解释风格。

entries.definition: Relating to society as a whole, often used for large-scale effects; it says nothing about the discipline.
entries.definitionCN: 指整个社会层面的，常用于大规模影响，与学科无关。

entries.definition: The name of the field; the adjective modifies nouns, while this noun can be a subject or an object.
entries.definitionCN: 是领域之名；形容词修饰名词，而这个名词可作主语或宾语。

entries.definition: The practitioner; a sociological argument need not be made by a sociologist.
entries.definitionCN: 指从业者；一个社会学式论证未必由社会学者提出。

entries.definition: Relating to structure in any field, from engineering to economics; sociological specifies a social kind of structure.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指任何领域的结构，从工程到经济；sociological 限定为社会结构。

entries.definition: Relating to established organisations and rules; it is one favourite cause inside sociological explanation.
entries.definitionCN: 指与既有组织及规则有关的，是社会解释中最常用的一类成因。

entries.definition: Relating to the statistical makeup of a population; it supplies evidence rather than the whole explanation.
entries.definitionCN: 指与人口统计构成有关的，提供证据而非整全解释。

entries.definition: Relating to the study of cultures through close observation; it overlaps with sociological work but starts from culture.
entries.definitionCN: 指通过近距离观察研究文化的，与社会学工作重叠但以文化为起点。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real noun base, the real adjective ending and the real phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的名词基底、真实的形容词词尾与真实的短语。

normal.en: The adjective is the discipline name with its regular ending, so it means belonging to that field.
normal.cn: 这个形容词就是学科名加上常规词尾，因此意为「属于该领域」。

normal.en: Its most common job is to mark an explanation that moves the cause from the person to the arrangement.
normal.cn: 它最常见的用途，是标出一种把原因从人移到安排的说明。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: a sociological study, a sociological explanation, sociological factors.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：社会学研究、社会学解释、社会因素。

normal.en: The family runs society, social, societal, sociologist, sociology, sociological.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 society、social、societal、sociologist、sociology、sociological。

normal.en: The famous phrase sociological imagination names the move from a private trouble to a public issue.
normal.cn: 著名说法「社会学想象力」正是指从个人困扰移到公共议题的那一步。

abstract.en: Picture a room with one wall removed, showing the pipes shared with the whole street.
abstract.cn: 想象一间屋子被拆掉一面墙，露出与整条街共用的水管。

abstract.en: Picture a queue whose length is blamed on the timetable rather than on the people in it.
abstract.cn: 想象一条队伍，其长度被归因于时刻表而不是队伍里的人。

abstract.en: Picture a single cough heard as the sound of a whole building.
abstract.cn: 想象一声咳嗽被听成整栋楼的声音。

examples.en: The paper offers a sociological account of why the two districts diverged.
examples.cn: 这篇论文对两个街区为何分化给出了社会学解释。

examples.en: What looks like a personal habit is often a sociological pattern.
examples.cn: 看似个人习惯的东西，往往是社会学的模式。

examples.en: The course trains students to ask sociological questions about ordinary routines.
examples.cn: 这门课训练学生对日常惯例提出社会学问题。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「soci 同伴 + ological 学问的」——从人群与结构看问题的，就是社会学的

root: sociology（拉丁 socius「同伴」+ 希腊「……之学」）+ 形容词词尾；学科名一般认为是孔德所造；socius 更深来源不确定。英语 sociological。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one outward turn of the gaze: the cause is moved from the person to the arrangement. The adjective marks the field, the explanation, the group as unit, the methods, the collective cause, the private trouble made public, a named subfield, and finally social facts treated as external constraints.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿目光向外的一次转动展开：原因从人身上移到安排上。这个形容词依次标出学科、解释、以群体为单位、方法、集体成因、被公共化的个人困扰、命名分支，最后是被当作外在约束的社会事实。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a room with one wall removed, revealing pipes shared with the whole street.
core.cn: 核心意象：一间屋子被拆掉一面墙，露出与整条街共用的水管。

branches.en: THE FIELD AND ITS TOOLS: the discipline's name and the methods that make its claims systematic belong together.
branches.cn: 学科与工具：学科之名与使其主张成为系统的方法，同属一体。

branches.en: STRUCTURE AND UNIT: explaining by structure and choosing the group as the unit are two halves of the same outward turn.
branches.cn: 结构与单位：以结构作解释，与把群体定为分析单位，是同一向外转动的两半。

branches.en: CAUSES OUTSIDE THE PERSON: collective conditions and social facts with force of their own both press on the individual from outside.
branches.cn: 人之外的成因：共同处境与自有力量的社会事实，都从外部压向个人。

branches.en: PRIVATE MADE PUBLIC: a personal failure is renamed as a question about how things are arranged.
branches.cn: 私事公共化：个人的失败被改名成关于事物如何安排的问题。

branches.en: NAMED SUBFIELD: every institution studied this way adds a compound to the adjective's range.
branches.cn: 命名分支：每一个被这样研究的制度，都为这个形容词增添一个复合用法。

intro.en: The adjective is a Greek-derived discipline name plus the ordinary English adjective ending, with a Latin root underneath.
intro.cn: 这个形容词是一个希腊来源的学科名加常规英语形容词词尾，底下还有一个拉丁词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin socius gives society, social, associate and sociable; the Greek element recurs in biology, geology and theology.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 socius 衍生 society、social、associate 与 sociable；那个希腊成分还出现在 biology、geology 与 theology 中。

items.example: The root supplies the social half of the meaning.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供词义中「社会」那一半。

items.example: The element turns a root into a discipline name.
items.exampleCN: 这个成分把词根变成学科名。

items.example: The noun is the base of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是形容词的基底。

items.example: The ending is the standard way to make a discipline adjective in English.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾是英语中把学科名变成形容词的标准方式。

items.example: The adjective also covers any explanation that stresses social causes.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词也覆盖任何强调社会成因的解释。

items.example: The adverb marks an argument made from this angle.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词标出从这一角度作出的论证。

items.example: The adverb is common in research writing.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词在研究写作中很常见。

items.example: The person noun names the practitioner of the field.
items.exampleCN: 指人的名词指该领域的从业者。

items.example: A sociological claim can be made by anyone, not only by this person.
items.exampleCN: 社会学式主张任何人都能提出，不必出自这位从业者。

items.example: A shorter suffix produces the adjective for society as a whole.
items.exampleCN: 一个更短的后缀造出指整个社会的形容词。

definition_zh: 属于；与……有关；适合于（身份、权利等）
definition_en: to belong or relate to something, especially as a right or duty proper to it
core_image: 系在主人身上：权利像链子一样拴在身份或职位上
scene: 老律师翻开地契，指着一行小字讲解权利的归属。 These grazing rights appertain to the owner of the hillside.
sceneCN: 这里 appertain 是「属于、随附于」（第 1 个义项：权利归属）；句意为：这些放牧权属于山坡的所有人。

derivatives.zh: 同根动词（去前缀），义为「关于；属于；适用」
同根派生，义为「切题的；相关的」
pertinent 的名词，义为「相关性；针对性」

senses.title: To belong as a right
senses.definition: to belong to someone as a legal or rightful possession
senses.definitionCN: 作为法定或正当的归属而属于某人
senses.example: The title and its privileges appertain to the eldest son.
senses.exampleCN: 头衔及其特权属于长子。
senses.why: The root tenere means to hold, so rights are pictured as held onto their owner.
senses.whyCN: 词根 tenere 意为握持，权利被想象为紧握在所有者手中。

senses.title: To relate to a subject
senses.definition: to have a connection with a topic or matter
senses.definitionCN: 与某一话题或事项有联系
senses.example: All documents appertaining to the sale were archived.
senses.exampleCN: 与销售有关的所有文件都归了档。
senses.why: Things held together belong to the same cluster of meaning.
senses.whyCN: 被一并握持的东西属于同一意义群。

senses.title: To attach to a position or status
senses.definition: to attach naturally to an office, rank, or role
senses.definitionCN: 天然地附着于某一职位、等级或角色
senses.example: Duties appertain to every office.
senses.exampleCN: 每个职位都自带职责。
senses.why: A role holds its own duties, just as a hand holds tools.
senses.whyCN: 角色握有自己的职责，正如手握着工具。

senses.title: To be proper or fitting
senses.definition: to be appropriate to a person or thing in character
senses.definitionCN: 在性质上与某人某物相称
senses.example: Silence appertains to grief.
senses.exampleCN: 沉默与悲哀相称。
senses.why: What belongs to a thing fits its nature, yielding the propriety sense.
senses.whyCN: 属于某物的就是合其本性的，于是产生相称义。

senses.title: To concern a person indirectly
senses.definition: to touch upon someone's interests without directly involving them
senses.definitionCN: 涉及某人利益但不直接牵连其本人
senses.example: The rumor appertains to her family, not to her.
senses.exampleCN: 传言涉及她的家人，而非她本人。
senses.why: A held thread can lead outward to nearby interests.
senses.whyCN: 被握住的线头可以牵到临近的利益上。

senses.title: To form part of a system
senses.definition: to be one of the elements held within a larger set
senses.definitionCN: 作为更大集合中的一员
senses.example: These rituals appertain to the old religion.
senses.exampleCN: 这些仪式属于旧宗教的一部分。
senses.why: The system holds its parts the way a circle holds its points.
senses.whyCN: 系统握住各部分，如同圆握住它的点。

senses.title: To pertain in legal use
senses.definition: in law, to attach to property or an estate as an incident
senses.definitionCN: 法律上作为附属事项附着于财产或地产
senses.example: Easements appertain to the dominant land.
senses.exampleCN: 地役权附着于需役地。
senses.why: Law fixes holding into formal ownership, sharpening the root image.
senses.whyCN: 法律把「握持」固化为正式的所有，强化了词根意象。

senses.title: To follow from a quality
senses.definition: to result from or accompany an inherent quality
senses.definitionCN: 由内在性质引发或相伴而生
senses.example: Respect appertains to wisdom.
senses.exampleCN: 敬重随智慧而生。
senses.why: Qualities hold their consequences, like a root holds its fruit.
senses.whyCN: 性质握有自己的结果，如同根握着果。

intro.en: Appertain comes from Latin pertinere, to reach through to, hence to belong, from per- plus tenere.
intro.cn: appertain 来自拉丁语 pertinere（贯穿而达，引申为属于），由 per- 加 tenere 构成。

items.en: The reconstructed root *ten- meant to stretch or extend.
items.cn: 重构词根 *ten- 意为伸展、延伸。

items.en: Tenere meant to hold; per- added the idea of thoroughness, so pertinere meant to extend right through.
items.cn: tenere 意为握持；per- 增加彻底之意，pertinere 即「贯穿延伸」。

items.en: Pertinere shifted to mean to belong or relate, the image of a chain held at both ends.
items.cn: pertinere 转义为「属于、相关」，如两端被握住的链条。

items.en: English formed appertain in the fourteenth century from pertain with the Latin-style prefix ap-.
items.cn: 英语十四世纪在 pertain 上加拉丁风格前缀 ap- 构成 appertain。

items.en: It survives mainly in formal and legal writing, meaning to belong or relate to.
items.cn: 如今主要见于正式与法律文体，意为属于或与……有关。

note.en: Appertain belongs to the ten-family of holding words and stands near several belong-words.
note.cn: appertain 属于 ten「握持」词族，并与若干「属于」类词相邻。

normalIntro.en: Anchor appertain in the ten-family of holding words.
normalIntro.cn: 把 appertain 锚定在 ten「握持」词族上。

normal.en: appertain = ap- (toward) + tain (hold): held toward its owner.
normal.cn: appertain = ap-（朝向）+ tain（握持）：被握向它的主人。

normal.en: Same root as contain, retain, obtain — all about holding.
normal.cn: 与 contain、retain、obtain 同根——都关乎握持。

normal.en: Classic pattern: rights appertain to the office.
normal.cn: 经典句式：rights appertain to the office（权利随职位而来）。

normal.en: pertain is the plainer twin; appertain is the legal, formal one.
normal.cn: pertain 是朴素的孪生词；appertain 更法律化、更正式。

normal.en: pertinent, the adjective cousin, means relevant.
normal.cn: 形容词亲戚 pertinent 意为切题的。

abstract.en: A crown held in a firm grip — the grip is who it appertains to.
abstract.cn: 一只手紧握王冠——握住的那只手就是它的归属。

abstract.en: A chain linking a key to a belt: the key appertains to the belt.
abstract.cn: 链条把钥匙拴在腰带上：钥匙属于腰带。

abstract.en: Appertain sounds like 'a purse-tain': the purse holds what belongs to you.
abstract.cn: appertain 听着像 a purse-tain：钱包握着属于你的东西。

examples.en: Certain duties appertain to the office of chairman.
examples.cn: 某些职责是主席职位固有的。

examples.en: Please file everything appertaining to this contract.
examples.cn: 请把与这份合同有关的一切归档。

examples.en: The honors that appertain to rank were never his goal.
examples.cn: 随地位而来的荣耀从来不是他的目标。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿婆疼」——阿婆疼谁，家产就「属于」谁，谐音仅助记，不是词源。

sensesIntro.en: From rights held by an owner, appertain extends to subjects related, roles and their duties, fittingness, indirect concern, membership in a system, legal incidents, and qualities and their consequences.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「权利握在所有者手中」出发，appertain 依次延伸到相关主题、职位职责、相称性、间接关涉、系统成员、法律附属以及性质与其结果。

branches.en: formal ownership: rights, offices, legal incidents
branches.cn: 正式的所有：权利、职位、法律附属

branches.en: relevance: matters and interests held in the same hand
branches.cn: 相关性：被同一只手握住的事项与利益

branches.en: what fits a thing belongs to it
branches.cn: 相称之物即属于此物

branches.en: membership held within a larger system
branches.cn: 被更大系统握住的成员身份

branches.en: qualities holding their own consequences
branches.cn: 性质握有自己的结果

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tenere（握持）是 contain、retain、tenant 等词的母词根。

同根派生，义为「切题的；相关的」

definition_zh: 地层学；层序学；考古地层；分层结构
definition_en: the study of the order, position and age of layered deposits, used in geology and archaeology to establish sequences
core_image: 一面陡壁被刮平，深浅不同的土带一层压一层，最下面的一层最老，最上面的一层最新
scene: 探方一侧的土壁被刮得平整，深浅不同的土带一层压着一层，最底下的土色最深。 The exposed wall shows stratigraphy as bands of soil stacked oldest at the bottom and youngest at the top.
sceneCN: 这里 stratigraphy 指「堆积层按上下顺序排列所构成的层序及其研究」（第 2 个义项：地层序列本身）；句意为刮平的土壁上，不同颜色的土层依次叠压，最下面的最老、最上面的最新。可辨识物件：土壁、土层带、刮刀、比例尺、层位线。

pos.zh: 地层序列；层位关系（不可数）

derivatives.zh: 地层的；层序的
地层学家
层；地层
使分层；按层排列

senses.title: The study of layered order
senses.titleCN: 地层学：研究层序的学科
senses.definition: the branch of geology and archaeology that studies how layers form, succeed and correlate
senses.definitionCN: 研究层如何形成、先后相接与对比的地质学与考古学分支
senses.example: Stratigraphy tells us which deposit formed first.
senses.exampleCN: 地层学告诉我们哪一层堆积先形成。
senses.why: Stratum is Latin for a layer spread out, from sternere, to spread; -graphy is Greek for writing, so the word means writing about layers.
senses.whyCN: stratum 是拉丁语「铺开的一层」，出自 sternere「铺展」；-graphy 是希腊语「书写」，因此这个词意为「对层的书写」。

senses.title: The layering itself
senses.definition: the actual arrangement of layers at a place, read from a section or a core
senses.definitionCN: 某地点通过剖面或岩芯读出的层的实际排列
senses.example: The stratigraphy at the trench edge is unusually clear.
senses.exampleCN: 探方边缘的层序异常清楚。
senses.why: The same word names both the discipline and its object, just as geology names both a science and a rock face.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词既指学科，也指其对象，正如 geology 既指地质学也指一处岩面。

senses.title: Archaeological stratigraphy
senses.titleCN: 考古地层：人类活动形成的堆积层序
senses.definition: the sequence of deposits made by human activity, such as floors, fills and dumps, and their cut relationships
senses.definitionCN: 由人类活动形成的堆积顺序，如居住面、填土与废弃物，及其切压关系
senses.example: Archaeological stratigraphy records a floor cut by a later pit.
senses.exampleCN: 考古地层记录了一个被后期灰坑打破的居住面。
senses.why: People also make layers, and they cut into older ones; the discipline reads both accumulation and intrusion.
senses.whyCN: 人也会制造层，并切穿更早的层；这门学科既读堆积，也读侵入。

senses.title: Correlation between sections
senses.titleCN: 地层对比：把分离的剖面接起来
senses.definition: the matching of layers across different places so that separate sequences can be joined
senses.definitionCN: 把不同地点的层相互对应，使分离的序列得以连接
senses.example: Stratigraphy links the two sides of the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 地层对比把谷地两侧连接起来。
senses.why: A layer exposed in one place is not the same layer everywhere; correlation uses colour, texture and contained finds to match them.
senses.whyCN: 在一处露出的层并不等于各处的同一层；对比依靠颜色、质地与所含发现物把它们配对。

senses.title: Rock-layer geology
senses.titleCN: 岩层学：地质上的成层研究
senses.definition: the geological study of sedimentary rock layers and their ages
senses.definitionCN: 对沉积岩层及其年代的地质学研究
senses.example: Stratigraphy placed the limestone below the sandstone.
senses.exampleCN: 地层学把石灰岩定在砂岩之下。
senses.why: The discipline began with rock, not with graves; sedimentary layers accumulate in order and carry the oldest at the bottom.
senses.whyCN: 这门学科起初研究岩石，而非墓葬；沉积层按顺序堆积，最老的位于底部。

senses.title: The law of superposition
senses.titleCN: 叠加律：上覆者晚于下伏者
senses.definition: the principle that in an undisturbed sequence the upper layer is younger than the layer below it
senses.definitionCN: 在未受扰动的序列中，上层晚于其下层的原理
senses.example: Stratigraphy assumed the rule held until a burrow was found.
senses.exampleCN: 地层学一直假定这条规律成立，直到发现一处动物洞穴。
senses.why: The rule is the whole basis of relative dating, and its exceptions, such as pits and burrows, are what fieldworkers watch for.
senses.whyCN: 这条规律是相对测年的全部基础，而灰坑与洞穴等例外正是田野工作者要留意的。

senses.title: Reading a section
senses.titleCN: 判读剖面：清理剖面并绘出层界
senses.definition: the practical skill of interpreting a cleaned section and drawing its layer boundaries
senses.definitionCN: 判读清理过的剖面并绘出层界线的实践技能
senses.example: Her stratigraphy of the section was checked by a second recorder.
senses.exampleCN: 她对剖面的层序判读由第二位记录员复核。
senses.why: Layers are not labelled in the ground; the reader must decide where one ends and the next begins, and that decision is an interpretation.
senses.whyCN: 层在地下并没有标签；判读者必须决定一层在哪里结束、下一层在哪里开始，而这个决定本身就是解释。

senses.title: Layered structure as metaphor
senses.titleCN: 分层结构：比喻意义上的层次
senses.definition: any system read as stacked levels, such as a text, a society or a set of rules
senses.definitionCN: 任何被当作叠置层次来读的系统，如文本、社会或一套规则
senses.example: The historian applied stratigraphy to the layers of the law.
senses.exampleCN: 这位历史学者把分层结构用于法律的各个层次。
senses.why: Once layers mean order, the image travels: anything built up over time can be read from bottom to top.
senses.whyCN: 一旦层意味着顺序，这个意象就会迁移：任何随时间累积的东西都可以从下往上读。

intro.en: Stratigraphy joins Latin stratum, a layer, with Greek -graphia, writing. The term was coined for geology in the nineteenth century and later borrowed by archaeology. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: stratigraphy 把拉丁 stratum「层」与希腊 -graphia「书写」连在一起。这个词十九世纪为地质学而造，后来被考古学借用。年代均为约数。

items.en: Sternere meant to spread out or lay flat; its participle stratus gave stratum, a layer spread over a surface.
items.cn: sternere 意为铺开、摊平；其分词 stratus 产生 stratum，即铺在表面上的一层。

items.en: Stratum named a bed or layer, and the plural strata became the standard word for rock and soil layers.
items.cn: stratum 指一层或一层床，复数 strata 成为岩石与土壤层的标准词。

items.en: Greek graphein, to write, gave -graphia, a writing or description; geography, biography and stratigraphy all use it.
items.cn: 希腊 graphein「书写」产生 -graphia，即书写或描述；geography、biography、stratigraphy 都用它。

items.en: Geologists needed a word for the description of layered rock, and stratigraphy supplied it; the principles of superposition and correlation came with it.
items.cn: 地质学家需要一个词来描述成层岩石，stratigraphy 正好补上；叠加与对比原理随之而来。

items.en: Archaeologists borrowed the term for human deposits, adding cuts and fills to the geological vocabulary of layers.
items.cn: 考古学者把这个词借用于人类堆积，在层的地质词汇中加入切与填。

items.en: Source uncertain: the coinage is generally attributed to nineteenth-century geologists, but no single author and date are agreed, and the first use in archaeology is also undocumented.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这个词的创造一般归给十九世纪的地质学家，但没有公认的单一作者与年代，它在考古学中的首次使用同样缺乏记载。

note.en: The first group holds terms from the same layer stock; the second group holds words for ordering and for layers.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「层」词干的术语；第二组是表示排序与层的词。

entries.definition: A single layer; stratigraphy is the study of many layers and their order.
entries.definitionCN: 单独的一层；stratigraphy 是研究多层及其顺序的学科。

entries.definition: Relating to stratigraphy; it describes a relationship or a position, not the discipline.
entries.definitionCN: 与地层学有关的；它描述关系或位置，而非学科本身。

entries.definition: The atmospheric layer named from the same Latin word for layer, but it has nothing to do with deposits.
entries.definitionCN: 大气层名，借用了同一个拉丁「层」词，但与堆积无关。

entries.definition: The study of the earth as a whole; stratigraphy is one of its core methods.
entries.definitionCN: 研究整个地球的学科；地层学是其核心方法之一。

entries.definition: The order in which things follow one another; stratigraphy is the reading of that order in deposits.
entries.definitionCN: 事物相继出现的顺序；地层学是从堆积中读出这个顺序。

entries.definition: The layer and association in which an object lies; stratigraphy supplies the framework for context.
entries.definitionCN: 物件所在的层与共存关系；地层学为情境提供框架。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the spreading root, the writing suffix, superposition and the two-section match.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：表示铺展的词根、书写后缀、叠加律，以及两个剖面的对比。

normal.en: sternere, to spread, gives stratum: a layer is something spread over a surface.
normal.cn: sternere「铺展」派生 stratum：层就是铺在表面上的东西。

normal.en: -graphy is writing: stratigraphy is writing about layers.
normal.cn: -graphy 是书写：stratigraphy 就是书写层。

normal.en: Superposition: in an undisturbed stack, the top is youngest and the bottom is oldest.
normal.cn: 叠加律：在未受扰动的叠层中，最上面最新，最下面最老。

normal.en: Pits and burrows cut older layers, and those cuts must be read as later events.
normal.cn: 灰坑与洞穴切穿更老的层，这些切口必须当作更晚的事件来读。

normal.en: Correlation matches colour, texture and finds to join separate sections.
normal.cn: 对比依靠颜色、质地与发现物，把分离的剖面接起来。

abstract.en: Abstractly, stratigraphy is time made visible as order: the vertical axis is history.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，地层学是把时间变成可见的顺序：竖轴就是历史。

abstract.en: It is the art of reading interruption: what cuts what tells you what came later.
abstract.cn: 它是判读打断的技艺：谁切穿了谁，就告诉你谁更晚。

abstract.en: Any archive, text or institution built up over time can be read as a stack of layers.
abstract.cn: 任何随时间累积的档案、文本或制度，都可以当作一摞层来读。

examples.en: The pit cuts the floor, so by stratigraphy the pit is later.
examples.cn: 灰坑切穿了居住面，因此按地层关系灰坑更晚。

examples.en: Without stratigraphy, the finds would have no order at all.
examples.cn: 没有地层，这些发现物就完全没有顺序。

examples.en: The two sections were correlated by their stratigraphy.
examples.cn: 两个剖面通过地层对比被连接起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「strata（层）+ graphy（写）」——把一层层土写成一张剖面图 → 地层学

root: 拉丁 stratum「铺开的一层」（出自 sternere「铺展」）+ 希腊 -graphia「书写、描述」；字面为「对层的书写」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one stack: the discipline reads the layers, the layers themselves, human deposits, matched sections, rock strata, the rule of superposition, the act of reading and the metaphor of levels.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一叠层展开：学科读层，层本身，人类堆积，剖面对比，岩层，叠加律，判读行为，以及层次的比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cleaned wall of soil, bands stacking oldest to youngest.
core.cn: 核心意象：一面刮净的土壁，土带自老至新依次叠压。

branches.en: THE DISCIPLINE AND THE ROCK: the same reading applies to soil and to sedimentary stone.
branches.cn: 学科与岩石：同一套读法既用于土壤，也用于沉积岩。

branches.en: NATURAL AND HUMAN STACKS: people add floors, fills and cuts to the natural sequence.
branches.cn: 自然叠层与人类叠层：人在自然序列上添加居住面、填土与切口。

branches.en: JOINING SECTIONS: correlation turns separate walls into one regional sequence.
branches.cn: 连接剖面：对比把分离的土壁连成一个区域序列。

branches.en: THE RULE AND THE READING: superposition gives the logic, and the recorder applies it at the section.
branches.cn: 规律与判读：叠加律提供逻辑，记录员在剖面上应用它。

branches.en: LAYERS EVERYWHERE: once order is visible as a stack, any accumulated system can borrow the image.
branches.cn: 处处有层：一旦顺序可见为一摞，任何累积系统都能借用这个意象。

intro.en: Stratigraphy is a Latin-Greek compound, and both halves build many English technical words.
intro.cn: stratigraphy 是一个拉丁—希腊复合词，两半都构成大量英语技术词。

latinIntro.en: Latin sternere, to spread, gives stratum, stratus and stratify; Greek graphein, to write, gives -graphy, -graph and graphic. The compound names the description of layers.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 sternere「铺展」衍生 stratum、stratus、stratify；希腊 graphein「书写」衍生 -graphy、-graph、graphic。这个复合词命名对层的描述。

items.example: Sternere gives stratum and prostration.
items.exampleCN: sternere 衍生 stratum 与 prostration。

items.structure: stratum (Latin noun, a layer spread out)
items.example: Each stratum held a different kind of soil.
items.exampleCN: 每一层土质都不同。

items.example: The strata dip toward the river.
items.exampleCN: 这些层向河流方向倾斜。

items.example: Water and wind stratify the sediment.
items.exampleCN: 水和风使沉积物分层。

items.example: The stratified sand records repeated floods.
items.exampleCN: 分层砂记录了一次次洪水。

items.example: Stratification takes centuries in still water.
items.exampleCN: 在静水中分层需要数百年。

items.example: Graphein supplies the -graphy of many fields.
items.exampleCN: graphein 为许多领域提供 -graphy。

items.meaning: writing or description of a field
items.meaningCN: 某一领域的书写或描述
items.example: Geography and stratigraphy share the suffix.
items.exampleCN: geography 与 stratigraphy 共用这个后缀。

items.meaning: relating to layers or their order
items.example: The stratigraphic boundary is marked in red.
items.exampleCN: 地层界线用红色标出。

items.example: The stratigrapher checked the section.
items.exampleCN: 地层专家检查了这个剖面。

definition_zh: 高架渠；输水道；导水管
definition_en: a structure that carries water over a long distance, especially a bridge-like channel
core_image: 跨谷的石桥上驮着一条水路：水在高处流过山谷
scene: 古城郊外，石拱桥高耸，桥顶的水槽直通城里的喷泉。 The Roman aqueduct still carries water to the fountain.
sceneCN: 这里 aqueduct 是「输水道、高架渠」（第 1 个义项：引水的桥式建筑）；句意为：罗马时代的输水道仍把水送到喷泉。

derivatives.zh: 同根词（aqu- 水），义为「水的；水生的」
同根词（duc- 引导），义为「导管；管道」
同根近形词，义为「导管；水道」
同构复合词，义为「高架桥」

senses.title: A bridge-like water channel
senses.definition: a raised structure with a channel for carrying water across a valley
senses.definitionCN: 带水槽的高架结构，跨谷输水
senses.example: The aqueduct spans the valley on stone arches.
senses.exampleCN: 输水道以石拱跨越山谷。
senses.why: The root ducere means to lead: the structure leads water where it must go.
senses.whyCN: 词根 ducere 意为引导：这种结构把水引向该去的地方。

senses.title: A conduit or pipe system
senses.definition: any pipe or channel built to transport water
senses.definitionCN: 为输水而修建的管道或水槽
senses.example: A modern aqueduct supplies the whole city.
senses.exampleCN: 一条现代化输水道供给全市用水。
senses.why: Leading water needs only a channel; the material may change.
senses.whyCN: 引水只需要一条通道，材质可以变化。

senses.title: An ancient Roman engineering work
senses.definition: one of the famous Roman structures that supplied cities with water
senses.definitionCN: 为城市供水的著名罗马建筑之一
senses.example: Tourists photograph the aqueduct at Segovia.
senses.exampleCN: 游客在塞哥维亚拍摄输水道。
senses.why: Rome built the model case, so the word recalls it.
senses.whyCN: 罗马建造了典范工程，这个词便让人想起它。

senses.title: An anatomy duct
senses.definition: a small natural passage carrying fluid in the body
senses.definitionCN: 体内输送液体的小型天然管道
senses.example: The aqueduct of the brain channels cerebrospinal fluid.
senses.exampleCN: 大脑导水管输送脑脊液。
senses.why: Bodies also lead water, so anatomy borrowed the engineering word.
senses.whyCN: 身体也要引水，解剖学便借用了工程术语。

senses.title: A long-distance supply line
senses.definition: a large-scale channel moving water from a distant source to cities or farms
senses.definitionCN: 把水从远处水源输往城市或农田的大型渠道
senses.example: The state aqueduct feeds farms in the dry valley.
senses.exampleCN: 州立输水道滋养干旱山谷中的农田。
senses.why: Leading water across regions extends the original crossing.
senses.whyCN: 跨区域引水是「跨越」一词的延伸。

senses.title: A symbol of engineering skill
senses.definition: an object used figuratively to represent great civil engineering
senses.definitionCN: 在比喻中代表伟大土木工程的事物
senses.example: The dam became the aqueduct of our age.
senses.exampleCN: 大坝成了我们这个时代的输水道。
senses.why: The perfect model case becomes the measuring stick for others.
senses.whyCN: 典范案例成为衡量其他工程的标尺。

senses.title: A lifeline of a city
senses.definition: the essential route without which a settlement cannot survive
senses.definitionCN: 定居点赖以生存的必需通道
senses.example: Cutting the aqueduct would starve the town.
senses.exampleCN: 切断输水道将令城镇陷入绝境。
senses.why: Because led water is led life, the channel becomes a lifeline.
senses.whyCN: 引来的既是水也是命，渠道因此成为生命线。

senses.title: A heritage monument
senses.definition: a preserved ancient structure valued as cultural heritage
senses.definitionCN: 作为文化遗产被保存的古代建筑
senses.example: The aqueduct was restored last decade.
senses.exampleCN: 输水道在上个十年得到修复。
senses.why: What once led water now leads memory and tourism.
senses.whyCN: 昔日引水，今日引来的记忆与游人。

intro.en: Aqueduct joins Latin aqua, water, and ductus, a leading, from ducere, to lead.
intro.cn: aqueduct 由拉丁语 aqua（水）与 ductus（引导）复合而成，后者来自 ducere（引导）。

items.en: The reconstructed roots *akwa- (water) and *deuk- (to lead) underlie both parts.
items.cn: 重构词根 *akwa-（水）与 *deuk-（引导）分别支撑两个部分。

items.en: Aqua meant water; ducere meant to lead or draw.
items.cn: aqua 意为水；ducere 意为引导、牵引。

items.en: Aquaeductus named the channels Rome built to lead water into cities.
items.cn: aquaeductus 指罗马为城市引水修建的渠道。

items.en: English took aqueduct in the sixteenth century, partly through French, partly from Latin.
items.cn: 英语十六世纪经法语或直接从拉丁语借入 aqueduct。

items.en: It now covers ancient monuments, modern supply channels, and anatomical ducts.
items.cn: 如今涵盖古迹、现代输水渠道与解剖学导管。

note.en: Aqueduct combines two famous roots and is often confused with viaduct.
note.cn: aqueduct 复合了两个著名词根，且常与 viaduct 混淆。

definition_zh: 联邦制；联邦主义；中央与地方分权的原则；（组织内部的）分权体制
definition_en: a system of government in which power is divided between a central authority and constituent units, or the principle or movement that advocates such a division
core_image: 一张地图被两种颜色的铅笔画过，同一条河的上游与下游各有自己的税则，中央只在交界处盖章

sceneCN: 这里 federalism 指中央与地方分权的政府体制（第 1 个义项：联邦制的权力划分）；句意为代表们用两种颜色在大地图上标出联邦制留给中央与各州各自的权限。图中可辨识物件：大地图、双色铅笔、州界线、盖章处。

senses.title: Power split between centre and units
senses.titleCN: 中央与成员单位分权的政府体制
senses.definition: a system in which a central government and regional governments each hold powers that the other cannot simply take away
senses.definitionCN: 一种中央政府对地区政府各自握有对方不能随意剥夺的权力的制度
senses.example: On the map the delegates drew two colours to show what federalism left to each level of government.
senses.exampleCN: 代表们用两种颜色在大地图上标出联邦制留给中央与各州各自的权限。
senses.why: The word is built on foedus 'treaty': units that once stood apart bind themselves by an agreement that each side keeps, so power is shared by contract rather than granted from above.
senses.whyCN: 这个词建立在 foedus「盟约」之上：原本分立的单位以一份各方都保留的约定结合，因此权力是按契约共享，而非由上而下授予。

senses.title: The principle, not the machine
senses.titleCN: 作为政治原则的联邦主义
senses.definition: the doctrine that governing power should be divided among levels rather than concentrated in one
senses.definitionCN: 主张治理权力应在多个层级间划分、而非集中于一处的主张
senses.example: Her essay defended federalism as a check on any single capital.
senses.exampleCN: 她的文章把联邦主义辩护为对任何单一权力中心的制约。
senses.why: A working arrangement can also be argued for as a value, and in that shift the noun stops describing an institution and starts describing a belief.
senses.whyCN: 一套运作安排也可以被当作价值来论证；在这一转手里，名词不再描述制度，而开始描述信念。

senses.title: A movement seeking union
senses.titleCN: 谋求结成联邦的政治运动
senses.definition: a movement that works to bring separate states or nations into a single federal union
senses.definitionCN: 致力于把分立的国家或民族结合为一个联邦联盟的运动
senses.example: Post-war federalism pushed for a directly elected European assembly.
senses.exampleCN: 战后的联邦主义推动了直选欧洲议会的出现。
senses.why: If a treaty can bind units, then someone will want to extend the treaty to new units, and the noun becomes the name of that campaign.
senses.whyCN: 既然盟约能约束各单位，就会有人想把盟约扩展到新的单位，名词于是成为那场运动的名字。

senses.title: The early American party line
senses.titleCN: 美国早期联邦党人主张的用法（专名义）
senses.definition: the programme of the late eighteenth-century American party that wanted a stronger central government
senses.definitionCN: 十八世纪末美国那个主张强化中央政府的政党所持的纲领
senses.example: Textbooks use federalism for the programme that funded a national bank and a standing fleet.
senses.exampleCN: 教科书用联邦主义指那套为国家银行与常备舰队提供资金的纲领。
senses.why: A party took the adjective as its name, and its programme inherited the noun, so one capitalised use points to a specific historical camp.
senses.whyCN: 一个政党把这个形容词当作党名，其纲领便继承了名词，因此有一个大写用法指向特定的历史阵营。

senses.title: Power sharing inside an organisation
senses.definition: the division of authority between a central body and regional branches of a union, party or church
senses.definitionCN: 工会、政党或教会中中央机构与地区分支之间的权限划分
senses.example: The union's federalism gave each branch the right to set its own strike ballot.
senses.exampleCN: 这个工会的联邦制让每个分支都有权自行决定是否投票罢工。
senses.why: The pattern of divided authority is easy to copy into any large body, so the noun travels from states to offices without changing shape.
senses.whyCN: 分权的模式很容易被复制到任何大型组织，于是这个名词从国家移到办公室而形状不变。

senses.title: Fiscal federalism
senses.titleCN: 财政职能在各级政府间的划分
senses.definition: the arrangement by which taxing and spending duties are allocated among levels of government
senses.definitionCN: 税收与支出职责在各级政府之间分配的制度安排
senses.example: Economists study fiscal federalism to see which level should pay for schools.
senses.exampleCN: 经济学家研究财政联邦主义，以判断应由哪一级政府为学校出资。
senses.why: Money follows the same line as law: if each level keeps its own revenue, it can act without asking the centre for every sum.
senses.whyCN: 钱跟着同一条线走：每一级保留自己的收入，就能不经中央逐笔拨款而行动。

senses.title: A doctrine of limited central power
senses.titleCN: 宪法解释中限制中央权力的主张
senses.definition: a reading of a constitution that reserves broad powers to the states and reads central powers narrowly
senses.definitionCN: 一种把广泛权力保留给各州、对中央权力作狭窄解释的宪法读法
senses.example: The court's federalism argument blocked the federal agency from regulating local water.
senses.exampleCN: 法院依联邦主义的主张，禁止联邦机构监管地方水域。
senses.why: If the split is written into a constitution, judges must decide where the line falls, and the noun becomes an argument about how to read that line.
senses.whyCN: 既然分权写进了宪法，法官就必须判定界线在哪里，名词于是变成一场关于如何读这条线的论证。

senses.title: A design choice in comparative politics
senses.titleCN: 比较政治中的一种制度设计选择
senses.definition: one of the institutional models a divided or multi-ethnic state may adopt, alongside unitary and confederal arrangements
senses.definitionCN: 分裂社会或多民族国家可选的一种制度模型，与单一制和邦联制并列
senses.example: Comparing federalism with unitary rule shows how many veto points each design creates.
senses.exampleCN: 把联邦制与单一制相比，可以看出每种设计产生多少个否决点。
senses.why: Once the arrangement is treated as a choice rather than a fact, the noun can be listed beside rival designs and weighed by their effects.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这套安排被当作可选而非既定，名词就能与竞争设计并列，并按效果被衡量。

intro.en: Federalism is federal plus -ism; federal goes back through French to Latin foedus 'treaty, league'. The political noun was coined in the late eighteenth century, when American writers needed a name for divided sovereignty.
intro.cn: federalism 由 federal 加表示学说的后缀构成；federal 经法语上溯到拉丁 foedus「盟约、同盟」。这个政治名词在十八世纪后期被造出，当时美国作者需要一个名字来称呼被分割的主权。

items.en: Foedus, genitive foederis, meant a treaty, league or covenant. The word names the bond itself, which is why federal arrangements are described as contractual rather than hierarchical.
items.cn: foedus（属格 foederis）意为盟约、同盟、约定。这个词命名的是纽带本身，因此联邦安排被描述为契约式而非层级式。

items.en: It is generally thought that foedus shares a root with fides 'faith, trust', from a reconstructed element meaning 'to trust'; the shared root is a reasoned reconstruction, not a recorded form.
items.cn: 一般认为 foedus 与 fides「信义、信任」共享一个词根，该词根出自一个表示「信任」的重构成分；这一共享词根属有理据的重构，并非有记录的词形。

items.en: French fédéral and the earlier Latin-derived foederalis carried the sense 'of a league' into early modern usage, still close to treaty and alliance.
items.cn: 法语 fédéral 以及更早由拉丁派生的 foederalis 把「同盟的」这一义带入近代早期用法，仍贴近盟约与结盟。

items.en: Federalism appears in English political writing in the seventeen-eighties and nineties, naming the division of sovereignty between a national government and the states.
items.cn: federalism 在十八世纪八九十年代的英语政治写作中出现，指国家政府与各州之间对主权的划分。

items.en: American writers also used it, often capitalised, for the programme of the party that favoured a stronger centre, which is how one proper-noun sense arose.
items.cn: 美国作者也用它（常大写）指那个偏向强化中央的政党的纲领，专名的一义即由此而来。

items.en: The earliest citation is not precisely dated: the seventeen-eighties figure is approximate, and earlier isolated uses in translation remain unverified.
items.cn: 最早书证没有精确年代：十八世纪八十年代只是约数；更早散见于译本中的用例尚未得到证实。

note.en: The first group is built on the same treaty word and is often mixed up; the second group names other ways of distributing authority.
note.cn: 第一组同出那个表示盟约的词，常被混淆；第二组是其他分配权力的方式。

entries.definition: The adjective describing anything belonging to a union of states, or to the central level of one.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，描述属于州联合体的事物，或属于其中央层级的事物。

entries.definition: The union itself as an entity, such as a national federation of clubs; federalism is the principle behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 指联合体这个实体，如全国性俱乐部联合会；联邦主义是其背后的原则。

entries.definition: A supporter of the arrangement, or the adjective describing such a position.
entries.definitionCN: 指这种安排的支持者，或描述该立场的形容词。

entries.definition: A looser union in which the units keep most sovereignty and the centre depends on their consent.
entries.definitionCN: 更松散的联合，各单位保留大部分主权，中央依赖它们的同意。

entries.definition: The Latin noun for treaty or league; it is the source of the whole English group.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语中表示盟约或同盟的名词，是整个英语词组的来源。

entries.definition: The handing of specified powers from a central parliament to regional bodies that remain subordinate.
entries.definitionCN: 中央议会把特定权力交给仍处于从属地位的地区机构。

entries.definition: Moving offices and decisions away from a capital without giving regions constitutional protection.
entries.definitionCN: 把机构与决策从首都外移，但不给地区宪法层面的保障。

entries.definition: A state in which one parliament holds final authority and regions act only as its agents.
entries.definitionCN: 由一个议会掌握最终权威、地区仅作为其代理人的国家。

entries.definition: The right of a group to govern its own affairs within limits set elsewhere.
entries.definitionCN: 在外部设定的限度内自行管理事务的权利。

entries.definition: The doctrine that decisions should be made in one place and applied uniformly.
entries.definitionCN: 主张决策应在一处作出并统一施行的主张。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin treaty word, the real family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁「盟约」词、真实的同族词与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: Foedus is Latin for treaty, so federalism is government by a kept agreement.
normal.cn: foedus 是拉丁语「盟约」，所以联邦制就是靠一份被各方共同遵守的约定来治理。

normal.en: The family runs federal, federalism, federalist, federalise, federalisation and federation.
normal.cn: 同族词有 federal、federalism、federalist、federalise、federalisation 与 federation。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the technical senses: fiscal federalism, dual federalism, cooperative federalism.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出技术义：财政联邦主义、二元联邦主义、合作联邦主义。

normal.en: The same root gives fides, faith or trust, which is why a treaty and a pledge sound alike in Latin.
normal.cn: 同一词根还给出 fides「信义」，所以在拉丁语里盟约与誓言听起来相近。

normal.en: One capital letter changes the reference: Federalism with a capital names a historical party line.
normal.cn: 一个大写字母就换了所指：大写的联邦主义指历史上的一个党派纲领。

abstract.en: Picture a map inked in two colours, neither able to erase the other.
abstract.cn: 想象一张被两种颜色画过的地图，哪一种都擦不掉另一种。

abstract.en: Picture a rope bridge whose planks are owned by the villages at either end, not by the river.
abstract.cn: 想象一座绳桥，桥板归两端村子所有，而不归河流所有。

abstract.en: Picture two keys to one door, cut differently, so neither side can open it alone.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门有两把齿形不同的钥匙，任何一方都无法独自打开。

examples.en: The constitution's federalism is visible in its list of state powers.
examples.cn: 宪法中的联邦制体现在它所列的州权清单上。

examples.en: Fiscal federalism explains why schools depend on local taxes.
examples.cn: 财政联邦主义解释了学校为何依赖地方税收。

examples.en: Supporters argued that federalism protects minorities from distant majorities.
examples.cn: 支持者认为联邦制能保护少数群体不受远方多数的支配。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「federal（联邦的）+ ism（主义）」——主张中央与地方分权的制度 → 联邦制

root: 拉丁 foedus（属格 foederis）「盟约、同盟」，一般认为与 fides「信义」共享一个表示「信任」的重构词根 → 法语 fédéral → 英语 federal → federalism。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one line drawn on a map: the line divides power, becomes a principle, then a campaign, then a party programme, then a rule inside a union, a budget rule, a judicial reading, and finally a model on a shelf of designs.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕地图上画的一条线：这条线分割权力，随后成为原则、运动、党派纲领、工会内部的章程、预算规则、司法读法，最后成为设计清单上的一种模型。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one line on a map, drawn by two hands, that neither side may rub out.
core.cn: 核心意象：地图上一条由两只手共同画的线，任何一方都擦不掉。

branches.en: STRUCTURE AND MODEL: a working arrangement and a design choice are the same line seen in a country or on a shelf.
branches.cn: 制度与模型：运作中的安排与清单上的设计，是同一条线出现在一个国家或一个架子上。

branches.en: THE ARGUMENT: once the line is defended as a value, the noun stops describing and starts advocating.
branches.cn: 论证：一旦这条线被当作价值来辩护，名词就不再描述，而开始主张。

branches.en: TWO CAMPAIGNS: a movement extending the treaty outward, and a party defending a stronger centre inward.
branches.cn: 两场运动：一场向外扩展盟约，一场向内维护更强的中央。

branches.en: THE OFFICE COPY: states are replaced by branches, and the same line is drawn inside a union.
branches.cn: 办公室的复本：国家换成分支，同一条线被画在工会内部。

branches.en: MONEY AND LAW: budgets and judicial readings are the line turned into arithmetic and into interpretation.
branches.cn: 钱与法：预算与司法读法，是这条线变成算术与解释的两副面孔。

intro.en: Federalism rests on a Latin treaty noun that also builds federal, federation and confederation, plus a doctrine suffix.
intro.cn: 联邦主义依赖一个拉丁语「盟约」名词，它同时构成 federal、federation 与 confederation，末尾再加表示学说的后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin foedus, genitive foederis, gives foederalis and through French federal; the same root is behind fides 'faith'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 foedus（属格 foederis）给出 foederalis，再经法语成为 federal；同一词根还在 fides「信义」背后。

items.exampleCN: 它把盟约名词变成形容词。

items.example: The adjective describes the union and its centre.

items.example: It names the principle as a whole.

items.example: The noun can mean the machine or the belief.
items.exampleCN: 名词既可指机器，也可指信念。

items.example: It names the advocate.
items.exampleCN: 它命名主张者。

items.meaningCN: 联邦主义者；联邦主义的
items.example: One form serves person and adjective.
items.exampleCN: 一个词形兼指人与形容词。

items.example: It forms the verb of conversion.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示转变的动词。

items.example: The verb names the act of drawing the line.
items.exampleCN: 动词命名画这条线的动作。

items.exampleCN: 它在「邦联」中标出更松的结合。

definition_en: a pleasant noticeable smell, especially from food or drink
core_image: 咖啡壶里飘出的暖香
scene: 清晨的厨房里，水汽正从壶嘴袅袅升起。 The aroma of fresh coffee filled the room.
sceneCN: 这里 aroma 是「香气」（第 1 个义项：怡人的气味）；句意是新煮咖啡的香气弥漫房间。

senses.title: A pleasant smell from food or drink
senses.definition: a strong, pleasant smell, especially one given off by cooking, coffee or wine
senses.definitionCN: 浓郁怡人的气味，尤指烹饪、咖啡或葡萄酒散发的香味
senses.example: The aroma of baking bread drifted down the stairs.
senses.exampleCN: 烤面包的香气飘下楼梯。
senses.why: The Greek word first meant spice, the very source of pleasant smells.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语原词本指「香料」，正是怡人气味的源头。

senses.title: A distinctive pervading quality
senses.definition: a noticeable quality or atmosphere surrounding a person, place or thing
senses.definitionCN: 环绕人、地、物的可感知特质或气氛
senses.example: The old hotel keeps the aroma of a vanished era.
senses.exampleCN: 这家老饭店保留着逝去时代的韵味。
senses.why: A smell spreads through air, so the word extends to immaterial atmospheres.
senses.whyCN: 气味在空气中弥散，词义便延伸到无形的氛围。

intro.en: Aroma comes from Greek arōma, meaning spice or sweet herb.
intro.cn: aroma 源自希腊语 arōma，本义「香料、香草」。

items.en: The root is uncertain; some link it to words for fragrant substances.
items.cn: 词根不确定，一般认为与表示芳香物质的词相关（来源不确定）。

items.en: Arōma meant spice, sweet herb, and also an aromatic balm for the body.
items.cn: 希腊语 arōma 指香料、香草，也指涂身的芳香油膏。

items.en: Latin borrowed the word as aroma with the same spice sense.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入该词作 aroma，仍指香料。

items.en: English took aroma from Latin in the seventeenth century for fragrant plants and drugs.
items.cn: 17 世纪英语经拉丁语借入 aroma，指芳香植物与药材。

items.en: The smell sense shifted from plants to food, and then to figurative atmospheres.
items.cn: 气味义由植物转向食物，进而衍生出比喻的氛围义。

note.en: Aroma is pleasant by definition; odor and smell stay neutral or worse.
note.cn: aroma 天然偏褒义；odor 与 smell 中性或偏负。

entries.definition: a smell, natural or artificial, pleasant or not

entries.definition: a pleasant smell, or scented liquid

normalIntro.en: Keep the food connection and the -atic adjective in mind.
normalIntro.cn: 记住与食物的关联及 -atic 形容词形式。

normal.en: aroma = a good smell, almost always of food or drink.
normal.cn: aroma 指好闻的气味，几乎总与食物饮品相关。

normal.en: The adjective is aromatic: aromatic herbs.
normal.cn: 形容词是 aromatic：芳香草本。

normal.en: In chemistry, aromatic compounds are benzene-based.
normal.cn: 化学中 aromatic compounds 指苯环化合物。

normal.en: Common phrase: the aroma of fresh coffee.
normal.cn: 常见搭配：新煮咖啡的香气。

normal.en: Figuratively, the aroma of success means its atmosphere.
normal.cn: 比喻用法：成功的气息。

abstract.en: Picture steam curling up from a morning cup under a window light.
abstract.cn: 想象晨光里杯中袅袅升起的水汽。

abstract.en: Recall the smell of garlic hitting hot olive oil.
abstract.cn: 回忆蒜香撞入热橄榄油的气味。

abstract.en: See the scent as a soft golden cloud spreading through a room.
abstract.cn: 把香味想成一团金色软云漫过房间。

examples.en: The kitchen was filled with the aroma of cinnamon rolls.
examples.cn: 厨房里满是肉桂卷的香气。

examples.en: Wine tasters praise its full-bodied aroma.
examples.cn: 品酒师称赞它浓郁的芳香。

examples.en: The market has the aroma of a hundred cuisines.
examples.cn: 这集市弥漫着百般菜系的韵味。

definition_en: an arrangement with a bank that holds a customer's money and records payments, withdrawals and interest
core_image: 一只写着名字的抽屉，钱进钱出都在抽屉旁的小本上留下痕迹
scene: 开学前，新生在分行填好表格，把生活费交给柜台。 Every student needs a bank account before the scholarship arrives.
