senses.title: The arrangement with a bank
senses.titleCN: 与银行订立的账户安排
senses.definition: an agreement under which a bank keeps a customer's money and records every movement of it
senses.definitionCN: 银行保管客户资金并记录其每一笔变动的约定
senses.example: Every student needs a bank account before the scholarship arrives.
senses.exampleCN: 每个学生在奖学金到账前都需要一个银行账户。
senses.why: bank names the institution and account names the reckoning it keeps for one customer, so the phrase is the record plus the promise to keep it.
senses.whyCN: bank 指机构，account 指它为某个客户保存的结算，因此这个短语是记录加上保存记录的承诺。

senses.title: The money on deposit
senses.definition: the balance actually held in such an arrangement at a given moment
senses.definitionCN: 某一时刻该安排中实际存放的余额
senses.example: The bank account holds barely enough for the rent.
senses.exampleCN: 这个银行账户里的钱几乎只够付房租。
senses.why: people name the container for what it contains, so the account came to mean the money inside it.
senses.whyCN: 人们常用容器指代其中的内容，于是账户也指其中的钱。

senses.title: A product type
senses.definition: one of the standard products a bank sells, such as a savings or a current account
senses.definitionCN: 银行出售的标准产品之一，如储蓄账户或活期账户
senses.example: A savings account pays a little interest each month.
senses.exampleCN: 储蓄账户每月支付少量利息。
senses.why: once banks offered several designs, the phrase began to name each product rather than any one arrangement.
senses.whyCN: 当银行提供多种设计后，这个短语开始指每一种产品，而不只是某一项安排。

senses.title: The identifying number
senses.definition: the number or code that identifies one such arrangement in a payment system
senses.definitionCN: 在支付系统中标识某项账户安排的号码或代码
senses.example: Write the bank account on the transfer form.
senses.exampleCN: 把银行账号写在转账单上。
senses.why: in a network each account must be findable, so the word is used for its address as well as for the thing addressed.
senses.whyCN: 在网络中每个账户都必须能被找到，于是这个词既指账户本身，也指它的地址。

senses.title: A shared account
senses.definition: an account held jointly by two or more people who can all draw on it
senses.definitionCN: 由两人或多人共同持有、各自都可支取的账户
senses.example: The couple keeps a joint bank account for rent.
senses.exampleCN: 这对夫妇为付房租保留了一个联名银行账户。
senses.why: the arrangement can be held by more than one person, and joint ownership is named by prefixing the phrase rather than by changing it.
senses.whyCN: 这种安排可以由不止一人持有，共有关系通过在短语前加修饰词表示，而不改变短语本身。

senses.title: An earmarked account
senses.definition: an account opened by an organization or a person to keep one purpose's money separate
senses.definitionCN: 组织或个人为把某一用途的资金分开保存而开立的账户
senses.example: The charity opened a separate bank account for donations.
senses.exampleCN: 这家慈善机构为捐款单独开了一个银行账户。
senses.why: separating money by purpose is the accounting habit that gave each column its own account, applied inside a bank.
senses.whyCN: 按用途分钱是会计的老习惯，让每一栏各有一个账目，这一习惯被搬进了银行。

senses.title: A digital account record
senses.definition: the online view of the arrangement, where balances and transactions appear as data
senses.definitionCN: 该安排在网络上的视图，余额与交易以数据形式呈现
senses.example: Her bank account was frozen while the bank checked the transfer.
senses.exampleCN: 银行核查这笔转账期间，她的银行账户被冻结了。
senses.why: the same record now lives in software, but the phrase stayed with the record rather than with the ledger.
senses.whyCN: 同一份记录如今存于软件之中，但短语仍跟着记录走，而不是跟着账簿走。

senses.title: A reserve of trust, figuratively
senses.definition: a store of goodwill or credibility that a person can draw on later
senses.definitionCN: 一个人日后可以动用的善意或信誉储备
senses.example: Goodwill is a bank account you draw on in hard times.
senses.exampleCN: 善意是一个在艰难时能取用的银行账户。
senses.why: the metaphor treat trust as money: it can be deposited by good acts and withdrawn when help is needed.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻把信任当作金钱：善举是存入，需要帮助时是支取。

intro.en: Bank account pairs the moneychanger's bench with a Latin reckoning. The two words met in English banking in the eighteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: bank account 把「钱商柜台」与一个拉丁「结算」词并置。两个词在 18 世纪的英格兰银行业相遇。年代均为约数。

items.en: Bank came into English through French and Italian from banca, the bench where a moneychanger counted coins.
items.cn: bank 经法语与意大利语进入英语，源自 banca，即钱商数钱的柜台。

items.en: Account descends from computare 'to reckon together', built on com- and putare, and reached English through Old French acont.
items.cn: account 来自 computare「合起来计算」，由 com- 与 putare 构成，经古法语 acont 进入英语。

items.en: As London banks kept a separate ledger page for each customer, the page was called the customer's account, and the phrase bank account followed.
items.cn: 当伦敦的银行替每位客户保存单独的账簿页时，这一页被称为客户的 account，bank account 这一短语随之出现。

items.en: Savings banks in the nineteenth century turned the account into a product, and cheque clearing gave it a number.
items.cn: 19 世纪的储蓄银行把账户变成一种产品，支票清算又给了它一个号码。

items.en: From the later twentieth century the account has been a database record, though the older ledger vocabulary survives in statements and passbooks.
items.cn: 从 20 世纪后期起，账户成为数据库中的记录，但旧账簿词汇仍留在对账单与存折上。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper origin): the first use of the exact phrase is not fixed, and both banca and putare rest on reconstructed earlier forms.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：这一确切短语的最早用例没有定论，banca 与 putare 的早期形式都属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds forms that look close because they share the stem account; group two holds documents and figures that sit beside a real bank account.
note.cn: 第一组是因共用 account 词干而形近的形式；第二组是与真实银行账户配套出现的单据与数字。

entries.definition: The single word can mean any account, including a story or an explanation; the compound narrows it to a bank.
entries.definitionCN: 单词本身可指任何账目，包括叙述或解释；复合短语把它收窄到银行。

entries.definition: The person who keeps and checks accounts, not the record itself.
entries.definitionCN: 保存与核查账目的人，不是记录本身。

entries.definition: The profession of keeping accounts, which looks close but names work rather than a record.
entries.definitionCN: 保存账目的职业，字形相近但指工作而非记录。

entries.definition: A periodic list a bank sends, showing what moved in the account; it is not the account itself.
entries.definitionCN: 银行定期寄出的清单，列出账户内的资金变动；它不是账户本身。

entries.definition: The amount standing in the account at one moment, as opposed to the arrangement that holds it.
entries.definitionCN: 某一时刻账户中的金额，与持有它的安排相对。

entries.definition: A type of account that pays interest and restricts withdrawals, a narrower label than bank account.
entries.definitionCN: 付息并限制支取的账户类型，是比 bank account 更窄的标签。

entries.definition: The account used for daily payments, called a checking account in American English.
entries.definitionCN: 用于日常支付的账户，美式英语称 checking account。

entries.definition: A locked box in a vault for valuables; it resembles an account in function but holds objects.
entries.definitionCN: 金库中存放贵重物品的锁箱；功能上与账户相似，但存的是物件。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: bank comes from the moneychanger's bench; account comes from a Latin verb of reckoning.
normal.cn: bank 来自钱商柜台；account 来自一个拉丁「计算」动词。

normal.en: The family runs bank, account, accountant, accounting, accountancy and banking.
normal.cn: 同族包括 bank、account、accountant、accounting、accountancy 与 banking。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: open a bank account, a joint bank account, a frozen bank account.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：开立银行账户、联名银行账户、被冻结的银行账户。

normal.en: The same record is called an account in Britain and often a bank account in full on forms.
normal.cn: 同一份记录在英国简称 account，在表格上常写全为 bank account。

normal.en: A statement reports the account; it is not the account.
normal.cn: 对账单是报告账户情况，它本身不是账户。

abstract.en: Picture a drawer with a name on it and a small notebook lying open beside it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只写着名字的抽屉，旁边摊开一本小本子。

abstract.en: Picture a jar of trust that fills with each favour and empties when help is asked.
abstract.cn: 想象一只信任的罐子，每次帮忙就装满一点，求助时就倒出一些。

abstract.en: Picture one page in a huge book, kept for you alone.
abstract.cn: 想象一本巨书中单独为你保存的一页。

examples.en: The branch opened her bank account in twenty minutes.
examples.cn: 分行在二十分钟内为她开好了银行账户。

examples.en: A joint bank account lets either partner pay the bills.
examples.cn: 联名银行账户让伴侣任何一方都能付账。

examples.en: He emptied the bank account before the trip.
examples.cn: 出发前他取空了银行账户里的钱。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「银行 + 账户」——银行替你记账的那一页 → 银行账户

root: 意大利 banca「钱商柜台」（中世纪拉丁 bancus）+ 拉丁 computare「合起来计算」（com- + putare）；两个成分经法语进入英语，18 世纪在银行业合成这一短语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one record: a bank keeps a page for a customer, and that page is then named for the money on it, the product it belongs to, its number, its shared or earmarked form, its digital image and finally a store of trust.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一份记录展开：银行替客户保存一页，这一页再依次指其中的钱、所属的产品、它的号码、共有或专用的形式、数字映像，最后指一种信任储备。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one named page in a bank's ledger, with money entering and leaving beside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：银行账簿中写着名字的一页，钱在它旁边进出。

branches.en: THE PROMISE: the bank undertakes to keep the money and keep the page.
branches.cn: 承诺：银行承担保管资金与保存这一页的责任。

branches.en: THE CONTENT: the money inside the record, whether seen in a passbook or on a screen.
branches.cn: 内容：记录中的钱，无论看在存折上还是屏幕上。

branches.en: THE PRODUCT: banks sell several standard designs, and each one gets the name.
branches.cn: 产品：银行出售几种标准设计，每一种都得到这个名称。

branches.en: THE ADDRESS AND THE SHARERS: a number finds it, and a joint name shares it.
branches.cn: 地址与共有人：号码找到它，联名共享它。

branches.en: SETTING MONEY APART: earmarking a purpose and storing goodwill are the same gesture outside banking.
branches.cn: 把钱分开：为用途专款专用与储存善意，是银行之外的同一种动作。

intro.en: This compound joins a Germanic bench-word turned bank to a Latin reckoning; neither half is a prefix or suffix, so the reading is two free forms plus their endings.
intro.cn: 这个复合词把一个由日耳曼「长凳」词变成的 bank 接在一个拉丁「结算」词上；两半都不是前缀或后缀，因此读法是两个自由词形加各自的词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin computare and putare underlie account, count and discount; Medieval Latin bancus supplies bank.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 computare 与 putare 构成 account、count 与 discount 的基础；中世纪拉丁 bancus 提供 bank。

items.example: The bank occupies the corner building.
items.exampleCN: 这家银行占用街角的建筑。

items.example: The account grows every month.
items.exampleCN: 这个账户每月增长。

items.example: Tellers count the notes twice.
items.exampleCN: 出纳把钞票数两遍。

items.example: The root carries the act of reckoning.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根带着结算的动作。

items.example: The accountant signed the report.
items.exampleCN: 会计在报告上签了字。

items.example: Accounting exposes any gap.
items.exampleCN: 会计记录会暴露任何缺口。

items.example: Accountancy is a regulated profession.
items.exampleCN: 会计是一门受监管的职业。

items.example: The branch manager is accountable for the loss.
items.exampleCN: 分行经理须为这笔损失负责。

items.example: Banking moved online within a decade.
items.exampleCN: 银行业在十年内转向线上。

items.example: The bank offered a discount on fees.
items.exampleCN: 银行在手续费上给了折扣。

definition_zh: 顶点；最高潮；最终成果；达到顶峰的阶段
definition_en: the highest or climactic point that a process reaches, or the act of reaching it
core_image: 登山队在最后一段雪坡上排成一列，把旗子插上峰顶
scene: 登山队在最后一段雪坡上排成一列，把旗子插上峰顶。 The summit was the culmination of ten years of planning.
sceneCN: 这里指长期努力达到的最高点（第 1 个义项：顶点、最高潮）；句意为登顶是十年筹划的顶点。图中可辨识物件：雪坡、冰镐、旗子、峰顶。

pos.zh: 名词：顶点；最高潮；最终成果（可数，常用单数）

collocations.phrase: the culmination of years of work

derivatives.zh: 同一词根的动词，义为「达到顶点；以……告终」
由该动词加现在分词词尾构成，义为「达到顶点的」
由该词根加形容词词尾构成，义为「处于最高点的」
同一拉丁词根的直接借用，义为「山顶；最高点」

senses.title: The highest point of a long effort
senses.definition: the point at which a long process reaches its highest level
senses.definitionCN: 一个长期过程达到最高水平的时刻
senses.example: The summit was the culmination of ten years of planning.
senses.exampleCN: 登顶是十年筹划的顶点。
senses.why: The Latin noun for a mountain top gave the word its shape: a process climbs and ends at a peak.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语中表示山顶的名词给了它形状：一个过程向上爬，最后停在峰顶。

senses.title: The final result of a process
senses.definition: the finished outcome in which earlier stages are gathered up
senses.definitionCN: 把先前各阶段收拢在一起的最终结果
senses.example: The treaty was the culmination of months of quiet talks.
senses.exampleCN: 这项条约是数月低调谈判的最终成果。
senses.why: A peak gathers everything below it, so the last stage stands for the whole effort.
senses.whyCN: 峰顶把下方的一切都收拢起来，因此最后一阶段代表全部努力。

senses.title: The peak of a career
senses.definition: the most successful or honoured moment of a working life
senses.definitionCN: 职业生活中最成功或最受尊崇的时刻
senses.example: The award marked the culmination of her career.
senses.exampleCN: 这个奖项标志着她职业生涯的顶峰。
senses.why: A working life rises and then levels off, and the word marks the moment it stands highest.
senses.whyCN: 职业生涯会上升然后走平，这个词标记它站在最高处的那一刻。

senses.title: The climax of a ceremony
senses.definition: the most solemn or exciting moment of a formal event
senses.definitionCN: 正式活动中最庄严或最激动人心的时刻
senses.example: The lighting of the flame was the culmination of the ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 点燃圣火是典礼的高潮。
senses.why: A ceremony is built as a slope, and the word names the step everyone waits for.
senses.whyCN: 典礼像一段斜坡，这个词点出所有人都在等的那一步。

senses.title: The peak of a trend, including a bad one
senses.definition: the point at which a development reaches its extreme before turning
senses.definitionCN: 某种发展在转向之前达到极端的时刻
senses.example: The crisis was the culmination of months of tension.
senses.exampleCN: 这场危机是数月紧张局势的顶点。
senses.why: A peak can be a summit or a breaking point; the word covers both.
senses.whyCN: 顶点可以是登顶，也可以是崩断点，这个词两者都管。

senses.title: Astronomical culmination
senses.definition: the moment a celestial body reaches its highest point above the horizon
senses.definitionCN: 天体到达地平线以上最高点的时刻
senses.example: The star's culmination occurs shortly after midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 这颗星的最高点出现在午夜过后不久。
senses.why: Astronomy kept the literal meaning: the body is literally at the top of its arc.
senses.whyCN: 天文学保留了字面义：天体确实处在其弧线的最高处。

senses.title: The climax of a story or artwork
senses.titleCN: 故事或艺术作品的顶点
senses.definition: the most intense point of a narrative or composition
senses.definitionCN: 叙事或作品中最强烈的时刻
senses.example: The final movement is the culmination of the whole symphony.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一个乐章是整部交响曲的顶点。
senses.why: A composition gathers its themes into one last passage, and that passage is the peak the word names.
senses.whyCN: 作品把各个主题收进最后一段，那一段就是这个词所指的高点。

senses.title: The finale of a season or competition
senses.titleCN: 赛季或赛事的收官高潮
senses.definition: the last and highest event that closes a series of contests
senses.definitionCN: 结束一系列赛事的最后一场高潮
senses.example: The final match was the culmination of a long season.
senses.exampleCN: 决赛是整个漫长赛季的收官高潮。
senses.why: A series needs an ending that outranks every earlier round, and the word supplies that ranking.
senses.whyCN: 一连串赛事需要一个压过此前各轮的分量收尾，这个词提供这种排序。

intro.en: Culmination comes from Late Latin culminatio, from culminare, to reach the top, from culmen, a summit or roof. English took the noun in the seventeenth century, first for astronomy and then for human affairs.
intro.cn: 这个词来自晚期拉丁语 culminatio，源头是动词 culminare「到达顶端」，后者出自名词 culmen「山顶、屋顶」。英语在十七世纪借入这个名词，先用于天文，后用于人事。

items.en: The noun meant a summit, a roof or the top of anything.
items.cn: 这个名词意为山顶、屋顶或任何东西的顶端。

items.en: The verb meant to raise to the top or to reach the summit.
items.cn: 这个动词意为抬到顶端或到达峰顶。

items.en: The noun named the act of reaching the highest point.
items.cn: 这个名词指到达最高点的行为。

items.en: English used the word first in astronomy, for a star's highest point.
items.cn: 英语最初在天文中使用这个词，指一颗星的最高点。

items.en: Later usage applied it to careers, ceremonies and finished works.
items.cn: 后来的用法把它用于职业、典礼与完成的作品。

items.en: Modern usage also calls a crisis the culmination of a trend; the date of that extension is uncertain.
items.cn: 现代用法也把危机称为某种趋势的顶点；这一扩展的年代不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the root or the top-of-arc image; the second group names neighbouring high points.
note.cn: 第一组共享词根或「弧线最高点」的意象；第二组是相邻的高点概念。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to reach the highest point or end in something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，意为达到顶点或以某结果告终。

entries.definition: The participle used as an adjective for a peak stage.
entries.definitionCN: 分词作形容词，指达到顶点的。

entries.definition: An adjective for something at its highest point.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指处于最高点的。

entries.definition: A borrowed Latin noun for a summit.
entries.definitionCN: 借自拉丁语的名词，指山顶。

entries.definition: A pillar, from a related word for a tall upright mass.
entries.definitionCN: 指柱子，出自一个表示高耸竖直物的相关词。

entries.definition: The most intense moment of a narrative or event, stressing intensity rather than height.
entries.definitionCN: 指叙事或事件最强烈的时刻，强调强度而非高度。

entries.definition: The highest level or value reached, often in graphs.
entries.definitionCN: 指达到的最高水平或数值，常用于曲线。

entries.definition: The top of a mountain, and by extension a meeting of leaders.
entries.definitionCN: 指山峰顶端，引申为领导人会议。

entries.definition: The point directly above an observer, used figuratively for a high point.
entries.definitionCN: 指观测者正上方的点，喻指高峰。

entries.definition: The act of finishing rather than the highest point.
entries.definitionCN: 指完成的行为，而非最高点。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the literal image of a mountain top, then follow the word into careers, ceremonies and stories.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用山顶的字面意象，再把这个词走到职业、典礼与故事里。

normal.en: The Latin noun meant the top of a mountain, so culmination is the moment a long climb ends.
normal.cn: 拉丁名词意为山顶，所以这个词就是漫长攀登结束的那一刻。

normal.en: The treaty ending months of talks is the finished result, not merely the last event.
normal.cn: 结束数月谈判的条约是最终成果，而不只是最后一场活动。

normal.en: An award can mark the culmination of a career, the highest point of a working life.
normal.cn: 奖项可以标志职业生涯的顶点，即职业生涯的最高处。

normal.en: Astronomy uses the word literally for a star at the top of its arc.
normal.cn: 天文学用它的字面义，指处在弧线最高处的星。

normal.en: A crisis can be the culmination of tension, because a peak may also be a breaking point.
normal.cn: 危机可以是紧张局势的顶点，因为顶点也可能是崩断点。

abstract.en: A peak is the smallest possible place from which everything below can be seen.
abstract.cn: 峰顶是最小的位置，却能从那里看见下方的一切。

abstract.en: Not every culmination is happy: some are simply the last point before a fall.
abstract.cn: 并非每个顶点都令人欣喜：有些只是坠落前的最后一点。

abstract.en: The word gathers time into a single height, which is why we remember summits and forget slopes.
abstract.cn: 这个词把时间收进一个高度，所以我们记住峰顶，忘了斜坡。

examples.en: The exhibition was the culmination of five years of research.
examples.cn: 这场展览是五年研究的顶点。

examples.en: His retirement speech was the culmination of a long career.
examples.cn: 他的退休演说是一段漫长职业生涯的顶点。

examples.en: The festival's culmination came with the final procession.
examples.cn: 节庆的顶点出现在最后的游行。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「卡尔米内申」——一路往上爬，最后站到最高的那一点，就是「顶点、高潮」：顶点、最高潮

root: 来自晚期拉丁语 culminatio，源头动词 culminare「到达顶端」，后者出自 culmen「山顶、屋顶」；英语在十七世纪借入，先用于天文，后用于人事。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses keep one shape, a process rising to its top: an effort, a result, a career, a ceremony, a trend, a star, a work and a season.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项保持同一个形状，即过程升到顶端：努力、成果、职业、典礼、趋势、星体、作品与赛季。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a climbing team roped on the last snow slope, a flag planted on the summit.
core.cn: 核心意象：最后一段雪坡上结组而行的登山队，以及插上峰顶的旗。

branches.en: THE HIGHEST POINT: a long effort or a working life reaches its peak.
branches.cn: 最高点：长期努力或职业生涯达到顶峰。

branches.en: THE FINAL RESULT: the treaty and the final match gather the stages below them.

senses.title: Relating to the study of ancient material remains
senses.titleCN: 与古代实物遗存研究有关
senses.definition: relating to the scientific study of past human societies through the objects, structures, and traces they left behind
senses.definitionCN: 与通过古人留下的器物、建筑与痕迹来科学研究过去人类社会有关
senses.example: The valley is protected as an archaeological zone.
senses.exampleCN: 这个山谷被划为考古保护区。
senses.why: Greek arkhaiologia joins archaeo- 'ancient' and -logy 'study'. The adjective adds -ical, so it names whatever belongs to that study: its methods, its sites, its evidence.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 arkhaiologia 由 archaeo-“古老的”与 -logy“研究”组成。形容词再加 -ical，因此它命名一切属于这门研究的东西：方法、遗址、证据。

senses.title: Pertaining to the remains themselves
senses.titleCN: 指遗存本身：地下的器物与痕迹
senses.definition: of or concerning the physical remains of past human activity, rather than the written account of it
senses.definitionCN: 指或关于过去人类活动的实物遗存，而非关于它的书面记述
senses.example: Archaeological evidence shows that the village burned twice.
senses.exampleCN: 考古证据表明这个村庄曾两次被烧毁。
senses.why: The study and its objects are named as one: what archaeologists deal with becomes 'archaeological material'. The adjective shifts from the discipline to the things that feed it.
senses.whyCN: 研究与研究对象被用同一个名字：考古学家处理的东西成了“考古材料”。形容词从学科转到喂养这门学科实物。

senses.title: Belonging to ancient history as a subject
senses.titleCN: 属于作为学科对象的古代史
senses.definition: in the older sense, relating to the written or literary study of ancient history, before archaeology became a field science
senses.definitionCN: 较早的义项：与古代史的书写或文献研究有关，那时考古学尚未成为田野科学
senses.example: In 1700, an archaeological lecture was a lecture on ancient history, not on a dig.
senses.exampleCN: 在 1700 年，一场“考古学”讲座其实是古代史讲座，而不是关于发掘的讲座。
senses.why: Archaeology entered English c.1600 meaning 'ancient history'. The adjective could therefore describe bookish ancient history, long before the 1825 sense of a scientific study of peoples and civilizations.
senses.whyCN: archaeology 约 1600 年进入英语时意为“古代史”。因此这个形容词可以描述书斋式的古代史研究，远早于 1825 年才出现的“对民族与文明进行科学研究”的义项。

senses.title: Relating to field excavation
senses.definition: relating to the practical work of excavating, recording, and interpreting a site layer by layer
senses.definitionCN: 与逐层发掘、记录和解读遗址的实地工作有关
senses.example: The archaeological dig was closed during the rainy season.
senses.exampleCN: 考古发掘在雨季暂停了。
senses.why: A study of ancient things must go to the ground to find them. The adjective attaches to the trowel, the trench and the layer, so 'archaeological' becomes fieldwork rather than library work.
senses.whyCN: 对古老事物的研究必须下到地里去找它们。形容词于是附着在铲子、探方与地层上，archaeological 也从书斋工作变成田野工作。

senses.title: Belonging to the academic discipline
senses.titleCN: 属于这门学科：系、课程与专业
senses.definition: relating to archaeology as an academic department, degree, or profession
senses.definitionCN: 与作为大学院系、学位或职业的考古学有关
senses.example: She is writing an archaeological thesis on coastal trade.
senses.exampleCN: 她正在写一篇关于沿海贸易的考古学论文。
senses.why: Once the study is organised into departments and degrees, its adjective marks membership: an archaeological thesis, an archaeological society. The root is the same; the referent is now the institution.
senses.whyCN: 当这门研究被组织成院系与学位，它的形容词就标记归属：考古学论文、考古学会。词根未变，所指变成了机构。

senses.title: Relating to a period or region: classical archaeology
senses.titleCN: 属于某一时期或地区：古典考古学
senses.definition: relating to a branch of the discipline defined by a period, region, or culture, such as classical or prehistoric archaeology
senses.definitionCN: 与按时期、地区或文化划分的学科分支有关，如古典考古学或史前考古学
senses.example: Classical archaeological methods differ from those used on prehistoric camps.
senses.exampleCN: 古典考古的方法与用于史前营地的方法不同。
senses.why: The modifier narrows 'ancient' to one stretch of the ancient past. The adjective still says 'of the study', but the study is now bounded by a period or a map.
senses.whyCN: 修饰语把“古老”收窄到古代中的某一段。形容词仍表示“属于这门研究”，只是这门研究被时期或地图圈定了。

senses.title: Relating to industrial remains
senses.titleCN: 与工业遗存有关：工业考古
senses.definition: relating to the study of factories, machines, and infrastructure from the industrial age, often standing or still in use
senses.definitionCN: 与对工业时代的工厂、机器与基础设施的研究有关，这些遗存常仍矗立或仍在使用
senses.example: An archaeological survey of the mill recorded every gear and chimney.
senses.exampleCN: 对这座工厂的考古调查记录了每一个齿轮和烟囱。
senses.why: The method of reading objects, not the age of the objects, defines the adjective. Industrial remains can be studied with the same layer-by-layer discipline, so 'archaeological' extends to the recent past.
senses.whyCN: 定义这个形容词的是“读实物”的方法，而不是实物的年代。工业遗存也能用同样的逐层方法研究，因此 archaeological 延伸到了近现代。

senses.title: Relating to submerged sites: underwater archaeology
senses.titleCN: 与沉没遗址有关：水下考古
senses.definition: relating to the study of shipwrecks, drowned settlements, and other remains lying under water
senses.definitionCN: 与对沉船、被淹没的聚落及其他水下遗存的研究有关
senses.example: Underwater archaeological work mapped the wreck before anything was lifted.
senses.exampleCN: 水下考古工作在打捞任何东西之前先测绘了沉船。
senses.why: The ancient thing is now under water, but the same 'study of ancient things' applies. The adjective travels with the method into a new environment.
senses.whyCN: 古老的东西现在在水下，但“对古老事物的研究”仍然适用。形容词随方法进入了新的环境。

senses.title: Metaphorical: digging through layers of thought
senses.titleCN: 隐喻用法：挖掘思想的层层堆积
senses.definition: used figuratively of an inquiry that uncovers the hidden layers and assumptions beneath a system of ideas
senses.definitionCN: 比喻性地指一种探究，揭开某个观念体系下面隐藏的层次与前提
senses.example: The book offers an archaeological reading of modern medicine.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书对现代医学做了一种考古学式的解读。
senses.why: The discipline's signature move is removing layer after layer to expose what lies beneath. Applied to ideas, archaeology becomes a metaphor for tracing how a system was built up, as in an archaeology of knowledge.
senses.whyCN: 这门学科的标志动作是一层层去掉覆盖物，露出下面的东西。把它用到观念上，archaeology 就成为追溯一个体系如何层层堆积起来的隐喻，如“知识考古学”。

intro.en: Archaeological is archaeology plus -ical. Archaeology is Greek arkhaiologia 'the study of ancient things': archaeo-, from arkhaios 'ancient', plus -logy, from -logia 'study'. Arkhaios itself comes from arkhē 'beginning'. The -ical ending is -ic plus -al, a compound adjective suffix. The archaeo- element means 'ancient' and has nothing to do with archi- 'chief' in architectural.
intro.cn: archaeological 是 archaeology 加 -ical。archaeology 来自希腊语 arkhaiologia“对古老事物的研究”：archaeo- 出自 arkhaios“古老的”，-logy 出自 -logia“研究”。arkhaios 本身出自 arkhē“开端”。-ical 结尾是 -ic 加 -al 的复合形容词后缀。archaeo- 成分意为“古老”，与 architectural 中 archi-“首席”毫无关系。

items.en: Greek arkhaiologia meant 'the study of ancient things'. It joined archaeo-, from arkhaios 'ancient', with -logia 'study, discourse'.
items.cn: 希腊语 arkhaiologia 意为“对古老事物的研究”。它把出自 arkhaios“古老的”的 archaeo- 与 -logia“研究、论述”结合起来。

items.en: Arkhaios 'ancient' derives from arkhē 'beginning': the ancient is what belongs to the beginning. The second element is -logy, the study of a subject.
items.cn: arkhaios“古老的”出自 arkhē“开端”：古老之物就是属于开端的东西。第二个成分是 -logy，即对某主题的研究。

items.en: English archaeology first meant 'ancient history', borrowed from French archéologie (16c.) or directly from Greek. It was a bookish term, not yet a field science.
items.cn: 英语 archaeology 最初意为“古代史”，借自 16 世纪法语 archéologie，或直接借自希腊语。它是个书斋词，还不是田野科学。

items.en: Only in 1825 does archaeology come to mean the scientific study of ancient peoples and civilizations through their remains.
items.cn: 直到 1825 年，archaeology 才指通过遗存对古代民族与文明进行的科学研究。

items.en: Archaeologic is recorded in 1731 and archaeological in 1766, both built on archaeology. The ending -ical is -ic plus -al: -ic makes the relational adjective, -al completes and stabilises it.
items.cn: archaeologic 记录于 1731 年，archaeological 记录于 1766 年，二者都建立在 archaeology 上。结尾 -ical 是 -ic 加 -al：-ic 构成关系形容词，-al 补足并稳定它。

items.en: Modern branches such as classical, industrial and underwater archaeology all keep the same elements. Only the modifier changes; archaeo- still means 'ancient', while archi- in architectural is Greek arkhi- 'chief'.
items.cn: 古典考古、工业考古、水下考古等现代分支都保留同样的成分。变的只是修饰语；archaeo- 仍指“古老”，而 architectural 里的 archi- 是希腊语 arkhi-“首席”。

note.en: The first group contains one true root-alike and two traps: architectural has archi- 'chief', while archaic shares the ancient root but not the discipline. The second group separates archaeology from neighbouring studies.
note.cn: 第一组包含一个真正同根的词和两个陷阱：architectural 里的 archi- 是“首席”，archaic 虽共享“古老”词根却不指这门学科。第二组把考古学与邻近学科分开。

entries.definition: relating to architecture or building design. Its archi- comes from Greek arkhi- 'chief', not from archaeo- 'ancient'.
entries.definitionCN: 与建筑或建筑设计有关的。它的 archi- 来自希腊语 arkhi-“首席”，不是 archaeo-“古老”。

entries.definition: very old or old-fashioned, often deliberately so. It shares arkhaios 'ancient' but describes age or style, not the study of remains.
entries.definitionCN: 古老的；过时的，常指刻意仿古。它共享 arkhaios“古老的”，但描述年代或风格，而不是对遗存的研究。

entries.definition: a person who studies ancient remains. It is archaeology plus -ist, so it names the practitioner rather than the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 研究古代遗存的人。它是 archaeology 加 -ist，命名从业者，而不是形容词。

entries.definition: the study of human societies and cultures, including living peoples. Archaeology is one branch of it when remains are the main evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 对人类社群与文化的研究，也包括在世的人群。当主要证据是遗存时，考古学是它的一个分支。

entries.definition: the study of ancient life through fossils. It deals with organisms, while archaeology deals with human material remains.
entries.definitionCN: 通过化石研究古代生命。它处理生物，而考古学处理人类的实物遗存。

entries.definition: the study of the past based mainly on written documents. Archaeology works from objects and traces, especially where no texts survive.
entries.definitionCN: 主要依据书面文献对过去的研究。考古学从器物与痕迹入手，尤其在无文字留存的地方。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: Greek archaeo- 'ancient' and -logy 'study', the 1731/1766 -ic then -ical formation, and the fixed phrases archaeological site and archaeological evidence.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：希腊语 archaeo-“古老”与 -logy“研究”、1731／1766 年先 -ic 后 -ical 的构词，以及 archaeological site、archaeological evidence 等固定搭配。

normal.en: Archaeo- is 'ancient', -logy is 'study': archaeology is the study of ancient things, and archaeological is everything belonging to it.
normal.cn: archaeo- 是“古老”，-logy 是“研究”：archaeology 是对古老事物的研究，archaeological 则属于这门研究的一切。

normal.en: Arkhaios comes from arkhē 'beginning', so the ancient is literally what belongs to the beginning.
normal.cn: arkhaios 出自 arkhē“开端”，所以“古老的”字面上就是“属于开端的”。

normal.en: Archaeologic came first in 1731, archaeological in 1766: -ical is simply -ic plus -al.
normal.cn: archaeologic 先在 1731 年出现，archaeological 在 1766 年出现：-ical 不过是 -ic 加 -al。

normal.en: Archaeological site and archaeological evidence are the standard frames: a place to dig and the objects that speak.
normal.cn: archaeological site 与 archaeological evidence 是标准搭配：一个可供发掘的地方，以及会说话的器物。

normal.en: Architectural has archi- 'chief', not archaeo- 'ancient': an architect is a chief builder, not a student of ruins.
normal.cn: architectural 里的 archi- 是“首席”，不是 archaeo-“古老”：建筑师是首席建造者，不是废墟研究者。

abstract.en: A trowel removes one thin layer at a time: the past is read from the top down, and each layer is younger than the one below.
abstract.cn: 一把铲子每次刮掉薄薄一层：过去要从上往下读，每一层都比下面那层年轻。

abstract.en: A grid of strings divides the ground into squares: the same ancient thing can be located precisely by its square and depth.
abstract.cn: 用绳子把地面分成方格：同一件古物可以靠它的方号与深度被精确定位。

abstract.en: Broken pots are fitted back together: archaeology rebuilds a whole society from fragments that were never meant to be a message.
abstract.cn: 破碎的陶罐被拼回原形：考古学用从未打算传递信息的碎片，重建整个社会。

examples.en: The archaeological team found a wall under the car park.
examples.cn: 考古队在停车场下面发现了一道墙。

examples.en: Archaeological evidence suggests the harbour silted up slowly.
examples.cn: 考古证据表明这个港口是慢慢淤塞的。

examples.en: She joined an archaeological survey of the old iron works.
examples.cn: 她加入了对那座旧铁厂的考古调查。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿凯奥勒吉扣」——阿凯（Ar-chae）在奥勒（O-le）的土层里一层层挖，吉扣（Ji Kou）把碎片拼成一只古碗 → archaeological 考古的

root: 源自希腊语 arkhaiologia“对古老事物的研究”：archaeo-（arkhaios“古老的”，出自 arkhē“开端”）+ -logy（-logia“研究”）；archaeological 是 archaeology + -ical。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of archaeological all hang on one act: removing layers to expose what ancient people left. From the discipline and its remains, the word extends to ancient history, field excavation, academic departments, period branches, industrial and underwater work, and finally to the metaphor of digging through ideas.
sensesIntro.cn: archaeological 的九个义项都挂在同一个动作上：揭开层层覆盖，让古人留下的东西露出来。从学科与遗存，它扩展到古代史、田野发掘、大学院系、分期分支、工业与水下工作，最后到“挖掘观念”的隐喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a trowel lifting one thin layer of soil from a marked square.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把小铲从划好的方格中刮起薄薄一层土。

branches.en: DISCIPLINE AND INSTITUTION: the study itself, and its departments, degrees and professions.
branches.cn: 学科与机构：研究本身，以及它的院系、学位与职业。

branches.en: REMAINS AND FIELDWORK: the objects that are studied, and the digging that finds them.
branches.cn: 遗存与田野：被研究的器物，以及找到它们的发掘工作。

branches.en: ANCIENT HISTORY: the earliest bookish sense, before archaeology became a field science.
branches.cn: 古代史：最早的、书斋式的义项，在考古学成为田野科学之前。

branches.en: PERIOD AND WATER: branches narrowed by a period or a region, including submerged sites.
branches.cn: 分期与水下：被时期或地区收窄的分支，包括沉没遗址。

branches.en: INDUSTRY AND METAPHOR: recent remains read like ancient ones, and ideas read like layers of soil.
branches.cn: 工业与隐喻：近现代遗存像古代遗存一样被阅读，观念则像土层一样被阅读。

intro.en: Archaeological is archaeology + -ical, where -ical is the compound of -ic and -al that makes a relational adjective. Archaeology joins archaeo- 'ancient' and -logy 'study'. The same archaeo- stem gives archaeologist, archaeometry, bioarchaeology, archaeobotany, archaic and archaism.
intro.cn: archaeological 是 archaeology 加 -ical，其中 -ical 是 -ic 与 -al 复合而成的关系形容词后缀。archaeology 由 archaeo-“古老”与 -logy“研究”组合。同一 archaeo- 词干给出 archaeologist、archaeometry、bioarchaeology、archaeobotany、archaic 与 archaism。

latinIntro.en: The word is Greek in origin, but New Latin coined archaeologia from the Greek compound, and Latin archaismus gave English archaism. Latin architectura is listed only to show the contrast: its archi- is 'chief', not 'ancient'.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词源于希腊语，但新拉丁语用希腊复合词造出 archaeologia，拉丁语 archaismus 则给出英语 archaism。列入拉丁语 architectura 只为显示对照：它的 archi- 是“首席”，不是“古老”。

items.meaning: relating to the study of ancient material remains
items.meaningCN: 考古学的；考古的（-ical 构成关系形容词）
items.example: The archaeological record is thin in that valley.
items.exampleCN: 那个山谷的考古记录很单薄。

items.meaning: the study of ancient peoples through their remains
items.example: Archaeology depends on careful recording.
items.exampleCN: 考古学依赖细致的记录。

items.meaning: a person who studies ancient remains

definition_zh: 稀释；冲淡；削弱（效果、权力）；稀释过的
definition_en: to make a liquid weaker by adding water or another solvent, or to make something less forceful
core_image: 一小杯浓果汁倒进一大壶凉水，颜色从深褐立刻变浅
scene: 厨房里，服务员把一小杯浓缩果汁倒进一大壶凉水，颜色立刻从深褐变浅。 The waiter diluted the strong juice with cold water before serving it.
sceneCN: 这里 dilute 指加水使浓度降低（第 1 个义项：稀释）；句意为服务员上桌前用凉水把浓果汁稀释。图中可辨识物件：浓缩果汁、水壶、玻璃杯、搅拌勺。

senses.title: To add water and lower concentration
senses.definition: to add water or another solvent to a liquid so that the amount of active substance in each unit falls
senses.definitionCN: 向液体中加入水或其他溶剂，使每单位中有效物质的量下降
senses.example: Dilute the acid with three parts water.
senses.exampleCN: 用三份水把这种酸稀释。
senses.why: dilute comes from Latin diluere 'to wash away', so the core action is washing strength out into a larger volume.
senses.whyCN: dilute 出自拉丁 diluere「冲走」，核心动作就是把强度冲散到更大的体积里。

senses.title: To weaken a solution before testing
senses.definition: to reduce the strength of a sample so that it falls within the range an instrument or a procedure can handle
senses.definitionCN: 降低样品的强度，使仪器或操作能处理
senses.example: The technician diluted the sample before testing.
senses.exampleCN: 技术员在检测前把样品稀释了。
senses.why: a sample that is too strong must be reduced, so laboratory routine turns the first sense into a standard step.
senses.whyCN: 过浓的样品必须减弱，实验室流程就把第一义变成标准步骤。

senses.title: To weaken power or influence
senses.definition: to make authority, influence or an advantage less effective by spreading it among more parties
senses.definitionCN: 把权威、影响力或优势分散给更多方，使其效力下降
senses.example: Adding more members diluted the chairman's influence.
senses.exampleCN: 增加成员削弱了主席的影响力。
senses.why: influence behaves like a solute: the same amount spread through more volume acts more weakly at any one point.
senses.whyCN: 影响力像溶质：同样的量摊进更大体积，在任一点上的作用就更弱。

senses.title: To weaken taste, colour or feeling
senses.definition: to make a quality fainter by mixing it with something neutral
senses.definitionCN: 通过与中性之物混合使某种性质变淡
senses.example: Too much water diluted the taste of the tea.
senses.exampleCN: 水太多，把茶味冲淡了。
senses.why: taste and colour are intensities carried in a liquid, so adding liquid lowers them just as it lowers concentration.
senses.whyCN: 味道与颜色是液体承载的强度，加水会像降低浓度一样把它们压低。

senses.title: Weakened by water, as an adjective
senses.titleCN: 形容词：稀释过的、浓度低的
senses.definition: having had water added, so that the substance is present at low strength
senses.definitionCN: 已加水，使物质以低强度存在
senses.example: A dilute solution of bleach is safe on the floor.
senses.exampleCN: 稀释的漂白液用在地面上是安全的。
senses.why: the adjective is the same form, describing the state that the verb has produced.
senses.whyCN: 形容词是同一形式，描述动词造成的那种状态。

senses.title: To make a promise less forceful
senses.titleCN: 使承诺或主张变得无力
senses.definition: to take the force out of a statement, promise or claim by adding qualifications or compromises
senses.definitionCN: 通过附加条件或折中，抽掉陈述、承诺或主张的力量
senses.example: The final clause diluted the promise of reform.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一条款把改革的承诺冲淡了。
senses.why: a claim is strong when nothing neutral is mixed in, so hedging works like adding water to a statement.
senses.whyCN: 主张在没有掺入中性成分时最强，因此含糊其辞就像给陈述加水。

senses.title: To reduce each shareholder's stake
senses.definition: to reduce the proportion of a company owned by existing shareholders by issuing more shares
senses.definitionCN: 通过发行更多股份，降低现有股东所占的公司比例
senses.example: Issuing new shares diluted existing holdings.
senses.exampleCN: 发行新股稀释了现有持股。
senses.why: ownership is a share of a fixed whole, so adding more shares spreads the same company over more claims.
senses.whyCN: 所有权是对一个固定整体的份额，增发股份就把同一家公司摊到更多索取权上。

senses.title: To spread intensity until it fades
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：把强度摊到更大范围直至变淡
senses.definition: used figuratively of any intensity that loses force when spread over more time, space or recipients
senses.definitionCN: 比喻指任何强度因摊到更多时间、空间或对象而失去力量
senses.example: Praise repeated too often is diluted into noise.
senses.exampleCN: 赞美重复太多，就被冲淡成噪音。
senses.why: the abstract sense keeps the arithmetic of dilution: the same amount divided among more units counts for less in each.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义保留了稀释的算术：同样的量分给更多单位，每一份就更少。

intro.en: Dilute comes from the Latin past participle dilutus, from diluere 'to wash away, dissolve, dilute', built on dis- 'apart' plus -luere, the combining form of lavere 'to wash'. It is recorded in English from the fifteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: dilute 来自拉丁过去分词 dilutus，出自 diluere「冲走、溶解、稀释」，由 dis-「分开」加 -luere 构成，后者是 lavere「洗」的组合形式。英语自十五世纪有记录。年代均为约数。

items.en: Lavere meant 'to wash'; its combining form -luere appears in diluere and in words about flooding, and its older root is reconstructed as a verb of washing.
items.cn: lavere 意为「洗」，其组合形式 -luere 出现在 diluere 以及表示洪水的词中，其更古老词根被重构为一个表示「洗」的动词。

items.en: Dis- 'apart' plus -luere gave diluere 'to wash away, to dissolve, to dilute', the image being strength carried off into a larger body of water.
items.cn: dis-「分开」加 -luere 构成 diluere「冲走、溶解、稀释」，画面是强度被带进更大一片水里。

items.en: The past participle dilutus 'washed away, diluted' is the direct source of the English adjective and of the verb built on it.
items.cn: 过去分词 dilutus「被冲走的、被稀释的」是英语形容词及由此构成的动词的直接来源。

items.en: From the fifteenth century English dilute meant to weaken a liquid by adding water, first in medicine and then in general use.
items.cn: 自十五世纪起，英语 dilute 指加水使液体变弱，先在医学中使用，后进入一般用法。

items.en: By the seventeenth century the verb described weakened power, claims and ownership, where the same arithmetic of spreading holds.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，这个动词已用于被削弱的权力、主张与所有权，因为「摊开」的算术是一样的。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Latin shape of the washing root is a reconstruction, and its exact first English citation is not recorded. Note that this root is not the luere 'to loosen' behind soluble.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：表示「洗」的词根在拉丁语之前的形式属于重构，英语最早书证没有确切记录。需注意这个词根并非 soluble 背后表示「松开」的 luere。

note.en: Group one holds look-alikes whose roots are different despite similar spelling; group two holds verbs for making something weaker.
note.cn: 第一组是拼写相近而词根不同的形近词；第二组是表示使某物变弱的动词。

entries.definition: The act or result of diluting; it is the noun built on this verb, not a separate root.
entries.definitionCN: 稀释的动作或结果；由这个动词构成的名词，并非另一个词根。

entries.definition: To break a solid apart into a liquid; dilute does not dissolve anything, it only lowers the strength of what is already dissolved.
entries.definitionCN: 把固体拆散进液体；dilute 不溶解任何东西，只降低已溶解物的强度。

entries.definition: From Latin latus 'wide': to widen or expand, as a pupil or an artery does; it has nothing to do with washing.
entries.definitionCN: 出自拉丁 latus「宽」：使变宽、扩张，如瞳孔或动脉；与「洗」无关。

entries.definition: From diluvium, a flood: water overwhelming everything, which is the violent version of the same washing image.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 diluvium「洪水」：水淹没一切，是同一「冲洗」意象的猛烈版本。

entries.definition: The broad verb for making anything less strong, with no image of water.
entries.definitionCN: 使任何事物变弱的通用动词，不含水的意象。

entries.definition: To make a liquid less thick, as paint with turpentine; it changes consistency rather than concentration.
entries.definitionCN: 使液体变稀薄，如用松节油调漆；改变的是稠度，而非浓度。

entries.definition: The plain phrase for adding water, and also for softening a statement; dilute is its formal counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 加水的日常说法，也指软化表述；dilute 是其正式对应词。

entries.definition: To reduce the strength of a signal, a virus or a force; common in physics and medicine rather than in cookery.
entries.definitionCN: 降低信号、病毒或力量的强度；多用于物理与医学，而非厨房。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Diluere 'to wash away': water carries the strength off into a larger volume.
normal.cn: diluere「冲走」：水把强度带进更大的体积。

normal.en: The family runs dilute, dilution, diluent, diluted, undiluted.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 dilute、dilution、diluent、diluted、undiluted。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the chemical sense: dilute acid, dilute a solution.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出化学义：稀酸、稀释溶液。

normal.en: The figurative phrases mark the rest: dilute the effect, dilute ownership, dilute the message.
normal.cn: 比喻搭配标出其余义项：削弱效果、稀释所有权、冲淡信息。

normal.en: Remember the root is 'wash', not 'loosen': do not tie it to dissolve or soluble.
normal.cn: 记住词根是「洗」而不是「松开」：不要把它与 dissolve 或 soluble 系在一起。

abstract.en: Picture a spoon of dark syrup turning a whole jug pale brown.
abstract.cn: 想象一勺深色糖浆把整壶水染成浅褐。

abstract.en: Picture applause spread thin over an hour until it sounds like background noise.
abstract.cn: 想象掌声摊薄在一小时里，最后听起来像背景噪音。

abstract.en: Picture one strong voice split among a hundred speakers.
abstract.cn: 想象一个洪亮的声音被分给一百个人。

examples.en: Always dilute the cleaning fluid before pouring it down the drain.
examples.cn: 把清洁液倒进排水口前一定要先稀释。

examples.en: The new partners diluted the founder's share to less than half.
examples.cn: 新合伙人把创始人的股份稀释到不足一半。

examples.en: Repeating the slogan at every stop diluted its effect.
examples.cn: 每到一站都重复这句口号，反而削弱了它的效果。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「di（分开）+ lute（冲）」——把浓的冲散开：稀释、冲淡、削弱

root: 拉丁 diluere「冲走、稀释」的过去分词 dilutus = dis-（分开）+ -luere（洗，源自 lavere「洗」）；与 soluble 背后表示「松开」的 luere 并非同一词根。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one washing away: water lowers a concentration, a sample is made testable, power is spread thin, taste and colour fade, the adjective names the weakened state, a promise loses force, shares are spread over more owners, and finally any intensity fades as it is divided.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着同一次「冲走」：水降低浓度，样品被调到可测，权力被摊薄，味道与颜色变淡，形容词命名被削弱的状态，承诺失去力量，股份被摊到更多持有人，最后任何强度都因被分割而变淡。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small cup of dark juice poured into a large jug of clear water until the colour turns pale.
core.cn: 核心意象：一小杯深色果汁倒进一大壶清水，颜色直到变浅。

branches.en: LOWERING STRENGTH: domestic dilution and laboratory dilution are one act at two scales.
branches.cn: 降低强度：日常稀释与实验室稀释，是同一动作的两个尺度。

branches.en: SPREAD AMONG MORE HOLDERS: influence and shares both lose force when divided among more parties.
branches.cn: 摊给更多持有者：影响力与股份一旦分给更多方，都会失去力量。

branches.en: FAINT QUALITIES: taste, colour and the force of a promise all fade when something neutral is mixed in.
branches.cn: 变淡的性质：味道、颜色与承诺的力量，都会因掺入中性之物而减退。

branches.en: THE WEAKENED STATE: the adjective simply names what the verb has already done.
branches.cn: 被削弱的状态：形容词只是命名动词已经做成的事。

branches.en: DIVIDED INTENSITY: any strength spread over more time or recipients counts for less at each point.
branches.cn: 被分割的强度：任何强度摊到更多时间或对象上，每一点的分量都更少。

intro.en: Dilute is a Latin verb made of a prefix and a root of washing, and the same pieces build the rest of its family.
intro.cn: dilute 是一个由前缀与「洗」词根构成的拉丁动词，同样的部分构成它其余的家族。

latinIntro.en: Dis- 'apart' plus -luere 'to wash' gives diluere and its participle dilutus; the same washing root appears in deluge and diluvial, not in dissolve.
latinIntro.cn: dis-「分开」加 -luere「洗」构成 diluere 及其分词 dilutus；同一「洗」词根出现在 deluge 与 diluvial 中，而不在 dissolve 中。

items.exampleCN: 两次稀释把样品调进了量程。

items.example: Water is the cheapest diluent here.

senses.title: A research hydrologist
senses.definition: a person who studies or practises hydrology, especially the measurement and modelling of water
senses.definitionCN: 从事水文学研究或实践、尤其负责水的测量与建模的人
senses.example: A hydrologist traced the missing water to a fissure beneath the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 一位水文学家把消失的水追踪到谷底的一条裂隙。
senses.why: Hydrology plus -ist marks the person who does the science, so the word names a practitioner rather than the field.
senses.whyCN: hydrology 加 -ist 标记做这门科学的人，因此这个词命名从业者，而非领域。

senses.title: A field practitioner
senses.definition: a worker who measures rainfall, river level and flow in the field
senses.definitionCN: 在野外测量降雨、河流水位与流量的工作者
senses.example: The hydrologist waded out to read the staff gauge.
senses.exampleCN: 水文学家涉水过去读取水尺。
senses.why: Most hydrological data are gathered outdoors, so the word often means the person at the gauge rather than the theorist.
senses.whyCN: 大部分水文数据在户外采集，因此这个词常指站在水尺旁的人，而不是理论家。

senses.title: A monitoring technician
senses.definition: a technician who maintains stations, sensors and records
senses.definitionCN: 维护水文站、传感器与记录的技术人员
senses.example: The hydrologist calibrated the pressure sensor before the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 水文学家在风暴前校准了压力传感器。
senses.why: Instruments need care, so a distinct working role grew around the maintenance of observation networks.
senses.whyCN: 仪器需要照料，于是围绕观测网络的维护长出一个独立的工作角色。

senses.title: A water-resource consultant
senses.definition: a specialist who advises on supply, recharge and allocation
senses.definitionCN: 就供水、补给与分配提供建议的专家
senses.example: The hydrologist advised the city on its aquifer budget.
senses.exampleCN: 水文学家就城市含水层收支向市府提供建议。
senses.why: When the science is sold as a service, the practitioner becomes an adviser to clients and agencies.
senses.whyCN: 当这门科学作为服务出售，从业者就成了客户与机构的顾问。

senses.title: An engineering hydrologist
senses.definition: a specialist who supplies design floods and waterworks calculations
senses.definitionCN: 提供设计洪水与水利工程计算的专家
senses.example: The engineering hydrologist set the dam's design flood.
senses.exampleCN: 工程水文专家确定了大坝的设计洪水。
senses.why: Infrastructure needs a specialist who can turn records into design values, so a professional branch is named.
senses.whyCN: 基础设施需要能把记录变成设计值的专家，于是出现一个以专业命名的分支。

senses.title: An ecohydrologist
senses.definition: a specialist who studies water together with plants, animals and ecosystems
senses.definitionCN: 把水与植物、动物及生态系统一起研究的专家
senses.example: The ecohydrologist mapped where the wetland would dry first.
senses.exampleCN: 生态水文专家绘出了湿地最先干涸的位置。
senses.why: Where water science meets ecology, the practitioner takes a compound title that names both.
senses.whyCN: 当水科学与生态学相遇，从业者获得一个同时命名两者的复合头衔。

senses.title: A climate hydrologist
senses.definition: a specialist who studies how climate change alters water cycles
senses.definitionCN: 研究气候变化如何改变水文循环的专家
senses.example: The climate hydrologist projected a shorter snow season.
senses.exampleCN: 气候水文专家预测雪季会缩短。
senses.why: Global warming moved water questions into climate science, so a hybrid role emerged.
senses.whyCN: 全球变暖把水的问题推进气候科学，于是出现混合角色。

senses.title: A citizen hydrologist
senses.definition: a trained volunteer who records water data for a shared network
senses.definitionCN: 为共享网络记录水数据的受训志愿者
senses.example: A citizen hydrologist photographed the flood mark.
senses.exampleCN: 一位公民水文学家拍下了洪水痕迹。
senses.why: Observation networks need many hands, so the title widened to include trained volunteers.
senses.whyCN: 观测网络需要许多双手，因此这个头衔扩展到受训志愿者。

intro.en: Hydrologist is hydrology plus the person suffix -ist, which reaches Greek -istēs. The word is a nineteenth-century professional label. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: hydrologist 是 hydrology 加人物后缀 -ist，后者上溯希腊 -istēs。这个词是十九世纪的职业标签。年代均为约数。

items.en: Hydōr 'water' is the root; its deeper origin is often linked to a reconstructed *wed- 'water', which remains a reconstruction.
items.cn: hydōr「水」是词根；其更深来源常被联系到重构的 *wed-「水」，那仍属重构。

items.en: Hydrology, the study of water, entered English in the eighteenth century from Greek hydro- plus -logia.
items.cn: hydrology 是对水的研究，十八世纪由希腊 hydro- 加 -logia 进入英语。

items.en: Greek -istēs marked a person who does or follows something; Latin -ista and French -iste carried it into English as -ist.
items.cn: 希腊 -istēs 标记从事或追随某事的人；拉丁 -ista 与法语 -iste 把它带入英语作 -ist。

items.en: Hydrologist appeared as water science became a paid profession in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries.
items.cn: 随着水科学在十九与二十世纪成为有薪职业，hydrologist 作为职业标签出现。

items.en: Later compound titles such as engineering hydrologist and ecohydrologist split the role by application.
items.cn: 后来工程水文专家、生态水文专家等复合头衔按应用把角色再细分。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin and first date): the pre-Greek source of hydōr is uncertain, *wed- is a reconstruction, and the first use of hydrologist is not precisely dated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源与首见年代）：hydōr 的前希腊语来源不确定，*wed- 属重构，hydrologist 最早的使用没有精确年代。

note.en: Group one holds the same-root person, field and adjective forms; group two holds neighbouring water professions that are not interchangeable.
note.cn: 第一组是同根的人物、领域与形容词形式；第二组是邻近但不可互换的水相关职业。

entries.definition: The science of water; hydrologist is the person who practises it.
entries.definitionCN: 研究水的科学；hydrologist 是从事它的人。

entries.definition: Relating to the science; it describes data or cycles, not a person.
entries.definitionCN: 与这门科学有关的；它描述数据或循环，不指人。

entries.definition: A person who measures and charts water bodies for navigation; the work is mapping rather than cycle science.
entries.definitionCN: 为航行测量并绘制水体的人；其工作是制图，而不是循环科学。

entries.definition: A person who studies groundwater in rock; it is a branch of hydrology, not the whole profession.
entries.definitionCN: 研究岩石中地下水的人；它是水文学的一个分支，不是整个职业。

entries.definition: An engineer who designs supply and drainage works; a hydrologist supplies the water data that engineer uses.
entries.definitionCN: 设计供水与排水工程的工程师；水文学家提供其使用的水数据。

entries.definition: A specialist in atmospheric water and precipitation; the focus is weather, not the whole land-water cycle.
entries.definitionCN: 研究大气水与降水的专家；重点在天气，而非整个陆水循环。

entries.definition: A scientist who studies organisms and their environment; an ecohydrologist works where water and life meet.
entries.definitionCN: 研究生物与其环境的科学家；生态水文专家工作在水与生命交汇处。

entries.definition: A trained volunteer who collects data; a citizen hydrologist is the water-specific version.
entries.definitionCN: 收集数据的受训志愿者；公民水文学家是水领域的专称。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real agent suffix, real professional titles and real branch names.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实施事后缀、真实职业头衔与真实分支名称。

normal.en: Hydrology plus -ist makes the person who does hydrology.
normal.cn: hydrology 加 -ist，就是做水文学的人。

normal.en: The hydrologist reads the gauge, not just the textbook.
normal.cn: 水文学家读水尺，不只读教科书。

normal.en: Engineering, ecology and climate give the role its compound titles.
normal.cn: 工程、生态与气候给这个角色带来复合头衔。

normal.en: A hydrographer maps water; a hydrologist explains its movement.
normal.cn: 水文测量员绘制水，水文学家解释水的运动。

normal.en: A citizen hydrologist is a trained volunteer in the same network.
normal.cn: 公民水文学家是同一网络中的受训志愿者。

abstract.en: Picture a person kneeling at a gauge while a whole valley's water passes by.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人跪在水尺旁，整个山谷的水从身边流过。

abstract.en: Picture a detective following a missing river underground.
abstract.cn: 想象一名侦探在地下去追一条消失的河。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge between a rain cloud and a city's taps.
abstract.cn: 想象一座连接雨云与城市水龙头的桥。

examples.en: The hydrologist warned that the aquifer was being mined.
examples.cn: 水文学家警告含水层正在被透支。

examples.en: A hydrologist must explain uncertainty, not just averages.
examples.cn: 水文学家必须解释不确定性，而不只是平均值。

examples.en: The hydrologist's forecast gave the town two days to evacuate.
examples.cn: 水文学家的预报给小镇争取了两天撤离时间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「hydrology（水文学）+ -ist（从事者）」——从事水文学的人 → 水文学家

root: 希腊 hydōr「水」（更深来源不确定，*wed- 为重构）+ -logia「研究」→ hydrology；加希腊 -istēs / 拉丁 -ista / 法语 -iste 形成的人物后缀 -ist → hydrologist。十九世纪起成为职业标签。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one practitioner: researcher, field worker, monitoring technician, consultant, engineering specialist, ecohydrologist, climate hydrologist and citizen volunteer.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着同一类从业者展开：研究者、野外工作者、观测员、顾问、工程专家、生态水文专家、气候水文专家与公民志愿者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person kneeling at a river gauge, a catchment map spread on the table behind.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人蹲在河岸水尺旁，身后的桌上摊着流域图。

branches.en: THEORY TO FIELD: the researcher and the gauge reader are the same role in two settings.
branches.cn: 从理论到野外：研究者与读水尺的人是同一角色在两种场景。

branches.en: SENSOR TO DESIGN: trustworthy readings become the design flood an engineer can use.
branches.cn: 从传感器到设计：可信的读数变成工程师可用的设计洪水。

branches.en: THE CONSULTANT: an estimate becomes a dam or drain on the ground.
branches.cn: 顾问：一份估算落到地上，变成大坝或排水沟。

branches.en: THE ECOLOGIST: the same training extends to how water shapes ecosystems.
branches.cn: 生态水文：同一套训练延伸到水如何塑造生态系统。

branches.en: CLIMATE TO CROWD: global projections and volunteer records both feed the same network.
branches.cn: 从气候到公众：全球预测与志愿者记录都汇入同一网络。

intro.en: Hydrologist is a transparent person noun: the field name plus -ist. The whole word can be read from its base and its agent suffix.
intro.cn: hydrologist 是透明的人物名词：领域名加 -ist。整个词可从基词与施事后缀读出。

latinIntro.en: The person suffix reached English through Latin -ista and French -iste from Greek -istēs; the base hydrology is Greek.
latinIntro.cn: 人物后缀经拉丁 -ista 与法语 -iste 上溯希腊 -istēs 进入英语；基词 hydrology 属希腊语。

items.example: Hydrology is the base of the title.
items.exampleCN: hydrology 是这个头衔的基词。

items.meaning: a person who does or follows
items.example: Biology plus -ist gives biologist.
items.exampleCN: biology 加 -ist 得到 biologist。

items.example: The hydrologist read the gauge at dawn.
items.exampleCN: 水文学家在黎明读取水尺。

items.example: Hydrologists shared the station data.
items.exampleCN: 水文学家们共享了站点数据。

items.example: The hydrological record spans a century.
items.exampleCN: 水文记录跨越一个世纪。

items.example: The hydrologic model runs daily.
items.exampleCN: 水文模型每日运行。

items.example: The hydrograph showed a sharp peak.
items.exampleCN: 过程线显示一个尖峰。

items.example: The hydrogeologist logged the borehole.
items.exampleCN: 水文地质学家记录了钻孔。

items.example: The hydrometeorologist forecast the rainfall.
items.exampleCN: 水文气象学家预报了降雨。

items.meaning: a specialist in water and ecosystems
items.example: The ecohydrologist mapped the drying wetland.
items.exampleCN: 生态水文专家绘出了干涸的湿地。

latinEntries.structure: -ista (m./f. agent suffix, medieval and modern Latin)

definition_zh: 排除；排斥；除外；被排除的状态；社会排斥
definition_en: the act of keeping someone or something out, or the state of being kept out
core_image: 一扇门在某人面前合上，门内是灯光和人群，门外只剩走廊。
scene: 实验室门口贴着「仅限授权人员」，新来的实习生被挡在门外。 A sign on the lab door reads authorised staff only, and the new intern stands outside: that is exclusion.
sceneCN: 这里 exclusion 是「被排除在外、不得进入」（第 1 个义项：被挡在某个范围之外的状态）；句意：实验室门口贴着仅限授权人员，新来的实习生被挡在门外，这就是被排除在外。

pos.zh: 排除；排斥；除外；被排除状态；（生态）竞争排斥

derivatives.zh: 排除；把……挡在外
排他的；独有的；高档的
专门地；唯独地
排他性的；造成排斥的

senses.title: Shutting someone out
senses.definition: the act of preventing a person or thing from entering or taking part
senses.definitionCN: 阻止人或物进入或参与的行为
senses.example: The exclusion of non-members from the vote caused an outcry.
senses.exampleCN: 把非会员排除在投票之外引发了抗议。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to shut the door. Exclusion is that closing seen as an act: the boundary is drawn by whoever holds the door.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为‘关上门’。exclusion 就是这次关门被视为一个动作：边界由掌着门的人画出。

senses.title: The state of being left out
senses.titleCN: 被排除的状态：人在门外的那一侧
senses.definition: the condition of being left outside a group, place, or activity
senses.definitionCN: 被留在群体、场所或活动之外的状态
senses.example: Her exclusion from the committee lasted two years.
senses.exampleCN: 她被排除在委员会之外长达两年。
senses.why: The same event can be told from the door's other side. Here the noun names the experience of the one who remains outside.
senses.whyCN: 同一件事可以从门的另一侧讲述。这里的名词命名的是留在门外那个人的经历。

senses.title: Exclusion clause
senses.titleCN: 除外条款：合同里预先排除的责任
senses.definition: a contractual or insurance clause that removes a risk or item from cover
senses.definitionCN: 把某项风险或项目排除在保障之外的合同或保险条款
senses.example: The policy's exclusion for flood damage was printed in bold.
senses.exampleCN: 保单对洪水损害的除外责任用粗体印出。
senses.why: Contracts define the protected space first, then list what is shut out of it. The clause is the door drawn on paper.
senses.whyCN: 合同先划定受保护的空间，再列出被关在门外的项目。条款就是画在纸上的那扇门。

senses.title: Social exclusion
senses.titleCN: 社会排斥：被挡在正常生活之外
senses.definition: the process by which groups are pushed to the margins of society and denied normal participation
senses.definitionCN: 某些群体被推到社会边缘、无法正常参与的过程
senses.example: Poor transport links deepen the social exclusion of rural families.
senses.exampleCN: 交通不便加深了农村家庭的社会排斥。
senses.why: Here the door is not one building but a whole set of institutions: work, school, housing, and health. Exclusion becomes structural rather than personal.
senses.whyCN: 这里的门不是一栋楼，而是一整套制度：工作、学校、住房与医疗。排斥由此变成结构性的，而非个人性的。

senses.title: Competitive exclusion
senses.titleCN: 竞争排斥：两个物种不能长期占同一生态位
senses.definition: the ecological principle that two species competing for the same resource cannot coexist indefinitely
senses.definitionCN: 两个物种争夺同一资源时无法无限期共存的生态学原理
senses.example: Competitive exclusion drove the native species from the pond.
senses.exampleCN: 竞争排斥把本地物种逐出了池塘。
senses.why: One species uses the shared resource slightly better, so the other is gradually shut out of its own niche. The door here is closed by competition, not policy.
senses.whyCN: 一个物种对共享资源的利用略好，另一个就被逐渐关在自己的生态位之外。这里的门由竞争关上，而非政策。

senses.title: Tax exclusion
senses.titleCN: 不计入项：税法里不纳入收入的部分
senses.definition: an item of income that is not counted for tax purposes
senses.definitionCN: 在计税时不计入收入的项目
senses.example: The tax exclusion for employer health cover reduced the bill.
senses.exampleCN: 雇主医保的免税待遇降低了税单。
senses.why: The tax base is a defined set. An exclusion removes one item before the rate is applied, so the item never enters the calculation.
senses.whyCN: 税基是一个被定义的集合。exclusion 在套用税率前移走一项，因此该项从未进入计算。

senses.title: Expulsion from an institution
senses.titleCN: 逐出：被学校或组织开除
senses.definition: the removal of a person from a school, club, or organization as a punishment
senses.definitionCN: 作为惩罚把某人从学校、俱乐部或组织中除名
senses.example: The exclusion was reduced to a suspension on appeal.
senses.exampleCN: 经上诉，开除处分被减为停学。
senses.why: An institution controls its own door. Expulsion is exclusion made punitive: the person is not merely outside but formally put outside.
senses.whyCN: 机构控制自己的门。开除是带惩罚性的 exclusion：当事人不仅在门外，而且是被正式放到门外。

senses.title: Exclusivity
senses.titleCN: 排他性：只让一部分人进入的安排
senses.definition: the quality of an arrangement that admits only a limited set of people
senses.definitionCN: 只接纳有限人群的安排所具有的性质
senses.example: The club's exclusion was part of its appeal.
senses.exampleCN: 这家俱乐部的排他性正是其吸引力的一部分。
senses.why: Here exclusion is valued rather than resented: the closed door itself becomes the product, because being inside signals membership.
senses.whyCN: 这里的排斥被珍视而非怨恨：关着的门本身成了产品，因为‘在里面’标志着 membership。

intro.en: Exclusion is from Latin exclusio, from excludere, to shut out: ex- out plus claudere to shut. The same claudere runs through include, conclude, and clause.
intro.cn: exclusion 来自拉丁 exclusio，源头是 excludere‘关在外面’：ex-‘向外’加 claudere‘关’。同一个 claudere 贯穿 include、conclude 与 clause。

items.en: To shut, close, or enclose. It gives English close, clause, cloister, and the -clude verbs. The root image is a door or a barrier.
items.cn: 关、闭、围住。它给出英语 close、clause、cloister 以及 -clude 系列动词。词根意象是门或障碍。

items.en: Ex- out plus claudere shut: to shut out, exclude, or cut off. The verb assumes an inside that is being protected.
items.cn: ex-‘向外’加 claudere‘关’：关在外面、排除、切断。该动词预设了一个被保护的‘里面’。

items.en: A shutting out. In rhetoric it could also mean omission or rejection of a possibility; in law, a bar to entry.
items.cn: 关在外面。在修辞学里也可指省略或排除某种可能；在法律里指禁止进入。

items.en: French passed the noun to English. The legal sense of a bar or an exception travelled with it.
items.cn: 法语把名词传给英语，禁止进入或除外条款的法律义随之而来。

items.en: English exclusion is recorded in the 15c. Early uses were legal and institutional: exclusion from office, from a court, from a will.
items.cn: 英语 exclusion 在 15 世纪有记录。早期用法是法律与制度性的：排除公职、排除法庭、排除继承。

items.en: The 20c added social exclusion and competitive exclusion, extending the closed door from law to society and ecology.
items.cn: 20 世纪加入社会排斥与竞争排斥，把‘关上的门’从法律扩展到社会与生态。

note.en: The first group is the exclude family; the second compares ways of removing someone or something, each with a different mechanism.
note.cn: 第一组是 exclude 词族；第二组比较把人或物移走的不同方式，各自机制不同。

entries.definition: to shut someone or something out. It is the action; exclusion is the act or state.
entries.definitionCN: 把人或物关在外面；是动作，exclusion 是行为或状态。

entries.definition: limited to a particular group, or not shared. It describes the arrangement, not the act of shutting.
entries.definitionCN: 限于特定群体的，或不共享的；描述安排，而非关门动作。

entries.definition: only, and to the exclusion of everything else. It turns the adjective into a restriction on scope.
entries.definitionCN: 只；唯独；把其他一切排除在外。它把形容词变成范围限制。

entries.definition: tending to exclude people or things. It is used of rules, practices, and policies.
entries.definitionCN: 倾向于排斥人或物的；用于规则、做法与政策。

entries.definition: something left out, often by mistake or by choice in writing. It does not require a door or a boundary.
entries.definitionCN: 被漏掉的东西，常因疏忽或书写选择；不需要门或边界。

entries.definition: the act of taking something away from its place. It focuses on the object being moved, not on who is kept out.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物从其位置拿走；聚焦被移动的对象，而不是被挡在外面的人。

entries.definition: the act of forcing someone or something out, often physically. It is more violent than exclusion.
entries.definitionCN: 强行把人或物弄出去，常是物理性的；比 exclusion 更暴力。

entries.definition: the deliberate avoidance or shunning of a person by a group. It is exclusion carried out by many small refusals.
entries.definitionCN: 群体对某人有意回避、排斥；是许多次小拒绝共同完成的 exclusion。

entries.definition: the enforced separation of groups, especially by race or sex. It divides space rather than simply shutting one door.
entries.definitionCN: 按种族或性别等强制分隔群体；它分割空间，而不只是关一扇门。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: ex- out plus claudere shut. Exclusion is the closing of a door in someone's face, seen either as an act or as a state.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：ex-‘向外’加 claudere‘关’。exclusion 就是在某人面前关门，可作为动作也可作为状态来看。

normal.en: Ex- out, claudere shut: exclusion is being shut out.
normal.cn: ex- 向外，claudere 关：exclusion 就是被关在外面。

normal.en: Include and exclude are the two directions of the same door.
normal.cn: include 与 exclude 是同一扇门的两个方向。

normal.en: An exclusion clause is a door drawn on paper.
normal.cn: 除外条款就是画在纸上的一扇门。

normal.en: Social exclusion closes many doors at once.
normal.cn: 社会排斥同时关上许多扇门。

normal.en: A club's exclusion is its selling point: the closed door is the product.
normal.cn: 俱乐部的排他性就是卖点：关着的门本身是产品。

abstract.en: Every inside is made by an outside; exclusion is how a group learns its own shape.
abstract.cn: 每个‘里面’都由‘外面’造出；排斥是群体认识自身形状的方式。

abstract.en: The same closed door can be a punishment or a privilege, depending on which side you stand.
abstract.cn: 同一扇关着的门，可以是惩罚也可以是特权，取决于你站在哪一侧。

abstract.en: Exclusion is cheaper than inclusion, which is why systems drift toward it.
abstract.cn: 排斥比容纳便宜，所以系统会自然漂向排斥。

examples.en: The exclusion of the small firms from the scheme was challenged in court.
examples.cn: 把小公司排除在该计划之外的做法在法庭上受到挑战。

examples.en: He worked on the project to the exclusion of almost everything else.
examples.cn: 他做这个项目，几乎把其他一切排除在外。

examples.en: The report treated social exclusion as a health issue, not only a moral one.
examples.cn: 报告把社会排斥当作健康问题，而不只是道德问题。

dict_mnemonic.text: “一颗死路”——走到一颗标着‘死路’的门前，被关在外面：exclusion 排除、排斥。

root: 源自拉丁 excludere（ex-‘向外’+ claudere‘关’）与 exclusio‘关在外面’；核心是“把某人或某物挡在门外的动作或状态”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of exclusion, one image: a door closes and someone stays outside. The door may be a club, a contract, a society, a niche, a tax base, a school, or a membership rule.
sensesIntro.cn: exclusion 的八个义项共用一个意象：门关上，有人留在外面。这扇门可以是俱乐部、合同、社会、生态位、税基、学校或会员规则。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a door closing with a person left in the corridor.
core.cn: 核心意象：门关上，一个人被留在走廊里。

branches.en: THE TWO SIDES OF THE DOOR: the act of shutting out and the experience of being outside.
branches.cn: 门的两侧：关门的动作与留在外面的经历。

branches.en: THE WRITTEN BOUNDARY: insurance clauses and tax rules remove items before they count.
branches.cn: 写下的边界：保险条款与税务规则在计算前移走项目。

branches.en: THE SOCIAL AND PUNITIVE DOOR: structural marginalization and formal expulsion both put a person outside.
branches.cn: 社会性与惩罚性的门：结构性边缘化与正式开除都把一个人放到外面。

branches.en: THE ECOLOGICAL DOOR: competition closes a niche on a rival species.
branches.cn: 生态的门：竞争对竞争者关上生态位。

branches.en: THE VALUED DOOR: exclusivity makes the closed door itself desirable.
branches.cn: 被珍视的门：排他性让关着的门本身变得有吸引力。

intro.en: Exclusion is ex- plus claud- plus -sion. The same root gives include, conclude, seclude, and the noun clause; the door image is shared across all of them.
intro.cn: exclusion 是 ex- 加 claud- 加 -sion。同一词根给出 include、conclude、seclude 与名词 clause；它们共享‘门’的意象。

latinIntro.en: The Latin forms are claudere, excludere, and exclusio. Excludere is built from a real prefix and a real verb, so no reconstruction is needed here.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁形式是 claudere、excludere、exclusio。excludere 由真实前缀与真实动词构成，这里不需要重构。

items.meaning: to shut out or leave out
items.example: The rules exclude late entries.
items.exampleCN: 规则排除迟交的参赛作品。

items.meaning: the act or state of being shut out
items.example: His exclusion from the team was temporary.
items.exampleCN: 他被排除在队伍之外是暂时的。

items.meaning: restricted to a few; not shared
items.example: The shop sells exclusive designs.
items.exampleCN: 这家店出售独家设计。

items.example: The room is used exclusively for meetings.
items.exampleCN: 这个房间只用于开会。

items.meaning: the state of being restricted to a few
items.example: The brand charges for exclusivity.
items.exampleCN: 这个品牌为排他性收费。

items.example: The zoning rules had an exclusionary effect.
items.exampleCN: 分区规则产生了排斥效果。

items.meaning: to shut inside, hence to contain
items.meaningCN: 包含；把……关在里面（in-‘在内’+ claudere‘关’）
items.example: The price includes breakfast.
items.exampleCN: 价格包含早餐。

items.meaning: to close together, hence to end or infer
items.meaningCN: 结束；得出结论（com-‘一起’+ claudere‘关’）
items.example: The talk concluded with a short summary.
items.exampleCN: 讲座以简短总结结束。

items.meaning: to shut apart, hence to isolate
items.meaningCN: 使隔离；隐居（se-‘分开’+ claudere‘关’）
items.example: The cabin was secluded by tall pines.
items.exampleCN: 小屋被高松林隔离起来。

items.meaning: a distinct part of a sentence or contract
items.meaningCN: 从句；条款；源自‘关闭、收束的部分’
items.example: The final clause limits the agreement to five years.
items.exampleCN: 最后一条条款把协议限制在五年内。

definition_zh: 因变量；实验中随自变量变化而被测量、被解释的结果变量
definition_en: the variable that is measured in an experiment and expected to change in response to the independent variable
core_image: 记录板上只留一列读数，每一行对应一种处理条件，最后一栏写着结果
scene: 记录板上只留一列读数，每一行对应一种处理条件。 Plant height is the dependent variable here, recorded after each week of treatment.
