senses.title: The outcome that is measured
senses.definition: the factor that an experimenter measures, expected to respond to changes in the independent variable
senses.definitionCN: 实验者测量的因素，预期会随自变量的变化而作出反应
senses.example: Plant height is the dependent variable here, recorded after each week of treatment.
senses.exampleCN: 株高在这里是因变量，每周处理后记录一次。
senses.why: Its value is read only after the treatment is applied, so it hangs on the factor that was moved, and that dependence is the name.
senses.whyCN: 它的值只在处理实施之后才被读出，因此取决于被移动的那个因素，这种「依从」正是名称的由来。

senses.title: The response in statistics
senses.definition: in a statistical model, the quantity whose variation the analysis tries to account for
senses.definitionCN: 在统计模型中，分析试图解释其变异的那个量
senses.example: The response was treated as the dependent variable in every model.
senses.exampleCN: 每个模型都把响应量当作因变量。
senses.why: Statistics asks what explains variation, and the variable being explained sits on the outcome side of the equation.
senses.whyCN: 统计学追问什么解释了变异，而被解释的变量就坐在方程的「结果」一侧。

senses.title: The y of a function
senses.definition: in mathematics, the output of a function, whose value is fixed once the input is chosen
senses.definitionCN: 在数学中，函数的输出，其值在输入选定后即被确定
senses.example: In the equation, the dependent variable changes when the input changes.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个方程里，输入一变，因变量就变。
senses.why: A rule assigns one output to each input, so the output depends on the input by construction.
senses.whyCN: 规则为每个输入指定一个输出，因此输出在构造上就依赖于输入。

senses.title: The outcome in social research
senses.definition: in social science, the measured condition that a study tries to explain, such as a test score or a rate
senses.definitionCN: 在社会科学中，研究试图解释的被测状态，如考试分数或比率
senses.example: The study used the graduation rate as its dependent variable.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究把毕业率作为因变量。
senses.why: When the outcome cannot be manipulated, it is still measured, and the word keeps the experimental image of reading a result.
senses.whyCN: 当结果无法被操纵时，它仍可被测量，这个词保留了「读出结果」的实验意象。

senses.title: The behaviour recorded in psychology
senses.definition: in psychology, the observed response, such as reaction time or a rating, treated as the outcome of a manipulation
senses.definitionCN: 在心理学中，被观察的反应，如反应时或评分，被视为操纵的结果
senses.example: Reaction time was the dependent variable in the attention task.
senses.exampleCN: 注意任务中的因变量是反应时。
senses.why: Behaviour is what the experiment can see, while the mental process is inferred, so the visible response becomes the measured variable.
senses.whyCN: 行为是实验看得见的东西，心理过程只能推断，因此可见的反应成了被测量的变量。

senses.title: The endpoint of a trial
senses.definition: in a clinical trial, the pre-specified outcome used to judge whether a treatment works
senses.definitionCN: 在临床试验中，用来判断治疗是否有效的预先指定结果
senses.example: The trial's dependent variable was the number of symptom-free days.
senses.exampleCN: 这项试验的因变量是无症状天数。
senses.why: A trial must name its outcome before it begins, so the measured endpoint is fixed in the protocol and called the dependent variable.
senses.whyCN: 试验必须在开始前指定结果，因此被测终点写进方案，并被称为因变量。

senses.title: The explained side of a regression
senses.definition: in regression analysis, the variable on the left of the equation, whose values the predictors are used to estimate
senses.definitionCN: 在回归分析中，方程左边的变量，其取值由预测变量来估计
senses.example: Income sat on the left as the dependent variable.
senses.exampleCN: 收入作为因变量放在左边。
senses.why: Regression draws a line from predictors to an outcome, and the outcome is dependent because the line is fitted to it.
senses.whyCN: 回归从预测变量画一条线到结果，结果之所以为因变量，是因为这条线是照着它拟合的。

senses.title: The quantity on the vertical axis
senses.definition: the quantity whose values are read up the vertical axis when a relation is graphed
senses.definitionCN: 作关系图时，其取值沿纵轴向上读取的量
senses.example: With yield as the dependent variable, the trend rises to the right.
senses.exampleCN: 以产量作因变量，趋势向右上升。
senses.why: By convention the effect is placed on the vertical axis, so the graph puts the dependent variable where the eye reads change.
senses.whyCN: 按惯例结果放在纵轴，因此图把因变量放在眼睛读取变化的位置。

senses.title: The outcome an economic model explains
senses.titleCN: 经济模型要解释的结果
senses.definition: in economics, the quantity a model seeks to account for, such as consumption responding to income
senses.definitionCN: 在经济学中，模型试图解释的量，如随收入变化的消费
senses.example: Consumption is the dependent variable, with income on the other side.
senses.exampleCN: 消费是因变量，收入在另一侧。
senses.why: A model is written to explain one quantity by others, and that quantity is dependent on the explanatory side.
senses.whyCN: 模型是为了用其他量解释某一个量，那个量就依赖于解释的一侧。

intro.en: Dependent variable joins dependent, from Latin dependere 'to hang from', to variable, from variare 'to change'. The pair with independent variable belongs to modern mathematics and experimental design.
intro.cn: dependent variable 把 dependent（拉丁语 dependere「悬挂于」）与 variable（variare「变化」）组合起来。它与自变量成对使用，属于现代数学与实验设计。

items.en: Dependere meant to hang from or be attached to, from de- 'down' and pendere 'to hang'.
items.cn: dependere 意为悬挂于、依附于，由 de-「向下」与 pendere「悬挂」构成。

items.en: Dependent entered English through French in the fifteenth century, meaning reliant on another for support.
items.cn: dependent 经法语在十五世纪进入英语，意为依靠他者供养。

items.en: Variare meant to change, from varius 'varied', and it gave the noun variable.
items.cn: variare 意为改变，出自 varius「杂色的」，由此产生名词 variable。

items.en: In the mathematics of functions, the input was called independent and the output dependent; the labels became standard in nineteenth-century algebra.
items.cn: 在函数数学中，输入被称为自变量，输出被称为因变量；这对标签在十九世纪代数中成为标准。

items.en: Laboratory and agricultural design in the later nineteenth and early twentieth centuries applied the pair to treatments and measured responses.
items.cn: 十九世纪后期至二十世纪初的实验室与农业设计，把这组词用到处理与测得反应上。

items.en: Regression, psychology and clinical trials each adopted the term for their own outcome, and the protocol fixed it in advance.
items.cn: 回归、心理学与临床试验各自采用这一术语指自己的结果，而试验方案会预先把它固定下来。

note.en: The first group shares one of the two words; the second group names the other factors of a design, with the differences spelled out.
note.cn: 第一组共享短语中的一个词；第二组是设计中的其他因素，并写明差别。

entries.definition: Reliant on something else; the adjective inside the phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 依靠他物的；短语中的形容词。

entries.definition: The state of relying on another for support or value.
entries.definitionCN: 在供养或取值上依靠他者的状态。

entries.definition: A quantity that can take different values.
entries.definitionCN: 可取不同值的量。

entries.definition: To change; the verb behind the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 变化；名词背后的动词。

entries.definition: The factor that is deliberately changed, the cause side of the pair.
entries.definitionCN: 被刻意改变的因素，这一对中的原因一侧。

entries.definition: A factor held constant so it cannot explain the outcome; unlike the dependent variable, it is not measured as a result.
entries.definitionCN: 被保持恒定、因而无法解释结果的因子；与因变量不同，它不作为结果被测量。

entries.definition: The result itself, in ordinary language, without the statistical frame.
entries.definitionCN: 日常语言中的结果本身，不带统计框架。

entries.definition: What a system or subject does after a stimulus; the statistical word for the measured side.
entries.definitionCN: 系统或受试者在刺激之后的反应；统计中用来指被测的一侧。

entries.definition: The pre-declared measure of success in a trial, the clinical name for the dependent variable.
entries.definitionCN: 试验中预先声明的成功量度，是因变量的临床名称。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the hanging root, the x-and-y image, and the fixed contrast with the independent variable.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用「悬挂」词根、x 与 y 的意象，以及它与自变量的固定对照。

normal.en: Dependent is literally hanging from something: the measured outcome hangs on the factor that was changed.
normal.cn: dependent 字面是悬挂在某物上：被测结果挂在被改变的因素上。

normal.en: The family runs depend, dependent, dependence, variable, vary and variant.
normal.cn: 同族词有 depend、dependent、dependence、variable、vary 与 variant。

normal.en: In a graph the independent variable runs across and the dependent variable rises up the side.
normal.cn: 图上自变量横着走，因变量沿侧边上升。

normal.en: A trial declares its dependent variable, such as symptom-free days, before the first patient is enrolled.
normal.cn: 试验在第一位患者入组前就声明因变量，例如无症状天数。

normal.en: The pair is fixed: one factor is moved, the other is measured, and neither is held still.
normal.cn: 这一对是固定的：一个因素被移动，另一个被测量，两个都不被固定。

abstract.en: The dependent variable is the answer the experiment is allowed to give, and it must be chosen before the question is asked.
abstract.cn: 因变量是实验被允许给出的答案，而且必须在提问之前选好。

abstract.en: An outcome that nobody defined in advance can always be explained afterwards.
abstract.cn: 事先没有定义的结果，事后总能找到解释。

abstract.en: To depend is not weakness here; it is the mark of having been measured.
abstract.cn: 在这里，依赖不是软弱，而是「被测量过」的标志。

examples.en: The dependent variable was recorded at the same hour each day.
examples.cn: 因变量每天在同一时刻记录。

examples.en: A trial must state its dependent variable in the protocol.
examples.cn: 试验必须在方案中写明因变量。

examples.en: If the dependent variable is vague, the analysis cannot be repeated.
examples.cn: 如果因变量含糊，分析就无法重复。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「迪彭登特-维瑞额波」——挂在处理条件后面、等着被读出的那个结果：因变量

root: dependent 来自拉丁语 dependere「悬挂于」（de- 向下 + pendere 悬挂），经法语进入英语；variable 来自 variare「变化」。因变量与自变量成对，是十九世纪函数数学与实验设计的产物。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one measured outcome: the experimental response, the statistical response, the y of a function, a social outcome, a recorded behaviour, a trial endpoint, the left side of a regression, the vertical axis and an explained economic quantity.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项跟着同一个被测量的结果：实验反应、统计响应、函数中的 y、社会结果、被记录的行为、试验终点、回归左侧、纵轴，以及被解释的经济量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a board holds a single column of readings, one row per treatment, and the last row is the result.
core.cn: 核心意象：记录板上只有一列读数，每种处理一行，最后一行就是结果。

branches.en: THE MEASURED OUTCOME: weekly height, or symptom-free days declared before a trial begins.
branches.cn: 被测结果：每周的株高，或试验开始前就声明的无症状天数。

branches.en: THE RESPONSE SIDE: the variation a model explains, the quantity on the left of a regression.
branches.cn: 响应一侧：模型所解释的变异，回归方程左边的量。

branches.en: THE Y: the output fixed once the input is chosen, and the quantity rising up the vertical axis.
branches.cn: 那个 y：输入选定后被固定的输出，以及沿纵轴上升的量。

branches.en: THE EXPLAINED FACT: graduation rates in social research, consumption responding to income.
branches.cn: 被解释的事实：社会研究中的毕业率，随收入变化的消费。

branches.en: THE VISIBLE BEHAVIOUR: reaction time standing in for a mental process that cannot be seen.
branches.cn: 可见的行为：以反应时代表看不见的心理过程。

intro.en: The phrase pairs a Latin adjective of hanging with a Latin noun of change; the hyphen-free two-word unit is a modern technical name.
intro.cn: 这个短语把拉丁语「悬挂」形容词与「变化」名词配在一起；这个不带连字符的两词单位是现代技术名称。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is dependere, pendere, variare and varius, with -abilis in the noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语成分是 dependere、pendere、variare 与 varius，名词中还有 -abilis。

items.example: The adjective describes a value that follows another.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述随另一量而定的值。

items.example: It marks the point from which something hangs.
items.exampleCN: 它标出悬挂的起点。

items.example: It also gives pendant and pendulum.
items.exampleCN: 它也是「吊坠」与「摆锤」两词的来源。

items.example: The verb joins physical hanging to logical reliance.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把物理悬挂与逻辑依赖连在一起。

items.example: The noun names a measurable quantity.
items.exampleCN: 名词指可测量的量。

items.example: The verb is the root of the noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是名词的根。

items.example: It describes what is not uniform.
items.exampleCN: 它描述不齐一之物。

items.example: It builds the adjective that became the noun.
items.exampleCN: 它构成后来变作名词的形容词。

items.example: The pair splits moving from measuring.
items.exampleCN: 这一对把「移动」与「测量」分开。

items.example: The third term marks what must not move.
items.exampleCN: 第三个词标出不许变动的东西。

latinEntries.example: The compound gives English depend and dependent.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 这个复合词给出英语 depend 与 dependent。

latinEntries.structure: Latin verb pendere (pend-, pensum; to hang)
latinEntries.example: Latin pendere means to hang, and gives pendant and suspend.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 pendere 意为悬挂，并给出 pendant 与 suspend。

latinEntries.example: It is the verb behind variable and variation.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 它是 variable 与 variation 背后的动词。

latinEntries.example: The adjective supplies the idea of changeability.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 这个形容词提供「可变」这层意思。

latinEntries.example: It forms variabilis, the Latin adjective behind variable.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 它构成 variabilis，即 variable 背后的拉丁形容词。

definition_zh: 冷淡的；疏远的；超然离群的（副词：远离地；冷淡地）
definition_en: not friendly or forthcoming; distant and cool, or at a distance
core_image: 船头迎风站开、不靠人群的那个人
scene: 聚会上众人围坐说笑，他却站在窗边。 She remained aloof from the gossip.
sceneCN: 这里的 aloof 是「疏远的、超然的」（第 1 个义项：有意保持距离的冷淡）；句意是她对那些闲话保持超然。

derivatives.zh: 由 aloof 加 -ness 构成，义为「冷淡；超然」
同源航海词，义为「船头」的旧称

senses.title: Cool and distant in manner
senses.definition: physically or emotionally distant in dealing with others
senses.definitionCN: 待人接物时保持身体或情感上的距离
senses.example: The new manager seemed aloof at first.
senses.exampleCN: 新经理起初显得很冷淡。
senses.why: From sailors keeping "to windward", apart; distance became coldness.
senses.whyCN: 源于水手「迎风在上风处」避开；距离引申为冷淡。

senses.title: Uninvolved in a matter
senses.definition: deliberately not taking part or taking sides
senses.definitionCN: 有意不参与、不站队
senses.example: He kept aloof from office politics.
senses.exampleCN: 他对办公室政治置身事外。
senses.why: Standing apart in space maps onto standing apart in affairs.
senses.whyCN: 空间上的站开映射到事务上的不沾手。

senses.title: Reserved out of shyness
senses.definition: withholding oneself because of shyness rather than contempt
senses.definitionCN: 因羞怯而非轻蔑而退缩不前
senses.example: Aloof in crowds, she opened up one on one.
senses.exampleCN: 她在人群中拘谨，一对一却很健谈。
senses.why: The same distance can spring from fear of exposure, not pride.
senses.whyCN: 同样的距离感可以源于怕暴露，而非傲慢。

senses.title: Superior and disdainful
senses.definition: distancing oneself from others as if beneath one's notice
senses.definitionCN: 视他人不值得注意而与之保持距离
senses.example: The professor was aloof toward undergraduates.
senses.exampleCN: 教授对本科生态度高傲。
senses.why: Distance read upward becomes disdain.
senses.whyCN: 距离一旦向上解读就成了轻蔑。

senses.title: Objectively detached, positively
senses.definition: neutrally detached in judgment, free of bias or faction
senses.definitionCN: 判断上中立超然，不受派系或偏见影响
senses.example: A referee must stay aloof from the crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 裁判必须不为观众所动。
senses.why: Distance can be a virtue: the judge above the fray.
senses.whyCN: 距离也可以是美德：裁判立于纷争之上。

senses.title: Standing at a physical distance
senses.definition: as an adverb, standing or kept apart in space
senses.definitionCN: 作副词，指在空间上站开或保持距离
senses.example: The sentry called, "Stand aloof!"
senses.exampleCN: 哨兵喝道：「站开！」
senses.why: This is the original nautical sense before the emotional one.
senses.whyCN: 这是情感义之前的原始航海义。

senses.title: Guarded and unrevealing
senses.definition: guarded in speech, revealing little of oneself
senses.definitionCN: 言语谨慎，很少袒露自我
senses.example: He stayed aloof about his past.
senses.exampleCN: 他对自己的过去讳莫如深。
senses.why: Withholding words is a form of keeping distance.
senses.whyCN: 不吐露言语是保持距离的一种形式。

senses.title: Detached by temperament
senses.definition: having a naturally solitary, unsociable temperament
senses.definitionCN: 天性孤僻、不合群
senses.example: Cats are famously aloof.
senses.exampleCN: 猫以孤高著称。
senses.why: When distance becomes a character trait, the word describes nature, not mood.
senses.whyCN: 当距离成为性格，词就描述本性而非一时情绪。

intro.en: Aloof comes from the nautical phrase a-luff, "to windward", where a ship's head keeps clear.
intro.cn: aloof 源自航海短语 a-luff「迎风向上风处」，指船头保持清距。

items.en: lof or looch, "windward", the nautical term.
items.cn: 中古荷兰语 lof/looch「上风」，航海术语。

items.en: a loof, "to windward", used in sailing orders.
items.cn: 中古英语 a loof「向上风」，用于操船口令。

items.en: aloof as adverb, "at a distance, apart".
items.cn: 十六世纪 aloof 作副词「隔开、远离」。

items.en: The emotional sense "distant in manner" develops.
items.cn: 十七世纪发展出「态度疏远」的情感义。

items.en: Used by major writers for proud or shy detachment.
items.cn: 被重要作家用于写骄傲或羞怯的疏离。

items.en: Chiefly adjectival today; the adverb use is older-fashioned.
items.cn: 如今以形容词为主，副词用法较旧。

note.en: Aloof is distinct from aloft by one letter, and near in meaning to distant and reserved.
note.cn: aloof 与 aloft 仅差一个字母，意义上与 distant、reserved 相近。

entries.definition: up in the air; one letter apart, related nautical history but opposite direction.
entries.definitionCN: 在高处；仅差一字母，同有航海渊源但方向相反。

entries.definition: the Dutch nautical source of aloof.
entries.definitionCN: 荷兰语航海来源词。

entries.definition: an animal's foot; rhymes only.
entries.definitionCN: 蹄；仅押韵。

entries.definition: not intimate; broader, covering space and manner.
entries.definitionCN: 不亲近的；兼指空间与态度，更宽泛。

entries.definition: slow to show feelings; less cold than aloof.
entries.definitionCN: 不外露感情的；比 aloof 少冷意。

entries.definition: emotionally uninvolved, often neutrally.
entries.definitionCN: 情感上不介入的，常为中性。

normalIntro.en: Anchor aloof in the ship that keeps clear.
normalIntro.cn: 把 aloof 锚定在保持清距的船上。

normal.en: a + loof "to windward": a ship holding off, staying clear.
normal.cn: a + loof「上风」：船保持距离、不靠近。

normal.en: aloof vs aloft: up the mast is aloft; away from the crowd is aloof.
normal.cn: aloof 与 aloft：爬上桅杆是 aloft，避开人群是 aloof。

normal.en: Noun: aloofness; phrases: keep/stand/remain aloof from.
normal.cn: 名词 aloofness；短语 keep/stand/remain aloof from。

normal.en: Adjective or adverb: an aloof manner / stand aloof.
normal.cn: 可作形容词或副词：an aloof manner / stand aloof。

normal.en: Tone watch: aloof can blame (cold) or praise (impartial).
normal.cn: 语气注意：aloof 可贬（冷漠）可褒（超然）。

abstract.en: One chair pulled an arm's length back from the circle.
abstract.cn: 一把椅子被拉离人群一臂之遥。

abstract.en: A cat watching the party from the top of the bookshelf.
abstract.cn: 猫在书架顶上看派对。

abstract.en: A ship holding its bow into the wind, keeping a gap of gray water.
abstract.cn: 船顶着风，与人群隔开一线灰色的海。

examples.en: She stayed aloof during the quarrel.
examples.cn: 争吵期间她保持超然。

examples.en: His aloof manner hid deep shyness.
examples.cn: 他冷淡的举止掩盖了深深的羞怯。

examples.en: The judge kept aloof from the media frenzy.
examples.cn: 法官与媒体的狂热保持距离。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿路夫」——阿婆站在路口夫人们之外，隔着三步看热闹，冷冷的不搭腔。

root: 中古荷兰语 lof「上风」进入中古英语航海用语 a loof「向上风处（以避让）」，十六世纪转为副词「在远处」，十七世纪引申为「态度疏远冷淡」；与 aloft 同属航海方位词族但方向相反。

sensesIntro.en: From the ship holding off to windward, the senses cover cold manner, non-involvement, shy reserve, disdain, commendable detachment, literal standing apart, guarded speech, and solitary temperament.
sensesIntro.cn: 从迎风避让的船出发，义项覆盖冷淡态度、置身事外、羞怯拘谨、高傲轻蔑、可褒的超然、字面站开、言语设防与天性的孤高。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: holding off at a clear distance
core.cn: 核心意象：保持一段清距

branches.en: Cool manner and its commendable version.
branches.cn: 冷淡态度及其可褒版本。

branches.en: Standing apart from affairs.
branches.cn: 置身事外。

branches.en: Shy reserve and solitary temperament.
branches.cn: 羞怯拘谨与天性的孤高。

branches.en: Distance read as disdain.
branches.cn: 被解读为轻蔑的距离。

branches.en: Literal spacing and guarded speech.
branches.cn: 字面站开与言语设防。

intro.cn: aloof 是固化为单词的航海短语。

latinIntro.cn: 此处无拉丁词根：词族属荷英航海用语。

definition_zh: 像；与……相似
definition_en: to look or seem like someone or something else
core_image: 两个人站在一起，侧脸轮廓几乎重叠
scene: 这对双胞胎长得太像，连老师都会认错。 The twins resemble each other so closely that even their teacher mixes them up.
sceneCN: 这里 resemble 是「像」（第 1 个义项：在外貌或性质上相似）；句意：这对双胞胎长得太像，连老师都会认错。

derivatives.zh: 相似；相似之处
相似的

senses.title: To look like someone
senses.definition: to have a similar appearance to another person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 外貌与另一个人或物相似
senses.example: She closely resembles her mother.
senses.exampleCN: 她长得很像她母亲。
senses.why: The Latin root means like, so the verb starts with visible likeness.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为「像」，所以这个动词从看得见的外貌相似开始。

senses.title: To have similar qualities
senses.definition: to share features or qualities with something else
senses.definitionCN: 与另一事物共享特征或性质
senses.example: Their styles resemble each other in many ways.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的风格在许多方面彼此相似。
senses.why: Likeness moves from faces to abstract patterns and styles.
senses.whyCN: 相似从面容扩展到抽象的模式与风格。

senses.title: To seem like something
senses.definition: to give the impression of being something, often in formal description
senses.definitionCN: 给人某种印象，常用于正式描写
senses.example: The room resembled a small museum.
senses.exampleCN: 这个房间看起来像一座小博物馆。
senses.why: The verb can describe an overall impression, not only a physical match.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词可描述整体印象，而不只是外形吻合。

intro.en: Resemble comes from Old French resembler, from re- and sembler, to seem, ultimately from Latin similis, like.
intro.cn: resemble 来自古法语 resembler，由 re- 与 sembler（显得）构成，最终源于拉丁语 similis（像）。

items.en: Similis means like or similar.
items.cn: similis 意为相像、相似。

items.en: Similare means to make like.
items.cn: similare 意为使相像。

items.en: Sembler means to seem or appear.
items.cn: sembler 意为显得、看起来。

items.en: Resembler means to be like or resemble.
items.cn: resembler 意为相像、类似。

items.en: Middle English resemblen keeps the visual sense.
items.cn: 中古英语 resemblen 保留视觉上的相似。

items.en: Modern English extends resemble to styles, sounds, and situations.
items.cn: 现代英语把 resemble 扩展到风格、声音与情境。

note.en: Resemble is a likeness verb, and it sits near its family and near phrases for looking like.
note.cn: resemble 是一个「相似」动词，与自身词族以及表示「像」的短语相邻。

entries.definition: the state of being similar
entries.definitionCN: 相似；相似之处

entries.definition: similar to something
entries.definitionCN: 相似的

entries.definition: to bring people or parts together
entries.definitionCN: 集合；组装

entries.definition: to have a similar appearance
entries.definitionCN: 看起来像

entries.definition: to look or behave like an older relative

entries.definition: to reflect or match something closely

normalIntro.en: Resemble contains the old root similis, like: to resemble is to be like.
normalIntro.cn: resemble 含有古老词根 similis（像）：相像就是「像」。

normal.en: The re- adds the sense of looking back and seeing the same shape.
normal.cn: re- 增添「回头一看还是同一个轮廓」的感觉。

normal.en: Resemble each other is the most common phrase.
normal.cn: resemble each other 是最常见的短语。

normal.en: Resemblance is the noun for the likeness.
normal.cn: resemblance 是表示「相似」的名词。

normal.en: We resemble family members in looks or manner.
normal.cn: 我们在外貌或举止上像家人。

normal.en: Compare look like: resemble is more formal and uses a single verb.
normal.cn: 对比 look like：resemble 更正式，而且只用一个动词。

abstract.en: Picture two shadows falling at the same angle.
abstract.cn: 想象两道影子以同样的角度落下。

abstract.en: Imagine a face in a photograph echoing another face.
abstract.cn: 想象照片中的一张脸与另一张脸遥相呼应。

abstract.en: Think of two melodies that share the same opening notes.
abstract.cn: 想象两段旋律以相同的开头几个音起句。

examples.cn: 她长得很像她母亲。

examples.en: Their styles resemble each other in many ways.
examples.cn: 他们的风格在许多方面彼此相似。

examples.en: The room resembled a small museum.
examples.cn: 这个房间看起来像一座小博物馆。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re + semble」——一再看到同样的样子，就是相像；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 similis（像）→ 俗拉丁语 similare（使相像）→ 古法语 sembler（显得）→ resembler（相像）→ 中古英语 resemblen → 现代英语 resemble。

sensesIntro.en: The verb begins with faces, extends to qualities and styles, and finally to the overall impression something gives.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个动词从面容开始，扩展到性质与风格，最后指某物给人的整体印象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two outlines laid over each other until they nearly match.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个轮廓叠在一起，几乎重合。

branches.en: Physical likeness is the oldest and clearest sense.
branches.cn: 外貌相似，是最古老、最清楚的义项。

branches.en: Shared qualities extend likeness beyond appearance.
branches.cn: 共同性质把相似扩展到外貌之外。

branches.en: An overall impression can resemble something else.
branches.cn: 整体印象也可以像另一事物。

branches.en: People can look alike and behave alike at once.
branches.cn: 人可以同时长得像、举止也像。

branches.en: Shared qualities often create the impression of a match.
branches.cn: 共同性质常造成「相互吻合」的印象。

intro.en: Resemble is a French verb built on the Latin root for like, with English endings forming its family.
intro.cn: resemble 是建立在拉丁语「像」词根上的法语动词，词族由英语词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin similis means like, and similare means to make like; French sembler means to seem.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 similis 意为像，similare 意为使相像；法语 sembler 意为显得。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的词尾

definition_zh: 城市规划；城市总体规划；土地利用规划；交通与基础设施规划；城市空间设计
definition_en: the professional activity of deciding how land, transport and buildings in a city should be arranged
core_image: 会议桌上一张街区图，红线标出将来的轻轨，绿色块留给公园
scene: 会议桌上摊开一张街区图，红线标出将来的轻轨，绿色块留给公园。 City planning decides where the rail line will cut through the old quarter.
sceneCN: 这里 city planning 指「对城市交通与基础设施走向所作的专业安排」（第 4 个义项：交通与基础设施规划）；句意为城市规划决定了轻轨将怎样穿过老城区。可辨识物件：街区图、红线、绿色块、会议桌。

pos.zh: 城市规划（不可数，指专业活动或学科）

derivatives.zh: 基础词 plan 去掉 -ing 后的形式，来自拉丁 planum「平面」→ 由「平面图」偏移为「预先安排的方案」
plan + -er（施事后缀）→ 偏移为「做规划的人」
plan + -ing（动名词后缀）→ 偏移为「规划这一活动」
plan + -ed（过去分词作定语）→ 偏移为「按计划建成的」
un-（否定前缀）+ planned → 偏移为「未经规划的」
city + -scape（景观后缀，仿 landscape）→ 偏移为「城市景观整体」
zone + -ing（动名词后缀）→ 偏移为「按用途划分土地的制度」

senses.title: The profession
senses.titleCN: 城市规划这一专业与学科
senses.definition: the profession and academic field that studies how cities should be laid out
senses.definitionCN: 研究城市应如何布局的专业与学科
senses.example: City planning grew out of public health surveys of overcrowded housing.
senses.exampleCN: 城市规划是从对拥挤住房的公共卫生调查中生长出来的。
senses.why: planning names the activity of arranging in advance, and city names its object, so the phrase is the profession of arranging cities.
senses.whyCN: planning 指预先安排的活动，city 指其对象，因此这个短语就是安排城市的专业。

senses.title: A master plan
senses.definition: the single long-range document that sets a city's intended shape for decades
senses.definitionCN: 为城市数十年形态定下意图的长远文件
senses.example: The master plan of city planning reserved a green belt in the north.
senses.exampleCN: 城市规划的总体方案在北部保留了一条绿带。
senses.why: a profession needs one binding document, and the phrase shifts from the activity to that document.
senses.whyCN: 一个专业需要一份有约束力的文件，于是这个短语从活动转指那份文件。

senses.title: Land-use planning
senses.definition: the allocation of parcels to housing, industry, farming or open space
senses.definitionCN: 把地块分配给住房、工业、农业或空地
senses.example: City planning decides which fields may become factories.
senses.exampleCN: 城市规划决定了哪些田地可以变成工厂。
senses.why: land is the scarce thing a city allocates, so use-allocation is the core of the craft.
senses.whyCN: 土地是城市分配中最稀缺的东西，所以用途分配就成了这门行当的核心。

senses.title: Transport and infrastructure planning
senses.definition: the routing of roads, rail, water and power before they are built
senses.definitionCN: 在建造之前安排道路、铁路、供水与电力的走向
senses.example: City planning decides where the rail line will cut through the old quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 城市规划决定了轻轨将怎样穿过老城区。
senses.why: networks last longer than buildings, so their routes are fixed first and constrain everything after.
senses.whyCN: 管网比建筑存续更久，所以它们的走向先被定下，并约束其后的一切。

senses.title: Urban design and layout
senses.definition: the shaping of streets, blocks and public space at the scale of the neighbourhood
senses.definitionCN: 以街区尺度塑造街道、地块与公共空间
senses.example: Good city planning makes a square that people actually cross.
senses.exampleCN: 好的城市规划会做出人们真的愿意穿过的广场。
senses.why: planning at drawing scale becomes design, where dimensions and frontages decide how a place feels.
senses.whyCN: 规划落到图纸尺度就成了设计，尺寸与临街面决定一个地方给人的感受。

senses.title: Neighbourhood planning
senses.definition: planning carried out at the level of a district with resident participation
senses.definitionCN: 在有居民参与的区级层面进行的规划
senses.example: City planning at this level begins with the school run.
senses.exampleCN: 这一层面的城市规划从送孩子上学的那条路开始。
senses.why: national and city-wide rules must be applied somewhere, and that somewhere is a neighbourhood.
senses.whyCN: 全国与全市的规则总要落到某个具体地方，而那个地方就是街区。

senses.title: Rules and regulation
senses.definition: the ordinances, permits and zoning rules that give plans legal force
senses.definitionCN: 赋予规划法律效力的条例、许可与分区规则
senses.example: City planning without enforcement is only a drawing.
senses.exampleCN: 没有执行的规划只是一张图。
senses.why: a plan changes nothing until it is written into law, so the phrase covers the rule-making as well.
senses.whyCN: 规划不写进法律就什么都改变不了，因此这个短语也涵盖规则的制定。

senses.title: Planning for renewal
senses.definition: the replanning of districts that are already built, often with relocation involved
senses.definitionCN: 对已建成城区重新规划，常涉及搬迁
senses.example: City planning here means deciding who must move before the blocks come down.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的城市规划意味着在街区被拆掉之前决定谁必须搬走。
senses.why: when there is no new land, planning becomes a negotiation over existing space and existing residents.
senses.whyCN: 没有新土地时，规划就变成围绕既有空间与既有居民的协商。

intro.en: City planning joins city, from Latin civitas, to planning, from plan, whose Latin source is planum 'flat surface'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: city planning 把来自拉丁 civitas 的 city 与来自 plan 的 planning 组合起来，而 plan 的拉丁来源是 planum「平面」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Civitas named a citizen-body and its town; city entered English through French cité.
items.cn: civitas 指公民共同体及其城镇；city 经法语 cité 进入英语。

items.en: Planum meant 'a flat surface', from planus 'flat, level'. A plan was first a drawing on a flat sheet.
items.cn: planum 意为「平面」，来自 planus「平的、平坦的」。plan 最初指画在平面纸上的一张图。

items.en: French plan carried both the drawing and the scheme senses into English.
items.cn: 法语 plan 把「图」与「方案」两层意思一并带入英语。

items.en: City planning emerged as a named activity when industrial cities began to be laid out with sewers, parks and bylaws.
items.cn: 当工业城市开始被按排水、公园与附例来布局时，city planning 才作为一项有名字的活动出现。

items.en: In the twentieth century the phrase named a licensed profession and a municipal department, not only a drawing.
items.cn: 到二十世纪，这个短语指一门有执照的专业与一个市政部门，而不只是一张图。

items.en: Source uncertain: the exact first use of the phrase is unrecorded, and the deeper origin of planus is unsettled, so any earlier form proposed is a reconstructed form.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这个短语的确切首见没有记录，planus 的更早来源亦无定论，因此提出的更早形式均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one separates the phrase from its near-synonyms and from the documents it produces; group two holds the practices it overlaps with.
note.cn: 第一组把这一短语与近义说法以及它产出的文件分开；第二组是与之重叠的实践。

entries.definition: The commoner term for the same profession; it is wider because it covers regions as well as cities.
entries.definitionCN: 同一专业更常见的说法；它更宽，因为同时涵盖区域与城市。

entries.definition: The document or drawing produced; planning is the activity, a plan is its output.
entries.definitionCN: 所产出的文件或图纸；规划是活动，方案是产出。

entries.definition: The long-range framework document; it is one product of city planning, not the whole field.
entries.definitionCN: 长远的框架文件；它是城市规划的一项产出，而非整个领域。

entries.definition: The division of land into use districts; zoning is a tool that planning uses, not its equal.
entries.definitionCN: 把土地划为用途分区；分区是规划所用的一种工具，并不等同于规划。

entries.definition: The design of buildings, streets and spaces as a coherent whole; it is the three-dimensional side of planning.
entries.definitionCN: 把建筑、街道与空间作为整体来设计；它是规划的三维一面。

entries.definition: The allocation of land to uses; it is a core branch of city planning rather than a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 把土地分配给各类用途；它是城市规划的核心分支，而非同义词。

entries.definition: Rebuilding land that was already built on; it follows a plan and is not the planning itself.
entries.definitionCN: 对已建成土地的再建；它依规划而行，本身不是规划。

entries.definition: The routing of roads, water and power; it is one specialized branch of the wider field.
entries.definitionCN: 安排道路、供水与电力的走向；它是更宽领域中的一个专门分支。

entries.definition: A settled course of action adopted by an authority; planning produces policy but also responds to it.
entries.definitionCN: 权威采纳的既定行动方向；规划既产出政策，也受政策约束。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two real halves, the Latin source of plan and the real instruments.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个真实的部分、plan 的拉丁来源与真实工具名称。

normal.en: planum 'flat surface' gives plan: a scheme is first a drawing on a flat sheet.
normal.cn: planum「平面」给出 plan：方案最初是画在平面纸上的一张图。

normal.en: The family runs plan, planner, planning, planned, unplanned, zoning, cityscape.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 plan、planner、planning、planned、unplanned、zoning、cityscape。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the office: city planning department, city planning policy, city planning map.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出机构：城市规划部门、城市规划政策、城市规划图。

normal.en: The commoner synonym is urban planning, which also covers regional scales.
normal.cn: 更常见的同义说法是 urban planning，它还覆盖区域尺度。

normal.en: A plan without enforcement is only a drawing: policy turns it into law.
normal.cn: 没有执行的方案只是一张图：政策把它变成法律。

abstract.en: Picture a red line drawn across a map years before anyone digs the trench.
abstract.cn: 想象一条红线在地图上画下多年之后，才有人去挖那条沟。

abstract.en: Picture a green square that forbids a building that has not yet been imagined.
abstract.cn: 想象一个绿色方块，禁止了一栋尚未被想象出来的建筑。

abstract.en: Picture a meeting where the school run is used as evidence about a road.
abstract.cn: 想象一场会议，把送孩子上学的路线当作关于一条路的证据。

examples.en: City planning failed where the new blocks had no school.
examples.cn: 新区没有配学校的地方，城市规划失败了。

examples.en: The city planning office publishes its maps online.
examples.cn: 城市规划办公室把图纸公布在网上。

examples.en: City planning must consider drainage before it draws the streets.
examples.cn: 城市规划必须先考虑排水，再画街道。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「city（城市）+ planning（预先安排）」——给城市事先画好图、定好规矩 → 城市规划

root: city（拉丁 civitas「公民共同体」）+ planning（plan 来自拉丁 planum「平面」，planus「平的」）；短语在十九世纪工业城市布局中成为专门说法。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one act: someone arranges a city in advance, and that act appears as a profession, a master document, land allocation, transport routes, three-dimensional design, neighbourhood work, legal rules and replanning of what already stands.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个动作展开：有人事先安排城市，这个动作依次表现为专业、总体文件、土地分配、交通走向、三维设计、街区工作、法律规则，以及对已建成之物的重新规划。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line drawn on paper that will later become a trench, a wall or a park.
core.cn: 核心意象：画在纸上的一条线，日后会变成沟、墙或公园。

branches.en: THE ACT AND ITS DOCUMENT: a profession of arranging, and the one long-range plan it produces.
branches.cn: 动作与文件：一门安排的专业，以及它产出的那份长远方案。

branches.en: WHO GETS WHICH LAND: the allocation of parcels is the core decision of the craft.
branches.cn: 谁得到哪块地：地块分配是这门手艺的核心决定。

branches.en: ROUTES FIXED FIRST: transport and utility lines outlast buildings and constrain everything after.
branches.cn: 先定走向：交通与管线比建筑活得久，并约束后来的一切。

branches.en: FROM DRAWING TO FEELING: dimensions and frontages decide how a place feels, and residents meet the plan at street level.
branches.cn: 从图纸到感受：尺寸与临街面决定一个地方的感受，而居民在街道层面遇见规划。

branches.en: FORCE AND REVISION: rules give the plan legal force, and renewal applies them to ground already occupied.
branches.cn: 效力与修订：规则赋予方案法律效力，更新则把它们用于已被人占用的地面。

intro.en: City planning is two words, each with its own productive endings and compounds.
intro.cn: city planning 是两个词，各自带有高产词尾与复合形式。

latinIntro.en: Both halves trace to Latin: civitas for city and planum for plan, the latter from planus 'flat'.
latinIntro.cn: 两半都可上溯拉丁语：city 出自 civitas，plan 出自 planum，后者来自 planus「平的」。

definition_zh: 明智的；可取的；适宜的
definition_en: sensible and likely to bring a good result, and therefore worth doing or choosing
core_image: 山路入口竖着一块牌子，提示前方塌方、请走另一侧
scene: 天色转暗，向导抬头看了看压下来的云层。 It is advisable to begin the descent before the storm arrives.
sceneCN: 这里的 advisable 是「明智的、可取的」（第 1 个义项：值得采取、能避免麻烦的）；句意是在暴风雨到来之前开始下撤是明智的。

pos.zh: 形容词：明智的；可取的；适宜的

senses.title: Wise and worth doing
senses.definition: sensible because it is likely to produce a good result or avoid trouble
senses.definitionCN: 因为很可能带来好结果或避开麻烦而显得明智的
senses.example: It is advisable to begin the descent before the storm arrives.
senses.exampleCN: 在暴风雨到来之前开始下撤是明智的。
senses.why: The suffix -able makes the word mean 'able to be advised': an action that a sensible adviser would recommend is advisable.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -able 让这个词表示「值得被建议的」：一个明智的顾问会推荐的做法，就是 advisable。

senses.title: Suitable as a measure
senses.definition: described of a plan or measure that is judged proper and suitable in a formal context
senses.definitionCN: 正式语境中形容某项方案或措施被认为恰当、适宜
senses.example: The committee treated a full review as the advisable course.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会认为全面复查才是可取的做法。
senses.why: Placed before a noun, the word shifts from 'it would be wise to' to 'judged proper as a measure', which is how official reports use it.
senses.whyCN: 放在名词前时，它从「这样做会明智」转为「作为措施被认为得当」，官方报告正是这样用的。

intro.en: An adjective formed in English from advise, which itself came from Latin through French.
intro.cn: 这是英语在动词 advise 上构成的形容词，而 advise 本身经由法语来自拉丁语。

items.en: videre, to see, gave visum, 'what seems', the base of the whole advice family.
items.cn: videre 意为「看」，其分词 visum 表示「看来如此之物」，是整族词的底子。

items.en: Medieval Latin advisare meant to consider or take counsel, built on the same 'seem' root.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 advisare 意为「考虑、商议」，同样建立在「看来如此」这个词根上。

items.en: Old French aviser meant to look at, consider, or give an opinion, and English borrowed it as advise.
items.cn: 古法语 aviser 意为「察看、考虑、给出意见」，英语借入后成为 advise。

items.en: English added -able to advise, first in the sense 'able to be advised', then 'worth advising'.
items.cn: 英语给 advise 加上 -able，先表示「可以被告知的」，后来转为「值得建议的」。

items.en: Today the word almost always appears in the frame it is advisable to do something, especially in guidance and rules.
items.cn: 今天它几乎总出现在「it is advisable to do something」这一句框里，多见于指南与规章。

note.en: The first group shares the advice root; the second gathers adjectives of prudence and suitability.
note.cn: 第一组共享 advice 词根；第二组收表示「审慎、适宜」的形容词。

definition_zh: 解释偏差；释义偏差；解读偏倚
definition_en: a systematic tendency to read ambiguous information in a particular way, or to favour one meaning while coding and analysing material
core_image: 同一段访谈稿摊在桌上，两支荧光笔划出不同句子，旁边两份编码表用不同颜色标记

sceneCN: 这里指解读歧义信息时的系统性偏向（第 1 个义项：对歧义信息的解释偏向）；句意为解释偏差可以把同一句含糊的回应读成安慰，也可以读成威胁。图中可辨识物件：访谈稿、两支荧光笔、两份编码表、颜色标记、桌面。

senses.title: A systematic reading of ambiguity
senses.titleCN: 对歧义信息的系统性解读偏向
senses.definition: a tendency to resolve ambiguous material in one consistent direction, such as reading it as threat rather than as neutral
senses.definitionCN: 倾向以某个固定方向消解歧义材料，例如总读成威胁而非中性
senses.example: Interpretation bias can turn the same ambiguous reply into reassurance or threat.
senses.exampleCN: 解释偏差可以把同一句含糊的回应读成安慰，也可以读成威胁。
senses.why: When a signal has more than one meaning, the reader must choose, and a habit of choosing makes the choice systematic.
senses.whyCN: 当一个信号有多种含义时，读者必须选择，而选择的习惯使这种选择变得系统。

senses.title: The researcher's interpretive bias
senses.definition: a researcher's tendency to notice, select and code material in line with an existing frame
senses.definitionCN: 研究者按既有框架去注意、挑选与编码材料的倾向
senses.example: Interpretation bias in coding appeared as a preference for quotations that supported the main theme.
senses.exampleCN: 编码中的解释偏差表现为偏好支持主主题的引语。
senses.why: The analyst is not a neutral reader; the coding scheme and the expected finding both steer attention.
senses.whyCN: 分析者不是中性读者；编码方案与预期发现都会引导注意力。

senses.title: Confirmation-driven reading
senses.definition: the tendency to treat consistent evidence as strong and inconsistent evidence as flawed
senses.definitionCN: 把一致证据视为有力、把不一致证据视为有缺陷的倾向
senses.example: Interpretation bias made the team dismiss the two cases that contradicted the pattern.
senses.exampleCN: 解释偏差使团队忽略了两个与模式相矛盾的个案。
senses.why: A hypothesis is comfortable with friends and suspicious of strangers, and the reader inherits that comfort.
senses.whyCN: 假设对朋友感到舒服、对陌生人心存怀疑，而读者继承了这种舒服。

senses.title: A cultural or linguistic lens
senses.definition: the way a shared language, custom or educational tradition supplies a default meaning for a word or act
senses.definitionCN: 共同语言、习俗或教育传统为一个词或行为提供默认含义的方式
senses.example: Interpretation bias across languages can turn a polite refusal into agreement.
senses.exampleCN: 跨语言解释偏差可以把礼貌的拒绝读成同意。
senses.why: A word translated word for word may arrive with a meaning it never had in the original setting.
senses.whyCN: 逐字翻译过来的词，可能带着它在原场景中从未有过的含义到达。

senses.title: Bias built into a coding category
senses.titleCN: 编码类别本身带来的偏向
senses.definition: distortion produced when predefined categories force complex material into one available box
senses.definitionCN: 预设类别把复杂材料塞进现有格子而产生的失真
senses.example: A narrow coding frame creates interpretation bias before the first transcript is read.
senses.exampleCN: 狭窄的编码框架在第一份逐字稿被读之前就造成了偏差。
senses.why: A category is a question the data must answer, and some answers have no category to enter.
senses.whyCN: 类别是数据必须回答的问题，而有些回答根本没有类别可进。

senses.title: Bias in attributing causes
senses.definition: a tendency to explain an act by the actor's character in one group and by the situation in another
senses.definitionCN: 倾向把某一群体的行为解释为性格，而把另一群体的行为解释为情境
senses.example: Interpretation bias appeared in the way the same delay was blamed on laziness or on traffic.
senses.exampleCN: 同样的延误，一个被归为懒惰，一个被归为堵车，解释偏差就在这里出现。
senses.why: The same event admits a dispositional and a situational reading, and the choice between them can follow a group line.
senses.whyCN: 同一件事既可以按性格解释，也可以按情境解释，而选择往往沿着群体界线走。

senses.title: The effect on trustworthiness
senses.definition: the loss of credibility when readers cannot tell whether a finding comes from the data or from the analyst's frame
senses.definitionCN: 读者无法判断发现来自数据还是分析者框架时所造成的可信度损失
senses.example: Interpretation bias weakens trustworthiness even when the interviews were well conducted.
senses.exampleCN: 即使访谈做得很好，解释偏差也会削弱可信度。
senses.why: If the frame is invisible, the finding looks like the data speaking in its own voice, which is the problem.
senses.whyCN: 如果框架不可见，发现就像数据用自己的声音说话，问题正在这里。

senses.title: Reflexivity and peer coding as remedies
senses.titleCN: 反思与同伴编码作为对策
senses.definition: the practices of recording one's interpretive frame and having a second coder check the reading
senses.definitionCN: 记录自身解释框架并让第二位编码员核查解读的做法
senses.example: Peer coding is used to make interpretation bias visible rather than to pretend it is absent.
senses.exampleCN: 同伴编码用来让解释偏差变得可见，而不是假装它不存在。
senses.why: A second reader does not remove the lens, but can show where the lens is bending the material.
senses.whyCN: 第二位读者无法取下透镜，却能指出透镜在哪里弯折了材料。

intro.en: Interpretation bias joins interpretari, a Latin verb of explaining, to bias, from Old French biais, a slant. The origin of interpres, the Latin noun behind the verb, is uncertain.
intro.cn: 这个术语把拉丁语解释动词 interpretari 与来自古法语 biais「斜线」的 bias 组合起来；动词背后的名词 interpres 来源不确定。

items.en: Interpres meant a go-between, explainer or negotiator, but its own origin is source uncertain; a link to a word for price has been proposed.
items.cn: interpres 指中间人、解释者或谈判者，但它自身的来源不确定；有人提出与表示「价格」的词有关。

items.en: Interpretari meant to explain, expound or translate, and it supplied the English verb.
items.cn: interpretari 意为解释、阐发或翻译，提供英语动词 interpret。

items.en: English used interpret for explaining meaning and for oral translation; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语用 interpret 表示解释意义与口译；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The noun named an explanation or a translation, and English took it as interpretation.
items.cn: 名词指解释或翻译，英语借入为 interpretation。

items.en: Biais meant a slant or an oblique line, and its deeper origin is also uncertain.
items.cn: biais 意为斜面或斜线，其更早来源同样不确定。

items.en: Psychology and qualitative methods joined the two nouns to name a systematic reading habit, whether in a person or in an analyst.
items.cn: 心理学与定性方法把这两个名词组合，指一种系统的解读习惯，无论在个人还是在分析者身上。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like interpretation bias; the second group names neighbouring distortions of reading and analysis.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与 interpretation bias 相近；第二组是与「阅读与分析失真」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: To explain or assign meaning to material.
entries.definitionCN: 指解释或为材料赋予意义。

entries.definition: The meaning drawn from material, or the act of drawing it.
entries.definitionCN: 指从材料中得出的意义，或得出意义的行为。

entries.definition: A person who explains or translates speech.
entries.definitionCN: 指解释或口译的人。

entries.definition: Relating to explanation rather than measurement.
entries.definitionCN: 指与解释而非测量有关的。

entries.definition: To read something in a wrong way.
entries.definitionCN: 指以错误方式解读某物。

entries.definition: The tendency to seek and accept evidence that supports an existing belief.
entries.definitionCN: 指寻求并接受支持既有信念的证据的倾向。

entries.definition: Distortion introduced by the categories and rules used to label material.
entries.definitionCN: 指由标记材料的类别与规则引入的失真。

entries.definition: A systematic error in explaining the causes of behaviour.
entries.definitionCN: 指解释行为原因时的系统性错误。

entries.definition: The way a question or frame makes some meanings more available.
entries.definitionCN: 指问题或框架使某些意义更易得的方式。

entries.definition: The practice of examining one's own position in the research.
entries.definitionCN: 指检视自身在研究中所处位置的做法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations work through the real parts, word family and common phrases behind this term.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想依托这个术语背后真实的构词部件、同族词与常见搭配。

normal.en: Interpres was a go-between, and an interpreter stands between two parties who do not share a language.
normal.cn: interpres 是中间人，解释者站在两个语言不通的人之间。

normal.en: The same sentence can be read as threat or reassurance, and the habit of reading decides.
normal.cn: 同一句话可以读成威胁，也可以读成安慰，而阅读习惯作决定。

normal.en: A coding frame is a set of boxes, and material that fits no box is the first thing lost.
normal.cn: 编码框架是一组格子，放不进格子的材料最先丢失。

normal.en: Confirmation bias makes friends of consistent evidence and strangers of the rest.
normal.cn: 确认偏差把一致证据当朋友，把其余当陌生人。

normal.en: Peer coding does not remove the lens; it makes the lens visible.
normal.cn: 同伴编码不取下透镜，而是让透镜可见。

abstract.en: A text does not carry its meaning the way a box carries a stone; someone has to lift it.
abstract.cn: 文本携带意义不像箱子装石头，必须有人把它搬起来。

abstract.en: The frame you cannot see is the one that looks like the world.
abstract.cn: 你看不见的那个框架，最像世界本身。

abstract.en: Two readers can agree on every word and still live in different sentences.
abstract.cn: 两位读者可以对每个字都一致，却仍住在不同的句子里。

examples.en: The authors named interpretation bias as a limit of single-coder analysis.
examples.cn: 作者把解释偏差列为单人编码分析的一种局限。

examples.en: Training reduced interpretation bias in the scoring of open-ended answers.
examples.cn: 培训减少了开放式答案评分中的解释偏差。

examples.en: A second coder was added to expose interpretation bias in the theme labels.
examples.cn: 加入第二位编码员，以暴露主题标签中的解释偏差。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「解释」加「斜」——同一句话，有人读出安慰，有人读出威胁；斜的那一下，就是解释偏差。

root: 拉丁 interpres「中间人、解释者」（来源不确定，可能与「价格」有关）+ interpretari「解释、翻译」→ 英语 interpret / interpretation；古法语 biais「斜线」→ bias（更早来源不确定）；两者组合为解释偏差。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the ambiguous signal to the remedy: systematic reading of ambiguity, the researcher's frame, confirmation-driven reading, cultural lenses, category bias, attribution bias, effects on trustworthiness, and reflexivity or peer coding.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从歧义信号走向补救：对歧义的系统解读、研究者框架、确认驱动、文化透镜、类别偏差、归因偏差、对可信度的影响，以及反思与同伴编码。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one transcript on a table, two highlighters marking different sentences, and two coding sheets in different colours.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上一份访谈稿，两支荧光笔划出不同句子，两份编码表用不同颜色标记。

branches.en: THE HABIT OF READING: ambiguity resolved in one direction, and evidence sorted into friends and strangers.
branches.cn: 阅读习惯：歧义被固定方向消解，证据被分成朋友与陌生人。

branches.en: THE ANALYST'S STRUCTURE: the researcher's frame and the boxes built into a coding scheme.
branches.cn: 分析者的结构：研究者的框架与编码方案里预先搭好的格子。

branches.en: THE CULTURAL LENS: default meanings supplied by language and custom.
branches.cn: 文化透镜：语言与习俗提供的默认含义。

branches.en: THE CAUSAL READING: character or situation, chosen along a group line.
branches.cn: 因果解读：性格或情境，沿着群体界线选择。

branches.en: THE CREDIBILITY AND THE CHECK: an invisible frame weakens trust, and a second reader makes it visible.
branches.cn: 可信度与核查：看不见的框架削弱信任，第二位读者让它可见。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin verb of explaining to a French noun for a slant.
intro.cn: 这个短语把拉丁语「解释」动词与法语「斜线」名词组合起来。

latinIntro.en: Latin interpres and interpretari supply the first half; Old French biais supplies bias; both have uncertain deeper origins, noted rather than guessed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 interpres 与 interpretari 提供前半，古法语 biais 提供「偏差」一词；两者更早来源都不确定，这里只标注而不臆测。

items.example: Its deeper origin is uncertain and is not reconstructed here.
items.exampleCN: 其更早来源不确定，此处不作重构。

items.example: It supplies English interpret.
items.exampleCN: 它提供英语 interpret。

items.example: It forms interpretation.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 interpretation。

items.exampleCN: 它构成 interpreter。

items.exampleCN: 它构成 interpretive。

items.exampleCN: 后半从物理斜面开始。

items.exampleCN: 后半命名失真。

items.meaning: a systematic habit of assigning meaning
items.meaningCN: 赋予意义的系统性习惯
items.example: The compound names the reading, not the text.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词命名阅读方式，而非文本。
